Report 33: a 3-habit cap (sometimes 2) draws 213 complaints (5.41%, mean 2.31) — 'isn't much of a test run'; 'if … 5 rather than 3 … I'd have … probably upgraded' — but is far milder than the take-backs; the report proposes testing 3 habits + unlimited check-ins vs 5 habits vs a 14-day full trial; Spain, the UK and Brazil show the highest cap rates (10.5–10.7%). Report 34: a 2-habit cap (2018–2025) is 39 complaints (5.25%, mean 2.44) and 15 of 37 1★ (40.5%), rising to 9.7% of E4; reviewers benchmark 5 as the norm ('Other apps usually have 5 free habits'; 'with three I'd have kept it for decency; with five I'd have … got hooked, and then bought'); the same cap is the most common purchase trigger for users whose two habits worked; the 2026 reports of a 4-habit tier are too few to read. Report 36: an unlimited free tier (praised: 'you can still get limitless habits w/ the free version — please keep it that way', 2023) capped at 2 then 1 in 2026; three reviewers volunteer three as the fair number ('Three would be reasonable for a paywall but only one??'; 'Ein Cap bei 3 Gewohnheiten hätte ich in Ordnung gefunden'); one mistook the cap for a bug; the cap upset US and non-US equally (5.56% each). Report 41: a 3-habit cap is 28 complaints (3.44%, mean 2.32) — 66.7% of 2★ and 31.0% of 1★, spiking to 6.4% in 2025 — while 5 describe it as a working trial and 4 of them paid; fans inside the complaint name 5–10 habits as the line ('at least 8 or 10'; '10ish'; '5/7'; '4/5'); the cap hurts 2.3× more outside high-spend markets. Report 42: a 3-habit cap where time, date, reminders and repetition are also paid is 55 complaints (26.70%, mean 1.96) — the largest theme — read as the product being broken ('Everything is paid! Writing a routine, only the title is free'; 'There is no reason to subscribe to the app to only have 3 habits'); four reviewers say the free tier proves there is no reason to subscribe; the number 3 has been cited every year 2022–2026. Report 43 (natural experiment): a 3-item cap held 2016–~2022 produced 66 complaints (10.34%, mean 2.36), 25 of 76 one-star reviews and 16 'bait and switch' accusations ('how can anyone set up a productive day with only 3 available habits?'; 'at least 8 - 10 habits for free'); loosening it removed the theme within two years and replaced it with free-tier praise at 4.63; the cap appeared at 5★ eight times from users who found three focusing; the report: do not re-tighten. Report 46 (the unchanged case): a 3-habit cap held from Jan 2019 to the listing in Sep 2026 is the largest negative (180, 8.26%, mean 2.43; 41.0% of one-stars; identical 8.27% vs 8.25% across market groups — 'a global constant of this product'); its count never fell (26 / 32 / 22 / 18 in 2022–25) while prompted volume halved its rate; the counter-offer is modest (29 name 4, 5, 6 or 7 — nobody unlimited) and the free tier cannot fill the product's own 4-row widget; 66 (mean 4.92) defend three on habit-science grounds; 'discovered after setup' is the indefensible version ('you've already spent 20 minutes or more setting it up', 16 votes). Report 47: the changed case — habit count unlimited 2019–2024 ('完全無料!!… タスクの登録数が無制限') then capped at 6 for free users from December 2024 (7 complaints, mean 2.29: 'Agora eu não posso mexer nos meus hábitos se não irei perder todos'); tracking multiple goals is praised by 17 (mean 4.76). Report 48 (the counter-case to a fixed cap): a cap that moved 10 → 7 → 3 produced the corpus's only growing grievance (211, 4.79%, mean 2.68) — 'No one has just one habit they need to track'; the three-tracker tier 'cannot show' a multi-goal product; the 2015–18 era with ~10 free trackers produced the highest ratings (4.62★), the most free-tier gratitude (7.82%) and a growing payer base; report's E1: raise the tier until the differentiator is demonstrable. Report 50 (the direct 5-vs-3 comparison): at 5 free habits reviewers defend the cap — 'Tienes 5 hábitos por elegir gratis lo que considero perfecto ya que te hace ser prioritario' ('perfect since it makes you prioritise'); '5 x free habits is a great option for new habit trackers'; 'I have 5 and it's all I need, when I get a job I will actually buy a subscription' — while at 3 nobody does: '3 hábitos gratis es una mierda'; 'la versión gratuita debería ser funcional' — 'Five habits was above the threshold at which a user can demonstrate a routine to themselves… Three is below it'; the 3★ band is five convinced users stalled by the cap (praise → cap → rating, none objecting to the price); 'Give me like 6 or 7 free habits and I'll be happy'; the report's S1: revert to 5, grandfather existing users, or disclose before install; experiment: A/B 3 vs 5 vs 7 on conversion, retention and rating. Report 52: the free quota (most often 5; 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 also reported across cohorts) is the first wall and the persistent friction — PAY_CAP5 888 (4.30%, 2.96), 199 of them 5★ ('the quota is fine, the app is lovely'); a February 2020 install surge produced 51 quota complaints and 57 one-stars in one month. Report 53: a 3-habit free cap (PAY_CAP3 89, 5.11%, 3.04) splits reviewers — 35 at 4–5★ find three enough to try or live with, 33 at 1–2★ call it a trick; top theme in Canada (11.94%); the report's M3 asks for a retention test of 5 habits rather than assuming bigger is better. Report 54: a 3-habit cap — the most-discussed decision (44, 11.92%, 3.16; 11 more call the free tier useless at 1.91) — hit mid-setup ('I was having fun setting up my habits until I maxed out my 3 free habits … Deleted immediately'; 'sleep, wake, exercise, and all three are used up', TW); reviewers name their own number, modal 5–8 (5, 5–7, 7–8, 8, 9 as 3×3 across time-of-day sections, 10); 23 of 44 rated 1–3★; D1: raise to 5–8 as a measured experiment. Report 55: a five-habit free tier praised more often than resented (PAY_FREE_OK 96 at 4.86 vs PAY_CAP 87 at 3.98, 44 of them 5★) and contrasted favourably with 3-habit competitors ('some apps make the free version so debilitating you have no choice but to delete or buy. But this app has a great free version'); more than five habits is the leading reason among satisfied payers; M2: keep it, never shrink it. Report 56: unlimited habits named by 4, always against competitors — 'without limiting me to preset habits or a specific number without paying first' (AR); 3 left competitors specifically over caps. Report 58: unlimited free habits against rivals' caps — 'Finally a habit tracker app where you can add more than 5 habits for free!' (HR); 'all the other apps like tell me I have to pay to put more things on the checklist' (SA); 'when we normalised that a habit tracker app, doesn't allow us to track habits?' (UY); 14 praise the absence of a cap. Report 59 (Tappsk): a 2-habit / 2-recurring free cap is the most frequent objection in every era — MON_FREE_LIMIT 697 (4.59%, Very strong, 3.82★), the top 3★ theme (80 of 481), third in 4★ (247), and 'great app, but only two habits free' is the typical 4★ (praise + price objection share 601 reviews); 'two habits is too few to evaluate' ('неинтересно так пробовать'; '2 alışkanlıktan fazlasına premium istiyor', the most-voted Turkish review); the report's experiment is raising the cap to three (reviewers propose three or five) and stating the caps on the listing, predicting fewer 1–3★ with no loss of lifetime purchases because purchases are driven by discounts, not the cap (13 of 1,090 purchasers cite it); SA, TR, SE and ES over-index on the cap complaint. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a 3-habit free cap is the most-named boundary — 4 of 45 (8.89%) and all four say 3, rated 5★ / 3★ / 2★ / 1★ ('Just a small suggestion to add… at least one more free task as we already have 3 but having 4 as free will give edge to the app', 5★; 'the free version only allows tracking 3 habits… so I ended up uninstalling' after a paragraph of praise; 'Only 3?????? … this app is useless') — 'not a complaint from people who dislike the app; it is a wall that people walk into on their way out'; the use cases described (water and steps, walking, three concurrent religious practices) need 4–6 habits, so the cap bites before the product proves itself; steady across 17 months; M1: raise the allowance from 3 to 5, or make the 4th habit a time-limited trial rather than a wall. Report 65 (Rabit): the free tier without a 3-habit cap was the positioning — PAY_FREE_OK 48 (9.64%, mean 4.88: 'you can log more than three habits for the free version'; 'te deja añadir más de 3 hábitos en su versión gratuita') — then a cap reported at 3, 4, 5 and 6 in different months of 2023 (PAY_FREE_LIMIT 34, 6.83%, mean 2.00; 26 of 99 reviews in Jan–Nov 2023, mean 1.85) — 'the limit was moved repeatedly rather than set once'; PAY_FREE_OK 15.3% → 2.2% as PAY_FREE_LIMIT 1.2% → 28.3% — 'the same axis, inverted'; two users in 2020 had pleaded in advance not to be capped at three. Report 69 (TheFor): the ledger's clearest case of an uncapped free tier as the moat — PAY_FREE_UNLIMITED 10 (12.50%, mean 4.80) naming the competitor behaviour avoided ('a maioria dos apps permitem de 3 a 5 itens de lista e so liberam mais no premium, esse tem quantidade de hábitos ilimitados no plano free'; 'I've been looking for this 😭'); free-offer praise 19 (23.75%, mean 4.89, none below 4★) rising 5.0% → 23.3% → 47.1% of reviews across 2023 / 2024 / 2025–26 as, reviewers say, the category capped at 3–5 — 'The moat is getting more valuable, not less'; zero cap complaints in 3.5 years; M1: publicly commit to unlimited free habits. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): here the habit cap is one and free — a design, not a monetization lever — and it is defended by the reviewers it limits (148 praise vs 44 asking for more). Report 71 (MyStreaks): a free streak cap reported at 3 active (Jan 2023, a 5★ user 'for over 2 years'), then 2 (Nov 2023, Feb 2024), then 1 (Nov 2024) — reported by one reviewer each, so the direction is reported, not established; the cap is the whole 1★ population (3 reviews, mean 2.00 vs 4.90 for the other 29): 'For an app all about self betterment i thought it wouldn't require me to pay to have MORE THAN 2 GOALS'; the only counter-offer: 'they could make the max like 5 or 10' (4★). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): the cleanest dated natural experiment on a cap in the ledger — reviewers name the free allowance as 3 (to 22 Dec 2024), then 1 (13 reviewers on six storefronts between 23 Dec 2024 and 3 Jan 2025, nobody before or after in 22 months), then 3 again; mean 4.848 → 4.293 → 4.725 and 1–2★ share 0.0% → 17.3% → 4.9%; version 1.0.8 (shipped 2024-12-18) covers 35 reviews at 3.80, the only release window below 4.0; the cap is 11 of 13 1★ and 5 of 7 2★ — 'This app is free but I literally can only make one habit before it corners me into paying'; 'Why download a habit tracker app for the purpose of tracking a single habit?'; 'Three is survivable; it is not comfortable' (8 complaints at 3; 'a limit of 6 habits would have been fine and would retain far more users'); §8.1 #1 'Set and hold the free habit cap at 3 or more. Never 1'; §8.7 'treat that number as a rating-sensitive setting, not a growth lever'. Report 75 (Habit Streak): a 3-habit free cap raised to 5 in Oct 2025 ('You asked, we listened') — cap objections stayed at 2 per era and turned from polite 3–4★ to hostile 1★ at the new number; 5 of 5 1★ reviews are about money and nothing else, four praising the product in the same sentence; a user reached a one-month streak on the free tier and called 3 'perfette per iniziare'. Report 76 (Way of Life): a 3-item free cap held for 16 years; MON_FREE_LIMIT 250 (3.22%, 3.53★, in every era 1.5–6.1%, peaking in E3) vs PR_FREE 249 (4.72★) — 'I actually think three habits is enough'; 'forced me to prioritize the three most important tasks by paywalling more than 3' (5★); cn: 'the free version's limit of three habits is actually better'; the cap is the #1 purchase trigger once the free tier has delivered value ('found myself wanting to add more and shelled out the $5'); 2★ reviews are 25% MON_FREE_LIMIT; 1★ 18.78%. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): a one-habit free cap — cap objections 4 of 71 (5.63%, mean 2.50★), all in the second half of the corpus (zero in the first 42 reviews, 4 in the last 29; the corpus cannot say whether the cap tightened or merely became visible); 'add one habit, then be interrupted repeatedly'; the report does not recommend raising the cap because converters are invisible, but notes the differentiator cannot be experienced at one habit ([[C296]]); E2 in §8.6: held-out cohort at cap=3. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): a 3-board free cap held for 770 days and converted on its own ('upgraded for more boards and to support the developer'); MON_FREE_GENEROUS 10 at 5.00★; the same cap read as a wall only after the widget left the free tier ([[C297]]). Report 83 (Roubit): an 8-routine free cap with a praised free tier (FREE_GENEROUS 14 vs FREE_LIMIT_ROUTINES 12); PAID_FOR_ROUTINES 3 ('the unlimited routines really make all the difference') — the cap converts a few and is tolerated by most; its value has been changed at least four times. Report 84 (HabitGrid): unlimited habits with no IAP — 'most of them only let you make around 4 habits before tealling you to pay. This one let me make as many as I wanted (10 so far)!'; two Russian reviewers searched 'a very long time' for a free app 'with unlimited habits and a clear chart'; U:paywall_contrast 16 (18.60%), all 5★, sets the app against the category's cap-then-pay default. Report 86 (Today): the clearest natural experiment on cap size in the series — the free tier went 1 → 3 (Mar 2016) → 5 (2017, n=1) → 1 (~2022): at one habit MON_FREE1 78 reviews at 1.97★ (71 in 2016 alone, the dominant theme of the first fortnight), raised to three within two weeks and noticed within a day ('because they actually listened to there customers I just paid full price for it!'), then zero one-habit complaints for four years (2017–2020); narrowing back to one in ~2022 re-imported the complaint in the same words ('you can only track ONE habit with the free version… If they had just advertised this as a paid app, it would have been fair', 2★); three-habit complaints (67) average 3.60★ — 'the same grievance, attached to a tier three times wider, arrives with a rating 1.63 stars higher'.

title: Daily check-in and reminders are free — never paywall the reminder
statement: Core loop must be free; it draws no complaints when it is. Report 13: exact-clock reminder times behind the paywall was the single most resented gate in an eleven-year corpus (227 requests); free users got only Morning/Afternoon/Evening buckets. Report 25: a specific clock time per habit with a notification at that time — not a generic reminder — was absent and is the top request from satisfied users (29; 4★ band 9.0%). Report 47: reminders free throughout and praised by 10 (all 5★ — multiple times per habit, editable text). Report 48: unlimited custom reminders per tracker with the user's own message text are free and praised by 224 (5.09%, 4.87) — reminders faulted by 78 at a stable ratio. [Merged from C257: Report 42: reminders sit behind the paywall and are the feature most often named as the thing behind the wall (5 reviews, mean 2.60 — 'I just wanted to use the habit reminder feature and that would cost me 40 a year? Come on. That's insane!'), while working reminders are praised at mean 5.00 (6); three reviewers independently conclude the phone's own tools substitute — 'better to use the native Lista app on iPhone… doesn't freeze and is free'; 'the paid version adds a reminder — you can set that in the calendar too'; 'Your alarm or reminder on your phone can do everything this app does. Wasted $20!' The report calls un-paywalling reminders 'the most defensible single paywall change'. Report 43 (counter-case): reminders, including the nag, are free and the app's reason to exist; only the habit count was ever gated. Report 46 (contrast): reminders are free; the paid gates are habit count, dark mode, offline use and sync.] Report 65 (Rabit): notifications were never gated, yet a reviewer asks whether they were — when the reminder breaks for everyone, free users read it as a paywall. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'you're only allowed to set 3 habits and you can't even get notifications for them' (Nov 2024) — 'a habit tracker whose free tier cannot remind you is not a smaller product, it is a different one'; §8.1 #3 verify and ungate. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): notifications were absent and requested in 2023–24 ('有料でもいいので' — 'even if paid'), then praised as present in 2026. Report 76 (Way of Life): reminders are free and praised (PR_REMINDERS 351, 4.83★) but the praise fades from 6.6% of E1 to 1.8% of E6 as reminders become table stakes; per-item reminders were requested for eight years (REQ_REMINDER_PER_ITEM 51, 2011 → 2019) and the request stopped when they shipped.

merged_from.title: Never paywall reminders — it moves the comparison from 'which habit tracker' to 'why pay for an alarm'
merged_from.note: C257 (report 42: reminders behind the paywall were the gate most often named, and the phone's own alarm substitutes) is the rule form of C008's free-tier line; reports 13 and 25 on C008 already showed exact-time reminders were the most resented gate

title: Basic widgets, icons and colours are free
statement: Loved, drives 5★, and re-paywalling widgets backfired. Report 7: with every widget Pro, the widget paywall was the only theme with zero 5★ reviews, while widgets were the best-loved feature; users proposed one free widget, more with Pro. Report 12: widget requests appeared only from Nov 2024 and came from retained payers ('I forget all the time to use this app cause I don't have a widget') — the highest-mean complaint theme. Report 23: custom app icons and theme colours (324, 4.46%, mean 4.51) are 'a small feature with an outsized delight response'; 54 more ask for more/custom icons. Report 25: widgets (Home, Lock Screen, Control Center) are almost purely positive (30, mean 4.43, 0 1★); custom icons and colours with hex input; one lifetime buyer asks for a minimal heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples. Report 26: a garden-view home-screen widget, reminders, a timer and day-of-week scheduling are free (21 widget mentions, mean 4.14). Report 29: colour coding per habit is free; 4 ask for a wider palette and custom colours. Report 34: widgets requested for 3.5 years (11.1% of E3) became the top new praise on launch (11.2% of E4), then were paywalled for some users ('Cant use widgets without subscription', 1★) — the report's advice is to keep at least one widget and basic colours free. Report 36: widgets gated in Oct 2023 (WIDGETGATE 14, mean 2.64) are load-bearing for adherence — '62 days in a row … wouldn't be possible without this app and it's widgets'; 'Ojalá los widget fueran gratuitos eso mejoraría el apego' — and reviewers accept paid skins but not paid widgets ('I can understand locking skins behind a paywall but ALL widgets???'). Report 41: interactive widgets (111 mentions, 13.62%) are the most-praised surface, stronger in the US (17.4%) and GB (18.8%) than DE / CA (~9.9%). Report 42: no widgets at all, framed as a competitive deficit — 'it has no widgets, so it loses against the rest of similar apps'; 'It's a paid app, so I have higher requirements… PLEASE add a WIDGET section' (a payer). Report 43: the widget is what makes the app work for the ADHD / accessibility segment — 'if I have to seek it out a lot of the time it's not happening. I can miss notifications, but not if it's on my Home Screen' — and is named a protected surface. Report 46: interactive widgets are free (contested) and rose from 0.81% to 3.98% of praise — 'I barely even open the app'; the widget holds four rows and the free tier three. Report 47: a widget was requested by 20 (3.40%) in every era 2019–2026 — the most-requested capability — and shipped in 2025 as a free surface; 'please make a widget that makes me want to continue', Duolingo the benchmark. Report 48: widgets arrived ~2020 and interactivity was later removed (12 praise at 5.00, 20 requests, 14 widget bugs). Report 52: premium icons, themes and some colours are paid and are both a purchase reason (161 payers at 4.50; DES_THEME lift ×3.65) and the top payer request (DES_ICON_WANT 561, lift ×2.83) — icons removed in 2024 and 2026 are asked back. Report 54: colours, pots and reminders gated resented (8, 3.00); more icons / colours / pots / themes requested (17, 4.35). Report 56: widgets free where 'free apps often have chopped widgets, or widgets just gated behind a subscription'; cosmetic limits (icons, colours, descriptions) cost two of four 4★ — 'i would have a 5 star rating if a few small changes could be made'. Report 57: dark mode Premium-gated ('shell out $13 for premium just for dark mode') against a photosensitive user; a colour picker praised by 22. Report 58: icons / emojis and colours / themes are the only repeat request (3 + 2) and what a 3★ asks for ('I feel like the app is depressed I hope you add colors') — ship the baseline expansion free first, and only then consider paid packs, because selling what a 3★ calls missing reads as a paywall on a deficiency. Report 69 (TheFor): 'having the free widget is awesome'; WID_GOOD 4 at a perfect 5.00. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_WIDGET 41 (0.53%) from 2014-11; the 2023 removal of the old Today widget drew NEG_LOST_FEATURE 7 ('Any updates on when the widget will be fixed?', 3★); widgets shipped for iOS 17+. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): the widget arc — requested by the very first review (2025-01-10), shipped and praised 33 days later ('Great widget too for each habit'), then reported behind the paywall ('You have to pay for widgets', pt 1★, the whole review, single-source) and found too narrow (one habit per widget); U:widget_gap 5 (7.04%, 3.80★); §8.2.2 'a widget is the cheapest daily-retention surface a habit tracker has, and this one is gated and limited to a single habit at the same time as the free tier is limited to a single habit'; §8.6 E7 ungating the widget. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): interactive, stackable widgets are the app's perfect-score feature (PRAISE_WIDGET 27, 15.70%, 5.00★: 'The widgets are a game changer'; 'thanks to the widgets, I was able to easily keep a track of my study habits'; 'Widgets work effectively without needing to go back into the app'); gating them in 2025 produced the angriest reviews (MON_WIDGET_GATED 2) and a proposed compromise of two free widget sizes; REQ_WIDGET_MORE 5 (smaller/compact widgets) shipped in v2.5.0. Report 84 (HabitGrid): free interactive widgets are the third concrete strength (PRAISE_WIDGETS 8: 'keep a widget on my home screen, and tick the specific habit… and that's it!') and the only feature on both sides — 2 of the 7 problem reports involve them (a counter increment landing on the next day; only one widget with one habit); a reviewer asked for widgets five months after the first widget praise; §8.4 do not move widgets behind payment. Report 86 (Today): the Notification-Centre widget shipped Oct 2016 after a day-two request and became the main way many used the app ('son Widget super bien pensé'); the home-screen widget never shipped in 5.5 years — 'they urgently need a widget and I swear I'd pay premium' (mx 4★); 'its lack of a widget means I'll probably need to look for something else'; a reviewer asks for one 'for IOS 26'.

title: Backfill missed days / edit start date
statement: Users accept a bounded free backfill window. Report 8 contests it: a ~7-day backfill window in a free app with weak history views was the worst-rated request (mean 3.52). Report 16: logging only today and yesterday cost earned streaks ('I forgot to log 2 days ago… my streak is permanently reset'); 33 requests from mostly 3–4★ users, unshipped for 31 months. Report 19: 'I did the habit so why can't I go back and track it?' — back-dating a completed habit was broken or absent. Report 23: 'today or yesterday?' retroactive completion and calendar backfill are included; backfill older days still requested 76 times (1.05%). Report 24: cannot undo a tick or backfill a missed day (70, mean 2.700) — the emotional cost is disproportionate because it breaks streaks the product made meaningful. Report 26: backfill the previous day and a configurable day boundary (29 verified, 0.76%) — night-owl and after-midnight complaints recur across five years; a next-day 'did you do it?' prompt exists and is praised. Report 27: backfill by tapping past dates is praised (and broke for the annual grid in 2025); two reviewers want to import an existing streak by start date ('the streak being automatically completed from that date, moving to a new phone was a bit tedious'). Report 30: editing history works inside the current month but not for prior months (asked politely by a 5★). Report 34: back-filling and long-press to mark yesterday praised by 10 (mean 4.90); editing days from the month calendar requested by 6, and one US reviewer left over it. Report 41: a payer upgraded specifically to backfill an 8-day streak and backfilling did not exist (1★); can't backfill / edit past days 5 (mean 3.40). Report 43: backfilling a day after it has passed requested by 4 (mean 3.75). Report 47: back-dating shipped 29 March 2020 after being 16% of 2019 reviews and is praised as available by 7 (all JP); the start-date-before-creation option exists but is hidden — 21 requests (3.57%), last July 2026, two reviewers could not find it after reading it existed; see [[C262]] for the 2024 video gate. Report 54: backfill only to yesterday — 15 (4.07%, 3.67); 'deleted on the second day because of the issue' (UA); if the schedule says Mon/Wed/Thu and you worked out Tuesday, you cannot record it at all. Report 55: log earlier days including before install — part of the praised tracking model. Report 56: back-dating existed but was hard to find — requested in June, 'a little hard' in July, 'super easy' in August. Report 57: past-date check-in went from top complaint (13, 2019–20: 'if you forget to track something you're just out of luck') to differentiator (4 praise at 5.000: 'ridiculously easy to add data for previous dates') — the one confirmed fix-to-differentiator in the corpus. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_BACKFILL 62 (rising to 0.8% in the latest era) — unfinished tasks roll to today and cannot be marked done for the day they were done ('если я выполнила задачу в 00:01 и хочу отметить её выполненной за предыдущую дату' — did it at 00:01 and want to mark it for the previous date); the report's experiment: mark done for a past date. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): any past day can be edited and a premium buyer was actively using the edit-previous-day buttons when the June build broke them; the counter-request is a lock, not removal. Report 65 (Rabit): marking the previous day was the capability premium took at launch (Nov 2020). Report 75 (Habit Streak): no backfill — 'j'ai commencé une habitude il y a une semaine et pour l'instant j'ai 0 % de réussite… j'ai pas la possibilité de marquer ce que j'ai fait avant… ça me décourage' (5★, the only helpful-voted review, asking twice for a reply) — 'the only request in the corpus that is demonstrably causing disengagement'; E5 measure D7 retention of users who backfill. Report 76 (Way of Life): NEG_BACKFILL 39 (0.50%, 3.79★, 2012 → 2024, 'hard to log past days'; jp 4.22×) against PR_BACKFILL 8 at 5.00★ once possible; REQ_FUTURE_ENTRY 9 want to mark future days; REQ_DAY_ROLLOVER 9 want a custom day end. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): back-dated entry exists but bulk back-entry is painful (UX_BULK_ENTRY 1, 5★). Report 84 (HabitGrid): marking past days is praised ('You can mark progress for past days and add a note. Ideal'). Report 86 (Today): REQ_BACKFILL 18 (2016 → 2021) — 'partially, then made harder'; the Nov 2018 redesign made checking in for an old day three taps.

title: Weekly / monthly / yearly reports
statement: The #1 stated reason people pay; under-counted by keywords, dominant in the qualitative read. Report 25 (counter-evidence): paywalling all statistics — success %, graphs, per-habit calendar — averaged 1.40 and 'removes the motivation loop the category sells'; keep the basic progress view free, sell the deep report. Report 31: charts once unlocked are a named purchase trigger ('excited to see them … upgraded immediately'); stats 145 mentions, called weak by power users who want all-habit overviews, weekly totals and % of days. Report 33: statistics praised by 182 rated 4–5★ ('The statistics … is what sold me') and a named purchase trigger; 58 request an all-habit weekly grid, raw totals and multi-year history ('I want a GitHub type chart'); yearly and daily-ratio stats were removed in Habitify X. Report 34: statistics requests 14 (1.88%) — month %, all habits in one grid, counts rather than streaks; the free stats screen is 'a bit too simple'. Report 36: statistics / counts / year-in-review requested by 10, the newest rising request (4.6% of E5); one reviewer counts completions per month by hand. Report 41: statistics are Premium ('in free version… No statistics'), named as a purchase trigger ('love statistics now visible'), and 'better / deeper statistics' is still requested by 9. Report 42: statistics are the actual premium value proposition — three of six named purchase triggers ('Seeing the progress percentage of habits and which days they were done… because I found it in this app I bought the premium version'; 'The detailed stats in premium version are worth it') — while the same feature miscalculates for non-daily habits (a payer) and history is capped for free users. Report 43: percentages, grades, streaks and the green / red calendar praised by 55 (8.62%, mean 4.82) — 'Thank you for %'s and grades. This is how my brain works… I'm actually completing it so I can stay at a 90% grade' — free. Report 46: stats praised by 54 (mean 4.91 — 'I exercised 60% of the time, wrote 80% of the time'); richer statistics requested by 11 (4.55). Report 48: better reports / trends is the top open request (76, mean 4.07, still open Aug 2026) and comes almost entirely from people who like the app — the report's candidate next paid feature. Report 52: year statistics moved behind VIP in Dec 2025 and drew a one-month complaint window; the report's M3 test is a free basic year summary with a paid detailed report, a split one reviewer asked for verbatim. Report 53: extended statistics are a named purchase reason ('bought premium with extended statistics', ru) and the paid feature that broke. Report 54: long-range history requested by 28 (7.59%) and per-habit stats by 16; 48 unique (13.01%, 3.83) want 'proof that they have been consistent, over a period longer than a week, for a habit they can name' — the second-largest need after the paywall. Report 56: analytics / charts requested once in a fully free app. Report 57: weekly / monthly / yearly reports praised by 24 (the yearly report called unique); history of past reports requested by 11. Report 65 (Rabit): performance charts over time (REQ_GRAPH 2, 5.00) and a completion-% score beside the streak. Report 69 (TheFor): 'só sinto muita falta de análise de dados, gráficos dos hábitos, como no aplicativo concorrente Ripples' — the only named competitor, named for better charts. Report 75 (Habit Streak): more statistics requested (Apr 2025); an Insights screen with weekly / monthly / yearly views and a heatmap shipped in v1.57.1 six months later — no review mentions it. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_STATS 72 (0.93%, 4.19★), REQ_DATE_RANGE 22, REQ_CHART_CUSTOM 8, REQ_CALENDAR 29 (calendar view, 3.93★) — more statistics and other time ranges on top of free charts. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_MORE_STATS 1, REQ_MULTI_GRAPH 1 (compare several habits in one graph), PRAISE_STATS 5 (4.40★: 'good line graph view'). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): PRAISE_ANALYTICS 9 (streaks, consistency, charts) at 5.00★; REQ_ANNUAL_VIEW 1 partially shipped in v2.7.0. Report 85 (Habitica): an eleven-year-old gamified tracker still lacks history and statistics — REQ_STATS 71 (2.06%), REQ_CALENDAR 33 ('if it had a calender for the habits and I could see how many days in a month I completed the task' carries 14 votes, more than any other request); §8.6 hypothesis: 'users who can see progress outside the avatar keep using the app past the point where the game content runs out'.

title: Week / month / year grid views
statement: 'Filling the squares' is the retention mechanic and emotional payoff. Report 23: statistics limited to the current and previous month (46 requests); the most-requested visualisation is a year heat-map / GitHub contribution grid, the single most-named competitor gap (Habitify). Report 25: statistics weak/unreadable (8) — rework the screen around 'why did I miss it'; a heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples requested. Report 26: statistics/history/calendar per habit was the top unmet need (40, 1.04% — 'this is a cosmetic habit tracker, it does not offer really understanding of progress'), something shipped ~late 2024, and the rate returned to 4.26% of substantive 2026 reviews because it is hard to find and stats cannot be reset. Report 27: daily, weekly and yearly views exist and a monthly view is the missing rung — requested five times over four years, the only feature request that repeatedly costs stars (2 of 6 3★); the year grid is the app's signature and its de-emphasis was noticed. Report 29: statistics (bar, pie, weekly analytics, completion rings) is the one advanced surface praised unprompted (10, mean 4.60) and asked to be extended — all-time records, a monthly/yearly grid, export — the safest place to add depth without violating simplicity. Report 30: per-habit and per-day completion percentages requested; history editing works only within the current month. Report 34: the per-habit year grid / 'year in pixels' / GitHub-style heatmap is the differentiator — 105 reviews (14.13%, zero 1★), 'the only habit tracker I could find with a whole year view'; 'Don't Break The Chain only makes sense if you can actually see your chain!' Report 46: a habit × day grid whose squares deepen in colour with each consecutive completion is the product — 228 reviews (10.47%, mean 4.86): 'Because I don't want the gradient to break, I'm motivated to check in every day'; 'Anybody that like seeing a git commit graph will love this app'; 'not ticks to check off but areas that fill with beautiful colours — so I don't feel stressed about not managing something' — praised at a near-constant 9.68–11.62% for eight years. Report 47: a dot grid that fills — and keeps what was filled — is the retention mechanic: 67 (11.38%, mean 4.70), rising to 17.1% of 2025–26 reviews ('マスが埋まっていくのを見るのが、地味に達成感を感じてとても良い'); calendar / month view praised 9; a combined all-habit overview calendar requested 6 (mean 4.50); the month view showing only a week is a payer's bug. Report 58: daily / weekly / monthly / yearly progress views with unrestricted history are an adoption reason for 5 ('you can see all of your history not just a month back'). Report 59 (Tappsk): habits show a week, not a month — 'Не нашел полноценную сводную статистику по всем привычкам' (no proper summary across all habits, 3★); REQ_STATS 114 (1.3% of the latest era); the experiment is a month view per habit. Report 60 (Mindway): a routine planner sold without any consistency view is judged 'just a to-do list' by 10 reviewers including 5 payers; the minimal fix proposed is a completion % plus current streak plus a 30-day grid (E4). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): statistics are not on the main screen and have to be sought out — named as a reason a 4★ is 'consider[ing] other options'; P6: reachable from the main screen without adding clutter. Report 69 (TheFor): the heat map is 'quite gimmicky' — tapping a day should show which habits were completed that day (REQ_DAY_DETAIL). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a History of completed cycles is praised (PR_HISTORY 31) while others want a calendar view (9) and a done list / time log (7). Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): the weekly grid is the unit people praise (5), and a monthly view is the third request (6) — 「月ごとの表示機能」 named as an immediate-purchase condition. Report 76 (Way of Life): the at-a-glance grid of green/red/grey cells plus charts is the second-largest praise (PR_INSIGHTS 838, 10.79%, 4.80★) and the #2 purchase trigger (14.3% of 349 purchasers: 'This is the only app I bought the paid version for, and I regret it not at all'); honesty through colour is the motivator — 'keeps me from fooling myself into thinking I did better than I really did'; 'I hate to break a winning steak'; PR_ACCOUNTABILITY 477 (6.14%). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): a calendar exists but does not show hits and misses — U:calendar_gap 3 (4.23%, 3.33★): 'my habit in a calendar graphic'; 'the calendar part doesn't operate well' (kr); a monthly hit-and-miss view is what replaces the streak's achievement feedback. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the GitHub-contribution grid is the product ('you've filled in every box for the first month, then you realise you've formed a habit'); PRAISE_ANALYTICS 9 (5.00★) after 'das neue Update mit den Analytics'; advanced analytics moved from paid to free in v2.4.0. Report 83 (Roubit): statistics and weekly reports ship; PRAISE_ALL_IN_ONE 23 — one user deleted separate to-do, goal and diary apps. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the grid is the app's name — 'remind me of github, very beautiful'; 'progress by day, week, for the year, clear statistics, beautiful visualisation. You can mark progress for past days and add a note. Ideal'; 'It is very motivating when you see your progress for the year'; U:visual_progress 16 (18.60%), free. Report 85 (Habitica): the avatar is the only progress view; REQ_CALENDAR 33 and REQ_STATS 71 ask for the grid/history that every other tracker in the series has. Report 86 (Today): the streak calendar card is the record users protect ('changed the check-in marks on the calendar from a fully filled-in square to a TINY dot', 2★); REQ_DASHBOARD 70 want all habits on one screen; statistics live in a profile screen found 'by accident'.

title: Cloud sync / multi-device as the paid differentiator
statement: Strongest true differentiator among buyers (lift ×9.8). Report 7: absent for 3+ years, sync was the #1 3★/4★ theme with named willingness to pay; ship it opt-in and end-to-end (CloudKit private database) to keep a no-account privacy promise. Report 28: cloud sync is bundled with any purchase ('I now realize just buying anything gives u cloud access'; 'il faut payer pour jumeler les comptes'); multi-device sync is named as the advantage over Finch. Report 30: iCloud sync and colour themes are advertised paid features that no reviewer in any market or period mentions. Report 33: one purchase covering iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, web, Android and Windows is a leading purchase trigger — and every platform that lagged became a support case (see C251). Report 47: account-based e-mail backup and sync (beta 2020, free in 'version 2.0', Feb 2024) spans iPhone, Android and iPad ('애플이랑 삼성 연동'); cross-platform sync unreliable in 2022; sync / backup failures 16 (mean 2.25, 7 in 10–18 Dec 2019 — '同期中ですとの表示が一向におわらず'); a platform bundle is a stated purchase condition ('Macのリリース、ウィジェット導入、iPadとの同期を求めます。そしたら課金します', 2026). Report 48: cross-device sync is the paid feature most often named as the purchase reason; multi-platform praise recovered from 0.78% to 3.13% with the Mac app (Mar 2022), yet sync failure is the one reliability theme that never improved (11 / 12 / 12 / 13 per era) and is the most common reliability complaint in 2022–26. Report 50: one account across iPhone, iPad and Mac, free within the cap. Report 54: iCloud sync / backup absent (8, 4.12) — 'I don't give it 5 stars because it lacks iCloud sync'. Report 55: cross-device sync was the headline paid feature and the most often named purchase reason (19 of 165 payers), mostly in 1–2★ because it failed ('If you are about to buy it for the sync option. I suggest you keep your money'; 'Paid £17.49 to sync phone/iPad/watch and it doesn't work'); SYNC_BUG 62 (1.90) with a 7.12× payer lift and 'servers are dead' by 2019. Report 56: optional iCloud sync shipped free and headlines a positive review ('Simple, free, privacy friendly - optional icloud sync'). Report 57: cross-device is the largest unmet need in the product's history — 72 (9.24%): sync 44, iPad 21, Mac 8, backup 17 — flat across eras (29 / 28 / 27) and 84% Korean; one JP report of iCloud working (2024) against six later Korean 'it doesn't'; a Premium user in 2026 'I bought Premium and iPad doesn't seem to sync'. Report 58: cross-device use requested by 2 (a 3★ whose whole review is 'so I can work in two different places') against 2 who chose the app because it has no account — if sync ships it must be optional and never a precondition for first use; accounts and servers bring the 1★ failure classes the corpus is free of. Report 59 (Tappsk): iCloud sync between devices is Premium and reviewers ask for it free ('в бесплатной версии синхронизировать устройства нельзя'; 'оставить синхронизацию в бесплатной версии'); the Mac app was sold separately in 2020–22 (MON_PER_DEVICE 59: 'Она платная для тех кто уже премиум?') and later folded into Premium. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'looked really promising and reasonably priced, but does not let you sync between your Phone and iPad' (US, 1★) — a willing buyer who did not buy solely for this; 'revenue-blocking, not cosmetic'. Report 65 (Rabit): platform_gaps 55 (11.04%, mean 4.25) — widget, Watch, iPad, desktop, sync — 'Rabit exists on exactly one surface'; SYNC_REQ 4 (4.75) and the entitlement failures share a root, no reliable account layer (S6). Report 69 (TheFor): sync_any 5 (6.25%, mean 4.20) — the corpus's only 3★ ('Love that the free version includes unlimited habits. And the paid version is a great price. However, needs to be able to sync across devices'), two 4★ iPhone ↔ iPad failures, two 5★ 'lack of iCloud sync… a notable drawback'; every one otherwise positive — 'the cheapest kind of rating to recover'; rising 0% → 7.0% → 11.8%; M2 / X1: sync is 'the classic additive premium feature' and Pro's first describable benefit. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_SYNC 139 (1.79%, 4.01★) in every era for 14 years, second most frequent request, 2.72× over-represented among purchasers; 'at this point I would pay to sync' (5★); 'A five star app without iCloud support is a one star app' (gb 1★); 'Five stars if I could open the app on any device and see my data' (3★); REV_STAR_TACTIC 19 make the fifth star conditional; §8.5 ship iCloud sync to iPad before a Watch app — sync is the paid feature reviewers say they would pay for. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_ICLOUD 2 (4.50★) — iCloud sync / backup / an account; the only account mention in 71 reviews is a request for one; 'I totally recommend it' from the 4★ who wants sync between devices.

title: Multiple reminders per habit
statement: Moderate purchase reason; first reminder stays free. Report 25: an optional intra-day recurring reminder (every N minutes until completed) requested by 4, including a paying user's medication use case. Report 31: multiple reminders per habit were paid in the one-time era and are among what buyers value after paying. Report 33: multiple reminders per habit were moved to Premium in 2019 and cited as a paid feature buyers value ('With the premium subscription, I can add multiple reminders'). Report 47: multiple reminders per habit with editable text are free here and praised by 10 (all 5★). Report 48: several alerts per day per tracker with user-written text — 224 praise (4.87), free. Report 55: early iOS builds allowed one reminder per day while Android allowed several. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_ADVANCE_REMINDER 68 — earlier or multiple reminders per task. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): one reminder per day only — 'Please make it possible to have reminders several times a day, so you can set a reminder to drink water or walk steps' (TJ, 3★). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_REMINDER_PER_ITEM 51 (0.66%) from 2011-04 to 2019-03 and zero after — consistent with per-item reminders shipping; REQ_REMINDER_REPEAT 9, REQ_REMINDER_SCHEDULE 8.

title: Shared / group habits
statement: Strong purchase driver where it exists, but the worst-executed feature — demand is proven, execution is the risk. Report 23: task sharing / accountability partner exists but is described as weak and one-way; social layer requested by 28 (0.39%). Report 24: in-app community ('Circles', 370, mean 3.897) and time-boxed group challenges exist; the word 'God' being blocked in Circles drew 14 complaints. Report 25: friends / accountability / leaderboard requested by 10 fans (mean 4.80); no social feature exists. Report 26: eight Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of the discontinued '种子习惯' (Seed Habit) app. Report 31: social / shared lists / family to-do requested by 49 (mean 3.27); a parent tracking attention to each child. Report 33: challenges, friends and sharing (2022+) are mixed (challenges 19, some gated), and the report recommends hiding them until enabled. Report 48: shared / partner accountability requested by 22 (mean 4.45), including a coach who would move 100 clients onto the app if it existed. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_SHARED 65 (0.43%) never stops across eight years; the listing advertises sharing a task to a friend's Tappsk, praised by only 5. Report 71 (MyStreaks): sharing streaks with a spouse, family and students (SOC-SHARE 3) — 'share with friends, students and people I want to be accountable to or vice versa' (a teacher / coach use case); comment replies and posting into Groups requested or buggy (2023). Report 85 (Habitica): parties that fight quest bosses together, where a missed Daily damages the whole party, are the strongest social-accountability mechanic in the series — PR_PARTY 158 (4.59%), party praise held at 5.0% of reviews even after the public community was removed; 'In my group, we keep each other motivated'; NEG_SOLO 16 want a party finder; BUG_SOCIAL 78.

title: Skip / holiday / pause mode (pause a habit or counter without losing history)
statement: Minor purchase factor; free or paid open. In report 3, pause/stop/archive is the highest-leverage missing feature (44 requests at mean 4.02, 'the only thing between me and 5★'). Report 23: pausing a task and un-pausing it marked the paused days as missed and destroyed the streak — the defect defeats the feature's entire purpose; reported 2023–24 with no visible fix (57 archive/pause mentions). Report 25: vacation/pause, skip-a-day ('Jump'), mark-not-done ('Cancel') and archive all exist and are praised. Report 26: a vacation/pause mode is requested with flexible recurrence (12). Report 27: a goal end date so a completed goal stops repeating but stays visible, and habit archiving, were asked for by a 3★ reviewer — both appear on the listing and were not findable. Report 28: 'the only way to remove a habit from view is to delete it, but that results in losing all its data'; one wants to mark a routine as 'established' and retire it. Report 29: an end-date / no-end-date control requested (4) — set a habit with no end and change it later. Report 30: there is no habit end-date, so deleting a finished habit wipes its history, and Skip breaks the daily completion ring so users feel they failed a day they completed — one frequency + end-date feature closes both. Report 31: every-N-days, bi-weekly, skip, vacation mode and end dates requested by 84 (mean 3.12) — 'lose a 100+ day streak because … vacation'; a streak freeze is named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: pause / vacation mode never existed (18 requests; a 'reschedule' swipe) — the report asks for a pause that preserves streaks. Report 34: skip / pause / sick day requested by 5 ('i am sick and cannot swim … i dont want to loose my results'). Report 46: skip marks — a half-square and a triangle — with a 'don't skip twice' rule are praised by 41 (mean 4.93: 'no punishment other than a break in the color gradient') and confuse 19 for seven years ('What does the triangle and squares mean?????'; a subscriber who will 'cancel until this is fixed') — a legend reachable from the grid. Report 48: no skip / vacation mode (13) and weekly goals that still demand a daily answer (21 weekday-scheduling) are 'the two structural scoring complaints', sustained across all five eras from otherwise-happy users — report's change #10. Report 50: streak freeze / habit pause is the most-requested missing capability (3, mean 4.33) and archive (2) — 'It makes me feel guilty for losing my streaks, but like sometimes your routine has to change for a few days!'; 'it's much easier for me to continue a streak when it's large rather than from ground zero'; skipped days visually distinct (1) — the report's S4: ship freeze / pause / archive together as retention mechanics. Report 53: the most-upvoted review in the corpus (274 votes) asks for archive / pause — 'to keep my page organized I have to delete some habits, which means losing all the records'; skips that don't count as failures (CORE_SKIP 20, 4.20). Report 55: a sick / skip day that keeps the streak (CORE_SKIP 5). Report 57: a skip / rest day shipped mid-2024 ('which I've been eagerly waiting for') but only reachable from the calendar step and still requested after. Report 65 (Rabit): S3 — skip / exempt a legitimately impossible day without killing the plant (CORE_SKIP 2), 'turns the gamification's biggest liability into a fair mechanic'. Report 68 (Ultiself): 'flagging a day as sick day' (4★). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a two-day-miss reset with no pause — 'sometimes you can't do it when you're unwell' (1★); 「生理が来ると、2日くらいお休みしたい人も中にはいるのです。」 (period); a school trip; REQ_PAUSE 10; §8.6: a limited honest rest day (e.g. two per cycle) plus an optional strict mode — 'Both camps have existed since 2018, so a single rule will keep losing one of them'. Report 76 (Way of Life): a skip state that keeps the chain is loved — 'skip option for when you have days where you need to skip without breaking your chain'; PR_SKIP 99 (1.28%, 4.66★); the request REQ_SKIP (7, 2011) stopped the moment it shipped (2012-05). Report 85 (Habitica): 'rest in the inn' pauses the health penalty but is undiscoverable (PR_REST 6, REQ_PAUSE 7); §8.9 an illness mode. Report 86 (Today): REQ_SKIP 11 (illness, travel, a bad mental-health day) + REQ_ARCHIVE 11 — the corpus's most-upvoted request (22 up / 36): 'could you add a way to stop a habit? Sometimes a habit is already formed or no longer needed, but currently you can only delete it, and all the data goes with it' (cn 5★); 'the design forces a user who succeeded to destroy their record of succeeding'; a skip exists and 'nobody understands it'.

title: Passcode lock
statement: Minor; decide whether needed at all. Report 31: a passcode / Touch ID lock was moved behind the paywall in 2019; privacy / passcode 16 mentions. Report 33: the passcode lock was removed in 2025, a lifetime holder's complaint. Report 55: passcode lock exists; Touch ID requested (LOCK 6), including in Germany. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_PASSCODE 12 (4.92★). Report 69 (TheFor): 'The only thing keeping me from 5 stars is the lack of a passcode and/or face id lock fuction' — one feature, one star, explicitly priced. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a passcode lock exists and is valued (PR_PRIVACY 4). Report 76 (Way of Life): passcode / Face ID lock ships (PR_PASSCODE 7 at 5.00★) and lock-outs are rare but severe (BUG_PASSCODE 7: 'LOCKED OUT OF APP', 1★). Report 86 (Today): the passcode / biometric lock is a paid feature, objected to on principle by one, crashed the app when enabled in March 2018, and leaks the habit list through the widget and background resume — 'a paid privacy feature that leaks is worse than none'.

title: App-icon themes
statement: Minor purchase factor. Report 23: the alternate app icon is frequently cited as a delight (included in the one-time price). Report 33: per-habit colours and themes requested by 48 ('I dislike blue … would pay more'). Report 65 (Rabit): an autistic user asks for an alternate app icon — 'não combina com quem quer ser produtivo… Sou autista e ele me incomoda muito' (REQ_APPICON 2).

title: Quit-habit / bad-habit mode
statement: Well received where shipped; see Quit Habit Decision research doc. Report 23: negative ('don't') tasks shipped in v3.0, Jul 2017. Report 25: a 'bad habit' mode exists and counts against the cap; a bad-habit limit exceeded at 200% is scored as success; a long review asks whether to name it 'smoked' or 'didn't smoke'. Report 31: build and quit habits in one list is praised by 96 ('the ONLY app I've found that does that'); quit-to-zero goals were removed in Mar 2022 and Jan 2023 (sobriety tracking), and 30 find quit/zero-goal habits confusing — restore them. Report 33: bad-habit / limit tracking done well requested by 23 — a tap per cigarette, auto-fail over the limit. Report 34: bad-habit / quit tracking 6 — 'I'd rather not see TO DO next to bad habits'. Report 36: a quit-a-habit inverse mode requested once. Report 41: break-a-bad-habit mode (max units per day) praised by 36 (mean 4.69); Screen Time as a trackable bad habit requested by 4. Report 43: negative / 'avoid' habit tracking requested by 3. Report 46: a habit-breaking mode (colour fades when the bad habit is logged) is praised by 42 (mean 4.98) — alcohol, sugar, screen time — though its logic is unclear to some. Report 48: bad-habit / 'less is better' tracking (a limit, not a goal; red / green inverts) praised by 105 (2.39%, 4.81) — a quit-smoking reviewer benchmarked 10+ rivals; yes / no semantics turn ambiguous in bad-habit logging (12). Report 50: a quit / reduce mode with a reset-on-relapse counter praised by 6 (4.83) — trichotillomania ('The fact that I have to reset the tracker every time I "fall back" gives me the more motivation'), drinking. Report 52: bad habits that deduct reward points (78, weak, mean 4.8). Report 53: limits and zero goals — 'no more than 3 coffees', count-down counters (CORE_BAD 21, 3.76). Report 54: quit-habit tracking requested (4). Report 55: quit-habit use for smoking, alcohol, nail-biting and NoFap (USE_QUIT 46, 4.83) via 'not more than' goals — 'a nail biter for 26 years but getting to tap yes! everyday is exactly what I needed to finally stop'. Report 76 (Way of Life): good and bad habits in one grid, colours inverting for habits to avoid — 'it reverses the red/green colours for yes and no' (5★); PR_YESNO 73; USE_ADDICTION 46 at mean 4.96★ ('Today marks 1 month clean'); REQ_NEUTRAL_HABIT 5 want a third, neutral kind. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_NEGATIVE_HABIT 2 (5.00★) — negative / inverse boards, both German, 17 months apart, same design (smoking; unfulfilled days as the streak) — 'opens the quit-habit use case the product currently cannot serve'. Report 86 (Today): a limit-type habit is the missing shape — 'if I only want to limit my intake to, say, two sodas a day, I can't both log each drink and show success for not going over the limit' (5★); REQ_BREAKBAD 15; USE_QUIT 16 (soda, meat, smoking, drinking).

title: Data export / backup / CSV
statement: Requested a lot from happy users, rarely a purchase trigger — charging for it generates requests, not revenue. Report 18: export was asked for from the app's fifth month to its last, named as a purchase condition twice ('add export and I'll subscribe for life'), and is the honest answer to five years of unresolved data-loss reports — it lets users protect themselves. Report 20: export never shipped (9 requests, mean 4.44). Report 23: CSV export is included in the one-time price. Report 25: CSV export exists but is described as weak (3). Report 27: data export is praised ('export data for nerdy kind') and the one-tap note export was removed in 2025, producing the only 2★. Report 28: no export mentioned; cloud sync paid. Report 29: add a local CSV/JSON export to Files, account-free, so a date bug can never again mean total loss — three independent export/backup requests. Report 31: backup to Dropbox/iCloud and CSV export were manual only with a repeated backup nag; export hangs ('I can't export my data to move to another app because it hangs on the CSV export') — export is the exit door, keep it open and fast; export to Google Drive was a purchase trigger. Report 33: CSV export was removed with Habitify X (Aug 2020) and back from 2022. Report 34: CSV export disabled in Feb 2026 ('Out of nowhere … years of data are stuck in this app'; 'Vendor Lock', 1★) and a paid backup required before deleting (1★) — both data-lock-in reviews are 1★ (mean 1.00) in a no-account app where export is the only exit. Report 41: CSV export shipped Feb 2023 after a year of requests ('Now that the developer has added CSV export… the app is 5-star awesome for me') and is named as a purchase reason ('so my data is safe'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 42: no export or backup; history beyond ~2 weeks paywalled ('if you don't pay you won't see last month's result'). Report 43: CSV / PDF export requested by 2; no export exists in a local-storage app that lost four-year histories. Report 46: export / backup / print requested by 3 in an app that lost users' history. Report 47: sharing / export requested by 3, RecStyle named as the CSV model. Report 48: CSV export is premium, praised and occasionally broken (16 requests, 4 export bugs). Report 52: data export requested (59, weak). Report 55: CSV / Excel export is paid and bought for; 5 of 15 export reviews report failures. Report 57: backup is manual Dropbox (Jan 2020) and Premium-gated — 'so you can't back up at all unless you buy — this is practically blackmail'. Report 65 (Rabit): backup moved behind the paywall in 2023 while restore failed for payers; zero export requests in six years. Report 76 (Way of Life): CSV/Excel export is free and praised (PR_EXPORT 50, 4.84★); NEG_EXPORT_FORMAT 4; REQ_IMPORT 6. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): CSV export praised as 'no lock-in' (PRAISE_EXPORT 1); REQ_IMPORT 2 (5.00★) — data import / migration 'directly reduces switching cost into the product, and pairs with the existing CSV export'. Report 83 (Roubit): no export or backup request appears in 500 reviews — until the diary tab blanked; §8.1 offer diary export as the fallback for a multi-year personal record. Report 84 (HabitGrid): import/export exists per the listing and is mentioned by zero of 86 reviews; the one data-safety warning and the one account request both come from users who did not find it. Report 86 (Today): 'Manage Data' export/delete shipped May 2018 ('Kudos for the new Manage Data section… If only more companies would follow suit'); REQ_EXPORT 14; a twenty-item 2016 request list asked for Excel export.

title: Apple Health integration
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent. Report 23: HealthKit auto-completion (277, 3.81%, mean 4.35) is 'the single highest-leverage integration in the category' — it removes the friction that killed every other habit app the reviewer tried; a weak tail of misfires (auto-completing without action 11; Health data miscounting 9). Report 25: two-way Apple Health is a purchase trigger (32, 2.44%) with a weak tail of demonstrably wrong mappings — weight read as an entry count, steps off by 568, running only measurable in minutes, step counting starting at 04:00 (9, 0.69%). Report 27: Apple Health integration (exercise, water, steps, sleep) requested once, 4★. Report 31: Apple Health integration covers ~10 preset tasks (steps, sleep, exercise minutes); 79 mentions (mean 2.85); Health sync named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: Apple Health auto-logging and Fitbit, Strava, screen-time and NFC habits, described as both free and Premium; Health integration complaints rose to 2.2% of E5 and Garmin / wearable auto-completion is requested. Report 36: Apple Health requested by 3 — a 10,000-step habit that auto-completes. Report 41: Apple Health auto-completion (53 mentions) is a switch reason ('Coming from Grit, I almost instantly bought it because the Apple Health habits actually work') and a payer failure ('I paid for it specifically for synching with the health app'); Health gaps 8. Report 43: Apple Health integration requested once. Report 48: Apple Health auto-logging of steps / weight and Siri Shortcuts voice logging praised by 17 (rising to 1.56% of 2022–26); 3 Health sync bugs. Report 50: Health auto-tracking of steps, calories, distance and exercise with historical import praised by 7 (4.71, 5 US); 5 (4.60; 4.50% of US) want weight, sleep, mindful minutes and Apple Fitness session types synced instead of hand-entered — one says weight sync would move the rating to 5; a Health sync break after an update (1). Report 53: Apple Health integration is what reviewers could not find elsewhere (HK_GOOD 40 — the Watch Breathe app 'automatically marks that as complete'; calories logged from the wrist) and they ask for more sources — sleep, running, calories, blood pressure, Fitbit, Garmin, Strava (HK_WANT 31). Report 54: Health app / Fitbit sync requested (2). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'It doesn't communicate with iPhone Health-fitness; it said it did' (TR, 2★) — if the listing promises it, an expectation mismatch, worse than an absent feature; I5: make the link work or remove the claim, the cheapest immediate fix. Report 64 (Critique AI): Apple Health and Hevy sync requested with exercise animations (us, 3★). Report 68 (Ultiself): Apple Health integration and automatic tracking are the long-term users' top asks (REQ_HEALTH 9, REQ_AUTO_TRACK 2); §8.8. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): Apple Health integration exists and is the only subsystem with more than one failure — the connection 'has not worked' for a lifetime buyer (2★) and 'the app crashes when adding Active Energy' (inside a 5★) — while a third asks for more of it (REQ_HEALTHKIT 2, 5.00★): wanted and, at least twice, broken; no reviewer says which tier it needs. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_HEALTH 1 (4★). Report 86 (Today): PR_HEALTHKIT 38 — 'EVERYTHING that is in your Apple Healthkit can be displayed and values for can be entered… I tried all popular health dashboards and activity tracker, but this is miles ahead'; a weight graph and a distance-swum card (jp); REQ_AUTOCHECK 11 (auto check-in from Health) never shipped.

title: Apple Watch app (done properly: timer, two-way sync)
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent; a half-built Watch app draws 2–3★. Report 20: an Apple Watch app was the highest-mean capability gap (62 requests, mean 4.15), asked for by the happiest users and named in churn-to-Streaks reviews; never shipped. Report 23: the Watch is the app's strongest differentiator and most fragile surface — 626 mentions (8.61%), 241 negative (mean 3.13) vs 385 positive (mean 4.35); it breaks on each watchOS generation (2016, watchOS 7, 2021–22 mirroring, watchOS 10 complications, 2024–26 blank complications); in Korea (13.5%) and Japan (13.3%) it is the dominant topic; 'I bought this for the Watch and it doesn't work' are the highest-value churn events. Report 24: in a 43,469-review coaching corpus the Watch (69, 0.16%) and widget (53, 0.12%) are marginal — the surface matters where the product is a checklist, not where it is content. Report 25: the Watch app (21 mentions, mean 4.48, 0 1★) is part of a praised Apple-platform surface (Watch + Mac + widgets + Shortcuts + Health), but one reviewer says it was 'suddenly removed' (Oct 2025) and another that the listing advertised Watch support that could not be installed. Report 26: no Apple Watch app throughout; requested by 8 (0.21%). Report 27: Apple Watch, Apple Health and macOS are each requested once (4★ 'Would be perfect with watch support'); the report says a paid tier, if ever, should attach only to such not-yet-existing capability. Report 31: the Watch app and complication were broken for long periods — 60 reviews (mean 2.33); support asked for a video, then silence; ''update coming soon'. 6 months later'; the v2 rebuild (Mar 2022) broke it and restored it months later. Report 33: the Watch app broke with iOS 13, would not launch after Habitify X, its complication broke with iOS 15.1 and sync lagged until 'finally' fixed Jan 2024 — 100 reviews (2.84 mean), 6.8% of E3, Japan 5.0% ('Streaks costs a tenth and works'); single-tap logging and area complications were removed. Report 36: Apple Watch requested by 9 (mean 4.11), one wanting the haptics on the wrist. Report 41: the Watch app shipped in 2021 on request (discussion peaked 13.7% then normalised); a privacy-minded payer cancelled because Watch sync requires iCloud and will return for 'easy normal Bluetooth sync between the phone and the watch'. Report 43: Apple Watch requested by 12 over five years (May 2019 'Not using your app due to lack of iwatch' → Jan 2024), the listing now ships Watch, and no request appears after Jan 2024. Report 46: Apple Watch shipped Mar 2021 and the request stopped (3 → 2 → 0 → 0); Watch ↔ phone sync is then a failure surface ('finished goals on the watch won't show up on the phone and vice versa… a deal breaker'). Report 47: Apple Watch requested by 6, all 2020–22; the listing shows iPhone, Mac and Vision only. Report 48: Watch app and complication praised by 24 (4.67) when working, faulted by 12 (2.33) when blank; 8 want a complication. Report 50: a Watch app shipped Jan–May 2025 after requests ('almost perfect, it just needs a watch app'); one 1★ calls it useless — no habit complication, notifications not working. Report 52: Apple Watch check-in requested every year since 2019 (PLAT_WATCH 256, 1.24%, 4.52) — 'one reviewer bought a Watch for this app'. Report 53: Watch complications configurable 'almost like watch faces themselves' are a purchase trigger (WATCH_GOOD 43, 4.70) while WATCH_BUG 62 (2.85) — duplicate water entries, sync, the Watch app crashing on launch in 2025–26; F6: re-certify the Watch app on every iOS release. Report 54: no Watch app (9, 4.22) — 'now I'm forced to use another app' (DE); 'lemme know if you're working on the watch app and I'll be the first one to buy this app' (PK). Report 55: no Watch app (PLATFORM_WANT 24). Report 56: an Apple Watch app requested once. Report 57: a Watch app shipped ~Mar 2020 ('moved to see it on the Watch') and hung on 'Loading…' for 26 (19 in 2020–21), then was largely fixed (0.94% of 2024–26). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_WATCH 81 fell from 4.7% of the launch year to 0.0% of the latest era as PR_WATCH 37 appeared — a request that stops is the trace of a shipped feature. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an Apple Watch app requested once (UZ, 4★); treated as absent as of Jan 2026, lowest priority of the set. Report 65 (Rabit): REQ_WATCH 5 (1.00%, mean 3.80) — two frame the Watch as how they would actually get reminded. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'will make it 5★ if Apple Watch is supported' (REQ_WATCH 5). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_WATCH 54 (0.70%, 4.30★) appears from 2015-08 and replaces the iPad request from 2016 (E5 1.8%); §8.5 ranks it after iCloud sync to iPad. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_WATCH 1 (5★). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_WATCH 3 (4.33★, 2024-12 → 2026-06) — 'quasi unentbehrlich' for fast capture; 'Bitte ganz nach oben auf die Prioritätenliste!!!! (dann gibt's auch ✱✱✱✱✱)' (4★); the listing is iPhone-only; §8.3 'the app's whole value is low-friction check-in and the Watch is where that friction is lowest'; §8.7 whether the Watch actually converts or is a stated preference. Report 83 (Roubit): Apple Watch requested only from Korea (within REQ_IPAD_WATCH_MAC 15); a paying user defected to a rival 'cheaper and works with Apple Watch'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): REQ_WATCH 2 (2.33%), both recent; the developer told one reviewer he would try; 'two requests do not justify building one' — check the developer's own Discord/Reddit where requests are cheaper. Report 85 (Habitica): REQ_WATCH 67 (1.94%), in every era from 2015-12-07 to 2026-04-29 — the longest-running unshipped request in the corpus; a Wear OS version exists ('It doesn't make sense that Habitica hasn't released for Apple Watch but Wear Os'); §8.8 a watchOS companion for checking off Dailies and Habits. Report 86 (Today): the Watch app was requested for 14 months (REQ_WATCH 34 from 2016-03-11), shipped ~May 2017, and never worked properly — BUG_WATCH 88 (4.93%, 2.98★) vs 21 praising it: check-ins revert ('I tap an icon to say I've done it, then 20 minutes late it's unchecked again!!'), phone and watch disagree, the complication works on one watch face; Infograph complication requests recur for seven years unanswered; watchOS 5 broke it ('Broken since iOS 12 / watchOS 5… App hasn't had an update in nearly 2 months'); a purchase trigger for one ('I bought this app for the watch incorporation') and a condition for others ('I will gladly pay for the full version but I really need it to work on my watch') — 'a shipped-but-unreliable companion app is a larger negative than its absence'.

title: Interactive widget check-off
statement: Mark done without opening the app; small volume, very high intent. Report 18: 'let me check off without launching the app' was the single most-repeated widget request across five years and every language; some builds fixed it (Jul 2025) and then it regressed. Report 23: an interactive Today-view widget shipped Jan 2017 to enthusiasm, was lost at iOS 14 (Sept 2020) and asked for back continuously for five years (36 named requests) — one of the top three reasons for a downgrade from a previously-happy user; restore it via App Intents. Report 26: an interactive widget to tick from the home screen requested (~5); the garden-view widget is free. Report 27: reviewers wrote the widget spec — 'a small widget that just showed the current streak count for a single goal'; 'a streak counter on the widget like duolingo'; 'a grayed out version if it's still to do and a coloured version if it's done'; tappable to check off — requested in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; in a streak app the widget is the retention surface. Report 28: an interactive check-off widget requested continuously for four and a half years by satisfied users (mean 4.64, zero negatives). Report 29: a Home Screen widget showing today's list requested by 16 across 26 months, 7 of them in 2026. Report 31: a tappable Today-view widget (2018–2021) was replaced in Oct 2021 by a non-interactive home/lock-screen widget limited to 4 habits (a user with a memory disability 'requesting a refund'); before that, the app had no iOS 14 widget for a year — 73 of 451 reviews (16.2%) Sep 2020 – Sep 2021 and 14.0% of E2 asked about it; the widget peaks in the 4★ band (12.6% vs 3.8%). Report 33: the 2016 Today widget was removed ('the entire reason I paid'), iOS 14 widgets were non-interactive, and the May 2025 redesign removed compact, incremental (+1) and streak widgets — widget complaints 6.3% of 2025, the one surface still worsening; interactive widgets named as the 4★ → 5★ piece. Report 34: 7 interactive-widget requests, all after static widgets shipped (Mar 2024) — 'The widgets still aren't interactive' (Feb 2026). Report 36: 'instead of taking advantage of the iOS 17 update with interactive widgets, they preferred to make that option paid' (2★); interactive widget requested by 4. Report 48: widget interactivity was removed after arriving ~2020; the request persists (20). Report 50: widgets with check-off shipped by Nov 2024 after a Mar 2024 request; interactive check-off, quick-append journal, compact and weekly-progress widgets still requested (3); widget lag (1). Report 52: 'Maybe the most important features of ShineDay are its widgets. Being able to check off completed habits without opening the app' — when iOS 14 replaced tap-to-check with a ring that opens the app (Oct 2020) 55 widget-bug reviews arrived in one month; check-in was removed from the widget again in 2026. Report 53: check off from the widget, hide completed, more habits per widget (WIDGET_WANT 18). Report 54: the top request (41, 11.11%, 4.29; P1 7.5% → P3 17.6%, open since Oct 2020, first asked one month after iOS 14), 19 of them five-star and a named purchase blocker for 3 of 5 ('If there were a home-screen widget I'd open it far more often — then I'd be more willing to buy', TW); framed as retention by ADHD and autistic users ('once it's closed i never use it'); D3: build it as a completion surface, not a display surface. Report 55: widget or notification check-off requested (WIDGET_WANT 16). Report 56: per-habit home-screen widgets with one-tap completion are the differentiator (9 of 67 name them; 'the empty dots on my home screen guilt trip me into being productive and honestly? it works'); a multi-habit widget designed in detail (dates across, habits down), more than 4 widgets and transparency requested; a widget tap that opened the app instead of completing broke the most-praised interaction (fixed in v2.3.2). Report 57: the widget tap launched the app instead of checking in from the iOS 14 rewrite (Nov 2020) until Dec 2023 — 16 reviews ('if it's a widget the check should happen right there — why is the app launching?'; 'give us back checking from the widget'), zero after. Report 58: 'THE WIDGET that is clickable?? the best ever'; 'The widget option is legit a life saver!'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a widget that shows the next unfinished habit is requested (UZ, 4★); widgets are credited with the strongest outcome statement in the corpus. Report 69 (TheFor): after the free widget shipped, the next ask (the most recent review, 2026-09-02) is interactive — 'a widget that allows me to see all my habits and their progress and allows me to check them off'; B2. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): some users keep the habit and lose the app — 'I couldn't even keep up opening this app every day' (12 votes); 'This is no different from a game's daily login bonus'; widget requests (17, 0.3% → 2.4% of eras) ask for the goal to be visible without opening the app (§8.8). Report 71 (MyStreaks): 'Home Screen widget for quick check-off… that is literally my only feedback' (5★, Apr 2023) — still absent after 25 releases, 'the cheapest item… open the longest', aligned with the most-praised mechanic, the 3-click check-off. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a widget requested 2023 → 2026 while the listing now claims widgets — possibly discoverability. Report 75 (Habit Streak): three of the first six reviews asked for a widget; it shipped by May 2025; demand then moved up the stack — complete a habit from the widget ('aus dem Widget heraus… als erledigt markieren'), the streak on the Lock Screen ('el fuego con el numero de días… en la pantalla bloqueada'), milestone widget art at 7 / 30 / 60 / 90 days citing chess.com; 8 of 41 (19.51%, cohort mean 4.75) touch the widget — 'the retention surface'; what users want on it is the streak number itself.

title: Streaks / gamification
statement: High-priority praise, moderate purchase factor. Report 10 (contested): streaks added to a non-punitive pet app generated their own defect stream (171, growing 74×) and pressure stream (96) — net-negative in the written record for an ADHD audience. Report 20: a streak counter was requested 71 times (mean 3.72) — always alongside, never instead of, the decaying strength score. Report 23: streak psychology is the highest-satisfaction theme (902, 12.41%, mean 4.75, 0.7% 1★ — reviewers get out of bed to preserve a streak); rewards/badges/levels are requested by fans (136, 1.87%, mean 4.43). Report 24: streak counters with 'freeze' passes and certificates; Duolingo is named for its streak freezes. Report 27: streaks are the core praised mechanic in a deliberately non-gamified app — no pets, no flashy graphics, no urgency; behaviour-change outcomes ('I'm on a 9 day vacuuming streak!') rose 0% → 11.9% across eras. Report 28: gamification (carrots, levels, rooms, a pet) is the differentiator in an 821-review corpus — but 10 (mean 2.40) say 'it's a game, not a tracker', an expectation mismatch the listing could pre-empt. Report 31: motivation through bars filling, streaks and sounds is praised by 200 rated 4–5★ ('an adult sticker chart!'); removing the streak count from the main list in v3.0 drew 52 complaints (100% E4), including medication and 30-day pill-cycle users; the report proposes a streak-on-list toggle and testing its default on logging frequency. Report 33: motivation / streaks praised by 130 (mean 4.75); non-daily streaks broke and the streak count on the complete button changed in redesigns. Report 47: the streak resets to zero on a miss — praised as motivating by 3 (5.00) and non-punitive framing praised by 4 ('scoring points, not losing them') vs empty squares demotivating 1; a cumulative total was added by 2025 after 2020–21 requests. Report 48: streak motivation 144 at mean 4.96 — the highest of any theme with n > 100 ('I can't bear to see it go'); 507-day and 1,000-day streaks; gamified rewards requested by 17 (4.47); a 2013–14 points system was disliked (10). Report 55: 'I completed a task because I didn't want to break my streak'; 'over 10K pushups… because I don't want to disappoint the app' — motivation layer 362 (17.89%, 4.86). Report 56: do not add streak pressure, scores or gamification to a product chosen for restraint — one streak request against 'no subscription, no guilt' and 39 restraint reviews. Report 58: streaks praised by 5 ('It's so fun every time I get a streak'). Report 60 (Mindway): the absence of streaks or any progress view is what payers name when they call the product under-built — the 'encouragement' and 'tracking consistency' they expected and did not get. Report 64 (Critique AI): XP, quests and leaderboards are 'unambiguously liked' (8, 1.91%, mean 4.00) and proposed as the free hook ('keep the workout and XP/leaderboard free'), with one sharp dissent that generated tasks 'seem more like XP grabs than anything else'. Report 76 (Way of Life): chains shipped 2015-11 and turned a request into praise — PR_CHAINS 0.3% E1 → 3.2% E4 (56 reviews, 'Chains is going to change my life') → 3.2% E6; REQ_STREAKS fell 18 → 3; REQ_GAMIFY 16 (4.06★) stays small; the red cell, not a reward, is the motivator ('I hate to break a winning steak'). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): gamification — acorns, a squirrel, foxes, achievements, Badges (v2.6.4) and a purchasable Habit Forest (v3.0) — PRAISE_GAMIFY 5 (4.60★), REQ_MORE_GAMIFY 1; a Korean 3★ questions why the squirrel/acorns and the Focus tab exist; Badges are mentioned by no reviewer and the Forest by exactly one, eight months after shipping — 'two headline features, one mention between them'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the counter-position — no imposed gamification is praised (PRAISE_NO_GAMIFICATION 2, 5.00★) and zero reviews ask for social, leaderboard or AI features; v2.4.0 added a toggle to disable streak/consistency stats. Report 83 (Roubit): gamification at its most effective in the series — 'habit app × gacha game' called 'excellent' even by a user uninstalling; PRAISE_GAMIFICATION 76 (15.20%, 4.68★); META_CALLS_IT_GAME 6; Duolingo named both as a nag to avoid ('it's not gonna harass you like Duolingo') and as a widget model. Report 84 (HabitGrid): weekly and monthly streaks shipped in 1.0.16 and no review mentions them; the year grid, not a streak, is what reviewers call motivating.
