Report 85 (Habitica, 3,445 reviews): the fullest gamification in the series — PR_GAMIFY 468 (13.58%, mean 4.72★ vs corpus 3.71); three mechanisms: instant reward (XP and gold on the tick), consequence (missed Dailies cost health, and in a party hurt friends: 'I still have adhd but now I feel anxious that my team could get dmg because of me not doing the dishes'), collection (eggs, pets, mounts: 'I am constantly doing chores just to earn food for them'); U_OUTCOME 502 (14.57%, 4.70★); PR_STICKY 78; the cost side: long-term players say the game runs out ('they are all essentially the same'; 'A progressão fica meio estagnada'), REQ_CONTENT 79 asks for battles and an endgame, and non-gamers still find value (SEG_NONGAMER 21: 'Best habit tracking app, even without the gamification'). Report 86 (Today): 'It doesn't give you confetti or a cookie' is praise; badges and milestones exist and are unremarked; NEG_REDESIGN objected to a shrunken calendar mark — the visual record, not a reward, is the motivator.

title: Scholarship / hardship / discount program
statement: The cleanest 5★ generator in report 1 (91 of 101 mentions 5★); also works around broken payment rails; never switch it off. Report 10: a 'Guardian' pay-it-forward sponsorship programme is one of the only monetisation themes with a positive mean (4.76 across 708 mentions); its one complaint is that there is no visible way to apply. Report 31: ~110 teen and low-income reviewers (2.12%, mean 2.31) in the 2022–23 TikTok cohort ('your target market at this point is us teenagers'; ages 14, 12, 11; a mental-health user who can't work) — lead with a student / low-income price in those markets. Report 34: a 50% annual offer converted ('I paid £9.99 for a whole year - bargain!'), affordability complaints come from students, Vietnam and ADHD users; the report proposes a student / regional price and New-Year sales. Report 36: AFFORD 5 (mean 2.20) — two on disability, a student, and 'there is no way I can afford it without being part of the demographic which can drop 60$ on a reminder app'. Report 41: a high-school student asks for a student deal; a Turkish 5★ says the one-time fee is too much 'at least in my country'; the report proposes purchasing-power-adjusted lifetime tiers in the long-tail storefronts. Report 42: 'I was ready to pay, but it has to be reasonable… I'm sure if you lower the price, revenue will grow' (RU); price objections at $39.99–$59.99 in high-income markets vs '500₽ a year, that's nothing'. Report 46: students and minors ask for a discount ('the only money i get is chore money and i have to wash the windows for it', 5★; a Cambridge scholarship student; 'please offer discount for students'; 'Is there a discount code for lifetime?'); the report's E5 is a student / youth discount; a discount honoured after it expired won a 5★. Report 49: 30 cannot afford it, 12 of them self-identified minors, in a 9+ app marketed on anime social media; an under-18 / student free programme exists but only 3 reviewers know of it — the report's experiment: surface it. Report 52: students without money are a named barrier ('forty-plus yuan, any conscience?', Grade 7; '¥30 when I was a student, ¥80 now'). Report 54: in CN the one-time ¥98 price competes against a ¥3/month anchor (a pricing-architecture problem). Report 57: 'how about a two-week trial then a discount — I'd just pay under ₩20,000'; a Mexican reviewer 'please put a discount on it'. Report 58: budget-constrained adopters ('as a broke student'; 'Good for broke but productive people'; 'I'm a young lady trying to save up') will not convert to a subscription. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): an informal hardship programme — 11 reviewers say the developer gave them premium free after they asked (six cite hardship, student status or being between jobs: 'I reached out to them about not being able to pay right now due to being in between jobs and they offered a free premium!'), all 11 are 5★, 10 of 11 US; grant union 15 (6.00%), all 5★; but it is invisible — others ask for a discount in public, and a 2★ ('I'm to tight for money') and a 1★ price objection are exactly its population; Russia (payment impossible) produced 1 grant and 4 unhappy reviews; §8.1 #4 / E3: surface the route inside the paywall in every shipped language — 'the cheapest available experiment in this whole report'; the cohort shifts the corpus mean 4.612 → 4.587 and must be disclosed as a selection effect. Report 76 (Way of Life): stated willingness to pay differs by market — 12 yuan (cn), 200 roubles (ru), £50 lifetime (gb) — and price objection is 15.5% of cn vs 4.8% of us. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'looking forward to buying it the moment I can afford it' (mx 5★) — an affordability barrier from a user sold on the concept and the one-time model. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 'a monthly subscription which isn't cheap for a student like me' (cz 3★); 'budget conscious buyers' asked for two free widgets (in 4★). Report 82 (Lasting Change): 'The only drawback is the price, especially for retirees or disabled people. It is just too steep' (4★) — the one accessibility-framed price objection. Report 86 (Today): the most self-aware affordability review in the series — 'Why 4 stars — mainly because I'm poor… I hesitated for one day and 22 hours over whether to uninstall… under 10 yuan I could accept. Isn't the point of making an app to let more people use it?' (cn 4★; MON_AFFORD 3); Canada's CA$7 launch price vs US$4.99 drew the highest cap-complaint rate among eligible markets ('$7 in the app world is premium').

title: Handle markets where card payment fails (RU, AR, TR, DZ, PK)
statement: Users who want to pay cannot; a discount/hardship path doubles as the workaround. Report 26: 16 reviews (mean 4.06 — willing buyers, not complaints) cannot pay — 8 Russian ('the trial button is not clickable… possibly because I live in Russia'; cards cannot be linked), 3 Chinese/Taiwanese ('tap subscribe and nothing happens'; a ¥38 tier shown with no in-app path), 2 Vietnamese (ShopeePay / MoMo requested); Russia is 19.18% of the corpus and its highest-satisfaction market — the highest-yield-per-effort monetisation item. Report 42: 'there's no way to pay from Russia' (Jun 2026) — a market with the worst defect exposure receiving paywall pressure it cannot convert. Report 49: dollar-pegged pricing in Türkiye, sanctions blocking cards, no UPI / local payment method (7). Report 52: 2018 purchase flow broken — 112 billing reviews that year, including no Alipay or WeChat Pay. Report 59 (Tappsk): the largest documented case — App Store payment became unavailable to Russian users from 2022-03; MON_PAYMENT_METHOD 74 (72 on the ru storefront, 54 of them 5★ because the reviewers want to pay and ask how — 'не могу оплатить премиум - версию, с кем мне связаться'; 'Вы теряете живые деньги' — you are losing real money); support arranged card or carrier billing case by case within minutes ('в течении 10-20 минут решили'; 'у меня мобильный оператор Megafon') and from 2024 a direct bank-card route is praised ('спасибо, что можно оплачивать напрямую по банковской карте'; 'за возможность альтернативной оплаты подписки для РФ'); the same era brought switchers from Trello and Notion after those services left Russia; the cost is the cancellation gap ([[C210]], [[C112]]). Removing the Russian storefront drops payment-access complaints from 0.7% to 0.0% and billing from 3.2% to 1.4%. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): Apple payment methods blocked from Russia and operator billing stopping in March 2026 made the app unpurchasable there — 'Не показывает цену, выдает ошибку'; 800 ₽ then 1,490 ₽ quoted on two cards, both declined; 'интерфейс красивый, но приложение абсолютно бессмысленно без платной версии'; 5 ru reviews, four in 2026, on the third-largest storefront (any_negative 27.59% vs 14.80%); support granted access case by case; §8.1 #5: fix purchase on ru or route those users to the grant path automatically. Report 76 (Way of Life): the Russian-speaking group (ru + ua + kz, 584 reviews) over-indexes on purchase/restore failures (ru BUG_PURCHASE 3.29×), subscription objections (2.83×) and platform requests (6.5% vs 4.3%) — and thanks the developer most (ru 1.99×, kz 4.06×).

title: Localise early — it unlocks revenue
statement: Missing localisation is the biggest market-specific complaint and a stated purchase blocker; shipping a language visibly converts (Japan). Report 10: localisation is HIGH-PRIORITY at country level in eight storefronts at once (cn 26%, ru 18%, tr 19%, br 13%, es 12%); reviewers say they will not pay in English. Report 13: Arabic is the largest unserved language (20.5% of Saudi reviews); users were also served the wrong language ('I am from Turkey but this app language is Korean', 41 votes) and shown store screenshots in languages the app does not have. Report 18: Japanese Instagram ads led to an app that opened in Korean with a KakaoTalk login; Korean push notifications persisted a year after the UI was fixed, the terms page stayed English-only (one reviewer refused to trial for that reason), Traditional Chinese was largely Simplified wording, and a Dutch translation was unintelligible. Report 19: an Instagram ad ran in Spanish for an English-only app — 'tell me if there's a Spanish version and if not, refund the money'. Report 20: Russian-first UI leaked to Chinese, French and Swiss users, Chinese localisation existed and was later removed ('there was Chinese a few years ago'), and Ukrainian was requested and never added. Report 23: bad German localisation ('Die Übersetzung ins Deutsche ist total fehlgeschlagen') undercut the premium price in the corpus's worst large market (mean 3.62); machine-translated Chinese help text drew 52 upvotes and was still cited seven years later; localisation-quality complaints span de, ru, se, kr, cn, tw, jp and es (mixed EN/ES notifications, English-only icon search); a Hangul IME bug went unfixed five years. Report 24: the praise vocabulary (small steps, coaching, art, 'life-changing') appears in every language and the forced-water complaint in six; language requests concentrate in Vietnam, Uzbekistan, Russia, Brazil and Italy; Germany praises the app's craft at 19.61% (3× the corpus); China (1,250 reviews, mean 3.431, 28.6% 1★) is unreadable by an English-anchored classifier. Report 25: localisation demand is new and growing (0% → 1.0% → 2.7%; Turkish 9, Korean 3, Italian 3, Russian/Ukrainian 3, Chinese 2, Japanese 1); Korea and China are 100% 5★ and 75%/50% localisation requests ('If there is Chinese, it will definitely be loved by the Chinese market') — reached only by users tolerant of an English UI; Turkish shipped Jul 2026 and the review stream responded. Report 26: localisation requests in Arabic, Thai and Spanish; Russian localisation quality criticised in 2023 ('hire a competent localiser') and praised by 2025; the German store listing carried a typo ('Gewohnheitstrinker' — habit drinker); Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of a discontinued app ('种子习惯'); the cn aesthetic rate of 3.12% is a classifier artefact. Report 27: localisation is not an issue — zero complaints across seven non-English reviews; the two Monday-week-start requests (DE, AU) are the only regional-convention issue. Report 28: 21 localisation requests/defects (2.56%) — Spanish 5, Turkish 3, Chinese 3, Japanese 2, Russian 2, French, Thai, Arabic, Portuguese; two are defects on an existing localisation (Japanese glyphs rendered for Chinese, habit names truncated; untranslated English with Chinese selected) and a 2022 localisation update rendered every 'r' as a black square; rest-of-world markets rate higher (4.181 vs 3.956) and are 5× more blocked by language (5.56% vs 1.09%) — 'the cheapest lever in the highest-satisfaction segment'; two name language as why they leave. Report 29: the listing supports 8 languages and not Spanish or Russian, yet 8 Spanish-language reviews arrive from UZ/CL/MX/AR/ES/US and one is blocked ('No puedo cambiar la lengua, ayuden me por favor') — Spanish first is the cheapest defensible localisation case. Report 30: 13 languages functioning and one explicit localisation compliment from Chile; an Arabic onboarding blocker; 11 reviews in a language not matching their storefront. Report 31: 61 localisation requests (1.18%) and French and German reviewers say localisation is their purchase condition ('J'achèterai la version premium quand elle sera traduite en français'; didn't buy Pro because there was no German); China is the happiest storefront (4.09) and the loudest localisation demand (23.9% — '无中文无满分', no Chinese, no full marks); Ukraine 26.7%, Russia 13.6%, France 11.3%; recommended: Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, German, French, Russian. Report 33: localisation grievances are about quality — 「たどたどしい日本語」 (halting Japanese), simplified-Chinese glyphs in Japanese, an offensive German UI string ('Pisst du dabei?'), a lost Russian UI, English-only support replies — 62 reviews (1.57%); Chinese reviewers praise the localisation; Arabic users ask for an Arabic UI; motivational copy read as 'far too American and over the top' in the Netherlands. Report 34: 19 polite localisation requests (none 1★) — Chinese 9, Russian 4, Spanish 2, French 2, Ukrainian 1 — 11 of them arriving in E3, starting the day a free-lifetime promotion reached br, vn, cn and co: promote into a market only once the app speaks its language. Report 36: localisation requests were 7.0% of E1 (six Chinese-market, May–June 2022, plus MX 1★ 'solo esté en inglés me hace perder el interés') and stopped after mid-2022, consistent with localisation shipping. Report 41: shipping Italian and Traditional Chinese (Jun 2026) brought reviewers straight back to rate 5★ ('I ran straight here to give 5 stars'); missing Spanish blocked a purchase ('es por eso que aún no acabo de lanzarme a comprarla'); Russian — requested from five unrelated storefronts — is the largest unserved language; non-English storefronts like the app equally (4.581) but self-report paying at 5.52% vs 9.9%. Report 42: Russian-language support was the original wedge in Russia ('the competitor has no Russian'), and Russia is both the most appreciative and the most defect-exposed market — where users now cannot pay at all. Report 43: all 10 language requests are non-US (4.37% of non-US reviews) — Arabic three times in fourteen months from Saudi Arabia and Oman, each capping the rating at exactly 3★ ('Nice app but it lacks Arabic support, so it deserves ⭐️⭐️⭐️'); Portuguese and Spanish requests appear answered by the listing's five languages; one 'full of spelling mistakes' (GB, 1★). Report 46: the UI reached 15 languages (Catalan praised by name; Turkish requested with 16 votes in 2020 and praised in Turkish by 2022) but the Learn content, videos and e-mails stayed English — 'all the support is in English, which surprised me because the developer is Spanish. If it were in Spanish, I'd consider subscribing' (ES); Arabic and Russian reviewers ask the same; the report: localise content, Spanish first. Report 47: machine-translated UI costs installs in every non-Japanese market — '적절한 한글화가 절실'; notification options rendered as '汽車' and '手冊' ('car' and 'handbook', TW); 'une traduction française faite de façon automatique et de très mauvaise qualité' — installed and deleted; mainland-Chinese terms shown to Taiwan (5 reviews, none Japanese); Korea's share fell from 32 (2020) to 1 (2025). Report 48: Russia (10.13% no-localization, requests 2013–17) and China (12.33%) are the clearest localization signals; a 2022 review celebrates Chinese localization arriving; rest-of-world raises localization four times as often as high-spend markets; the listing reached 10 languages. Report 49: German added May 2025 but 'sprachlich nicht ganz sauber'; the book summaries and meditations stay English-only — 'localise the content, not just the chrome' — requested in DE, KR, JP, ES, BR, PL; Korea reports unnatural translation in 18.2% of its reviews; behaviour-change praise runs 7.69% in Germany vs 18.13% in the US, plausibly a localisation-quality gap. Report 50: Korea — 4 reviews all 5★, two asking for Korean ('Add korean'; a detailed 5★ written in Korean that still cannot use the app in Korean) — the cleanest unmet-demand signal from a small storefront; experiment: localise into Korean. Report 52: incomplete English — notifications, pop-ups and ads still in Chinese on English devices — is the single largest theme in every eligible non-Chinese storefront (us 22.30%, ca 22.95%, au 20.75%; English-primary 22.1% at mean 3.00) and Traditional Chinese is missing in Taiwan (22.89%); unfixed since a 2020 peak; the ADHD / Focus store subtitle reaches a population that cannot read the app. Report 53: machine-translated or mixed-language UI in ru, br, it, se, kr and jp (DES_LOC 19 — 'you need to study more Japanese'; lock-screen reminders alternating Chinese and English). Report 54: habit lessons English-only inside localised UIs ('this software is all in English', CN; 'English texts are not translated', DE); Arabic and full Chinese requested; a German reviewer calls it 'the only habit tracker in German'; outcome language 16.9% in developed markets vs 4.6% elsewhere — 'a behaviour-change tool in developed markets and a cute utility elsewhere'. Report 55: Brazil — several give 4★ 'only because' there is no Portuguese (DES_LOC 8 of 21, 7.7% of br); a Spanish localisation that was available and then removed ('Antes estaba en español y ahora no'); R6: pt-BR first, then Russian. Report 56: the listing claims Korean and Japanese yet 24 of 43 polled storefronts, Japan included, returned zero reviews; non-English reviewers rate 5.000 vs English 4.882. Report 57: Japan is the most price-sensitive and least-localised storefront — 'settings has English and Korean mixed in'; 'I can't understand explanations written in English… the screen is so minimal that [features] aren't self-evident' (1★); incomplete Simplified Chinese (CN). Report 59 (Tappsk): Ukraine is the only storefront where a language request is distinctive — REQ_LANG 8 (7.75×) ask for a Ukrainian interface, which the 17-language listing does not declare (nor Kazakh); Russian is written from 46 storefronts including 59 reviews on the US storefront; BUG_TRANSLATION 7 (a German widget in Russian). Report 60 (Mindway): the paywall complaint appears in 13 storefronts and 6 languages with the same structure and the benefit claims in near-identical words across ten languages — 'Mindway's value proposition translates'; 59 bodies (27.31%) are non-English across 22 storefronts, and 90 of 125 polled storefronts (Japan, Korea, Spain, India, Russia, Indonesia, Philippines) returned zero reviews. Report 65 (Rabit): Spanish requested Dec 2020 ('Solo pediría añadir el español'), also German, Russian and Vietnamese (LOC_REQ 4); a Brazilian storefront user got English onboarding; being in Portuguese with a Brazilian developer is itself valued ('Amoo a pegada brasileirinha do app 😍 me sinto em casa'; DEV_LOCAL 2). Report 67 (Habio): REQ_LANG 41 (2.00%) — the only request at meaningful strength — from the free era onward ('ojalá pronto la pongan en español también'; 'Nur wie kann ich die App auf deutsch umstellen?'); France 13.19%. Report 69 (TheFor): English-only — 'No tiene en idioma español. No entiendo inglés.' (1★, the only 1★ with a cause the developer can remove entirely); 17 reviewers (21.25%) wrote in other languages and used it anyway — simplicity makes it usable without localisation; P3: Spanish, then Portuguese (12.5% of reviews). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 27 languages including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Thai and Vietnamese, yet zero written reviews in Japan, Korea, China, India or Turkey — 'the largest gap between what the app is localised for and where it is used'; no localisation complaint across 138 non-English reviews. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): emoji-search keywords stay English under a Japanese locale, raised by a paying customer — 「有料なのですから、対応お願いします」; a shorter home-screen app name requested. Report 75 (Habit Streak): 22 localisations and 24 of 41 non-English reviews, zero localisation complaints; 10 reviews written in English from non-English storefronts. Report 76 (Way of Life): 25 declared languages; REQ_LANG 13 ask for Chinese, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Kazakh, Galician or a working language switch; BUG_LANG 15 translation errors reported in 8 languages; English is the review language of 78 storefronts, Russian is written from 14. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): one request — '希望能增加中文' (cn 5★, 2025-03-02) — and ZH-Hans + ZH-Hant now ship; zero localisation complaints in six languages; 10 localisations ship but Japan, Australia and Taiwan produced no review at all despite a shipped Japanese localisation. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 16 languages ship, 13 appear in the corpus; a Russian request (5★, 2026-04-24) shipped ~7 weeks later in a 'localized for 10 more countries' release; a UI of icons and grids draws no other language complaints; China produced zero text reviews despite a shipped Simplified Chinese localisation. Report 83 (Roubit): 247 of 500 reviews (49.40%) are non-Korean for an app shipping only English and Korean; Portuguese (26) and Spanish (22) reviews are among the warmest (4.08★, 4.41★) with neither language shipped; Chinese (3) and Vietnamese (1) requests open; §8.7 decide from install data. Report 84 (HabitGrid): release 1.0.9 'Added languages' (2025-10-29) was followed by a 2.7× rise in review rate (2.65 → 7.09 per 30 days) and a new dominant market — zero Russian-language reviews before it, 39 of 73 after, Russia now 43% of reviews and 44% of public ratings, all 5★ ('the best tracker in Russia'); the listing still says English only. Report 85 (Habitica): NEG_LANG 195 (5.66%) is the most-voted complaint in the corpus — four of the six most-voted reviews ask for Turkish (154 votes between them); Korea is a single-issue storefront (40 of 52 reviews, 76.9%, about the missing Korean translation — which exists on Android); the listing declares 18 languages but not Korean or Turkish ('Man, there's even Hebrew but no Turkish'); three problems share the code — no translation at all (Turkish, Korean, Arabic, Vietnamese), translated elsewhere but not on iOS, and broken language switching (screens mix languages or revert to English; BUG_DISPLAY 20 of 63 in cn); §8.3 publish a translation call inside the storefronts asking loudest. Report 86 (Today): Chinese and Japanese localisation shipped Sep 2016 and was immediately criticised ('what the hell is check-in translated as? If you can't translate, add a language option'; the 3D Touch menu and widget untranslated); Traditional Chinese still missing in 2018 and never added (tw 16 reviews); a user posted an iOS Settings walkthrough in a review to force the language; 1,112 reviews (62.3%) are in English but only 595 from the US — 'country-based segmentation and language-based segmentation are different operations'.

title: Culturally complete icon set and calendars
statement: Islamic icons, disability icons, Hijri and lunar calendars, bigger fonts — cheap, and in markets already blocked by localisation.

title: Billing must be exactly right
statement: Wrong amount, double charge, surprise renewal are the fastest route to 1★ (×21 lift); single price shown, no trial-to-charge traps, refunds honoured, receipts clear. Report 19: a 105-review corpus that was 91% one-star and 71% about money — charged after cancelling (19), charged with no recognised subscription (19), double-billed (16), charged ≠ agreed ($29.99 annual agreed, $59.99/month billed), and terms permitting weekly renewal made 'again and again every week' structurally possible. Report 23: nothing supports deceptive billing on a single Apple payment; refund friction (79, mean 1.75, 70.9% 1★) is Apple's process, and reviewers address Apple through the review field. Report 24: charged after cancelling 1,620 (3.73%, mean 1.085), duplicate charges 584, charge without consent 338 (mean 1.047), not visible in Apple Subscriptions 125 — all consequences of billing outside Apple IAP; 1,412 edited reviews are mostly downgrades after a later charge. Report 31: billing-dispute language in 403 reviews (7.77%, mean 1.24) — refund, scam, fraud, estafa, arnaque, Abzocke, 欺诈 in eight languages — with 13 calling on Apple to remove the developer; billing & entitlement integrity rose 1.6% (E1) → 34.5% (E4) → 25.4% (E5): 768 reviews (14.81%, mean 1.30); discount offers checked out at full price in 69 (49 actually charged; '$59.99 crossed out and … $9.99 … My card was charged full price'; support: 'a bug that happens sometimes') — make the displayed price the charged price and audit introductory-offer configuration per storefront (CA, AU, GB, DE first). Report 33: billing integrity 147 (3.73%, mean 2.22) — charged more than shown (¥4,900 shown, ¥5,150 charged; a $39.99 offer charged $48.97; monthly chosen, annual charged; lifetime then an annual charge); billing-dispute register 「詐欺アプリ」, 'Abzocke', 'CON ARTISTS', 流氓. Report 36: all 3 billing reviews are 1★ — a cancellation link that returns 'Cannot cancel subscription' ('roach motel'), an unauthorised annual charge on a disabled reviewer, and five annual fees for one bundle membership with two refunds denied (China) — triaged regardless of 0.56% share as the only consumer-protection records. Report 42: three payers charged without intending — 'immediately charged for a subscription upon opening the app for the first time'; 'auto-selected a package and deducted money… hadn't even tried it' (499k₫); a promotional R$39.90/year that became R$99.90 at checkout — plus a trial that 'won't get the refund even if you cancel two minutes after'; 11 of 29 writing payers (37.9%) request refunds. Report 46: 13 billing failures (0.60%, mean 2.31) — charged on day one of a 7-day trial (twice), a subscription the app would not recognise ('App does not recognize it and won't let me add more than three habits, even after refreshing… On to the next app'; premium on iPad not on iPhone), a wrong amount (CHF 40.45 for 29.95), four refund requests — vs 2 refund references in report 43's one-time corpus. Report 47: 8 billing failures (1.36%) in a 13-payer corpus — premium reverting to free with ads back (3 in January 2021), '400円を2回も騙し取られた' (charged ¥400 twice), 'アプリを開くと毎回「購入に失敗しました。」' (a purchase-failed loop, Jul 2026), an unintended half-year subscription, a crash the moment a trial payment went through. Report 48: billing problem 23 (2.52) — 1 / 4 / 6 / 12 by era, the fastest-growing monetisation fault: charged $39.99 instead of the agreed $4.99; charged the full year at the start of a 7-day trial; charged twice after cancelling before the trial ended, blocking other App Store purchases; 'another active subscriber using the same receipt'; paid subscription not recognised after an update (3); 23 refund requests at mean 1.04★ — the lowest-mean theme with n > 10. Report 49: every overcharge review is a payer — €1.99/month becoming €30 at once, $2/month becoming $70, £25 on top of £29.99, a year charged during a trial, seven months of charges after cancellation (9; payers 8.49% vs 0.73% globally). Report 50: 3 reviews (mean 1.00, all 1★, Aug 2024 → Jan 2026) charged an amount not matching the quote — '$14.99 for the yearly membership' vs a $31.01 bank charge; 'said to be $14.99 after the free trial but I was charged $30 before my free trial was up. This app is a scam'; ~$50 annual auto-charge — the same ~$15 advertised vs ~$30 charged 17 months apart; 'The app does not accept any of my cards' (2 cannot pay) — the only defect class with a 1.00 mean and no exceptions; fix F1 and experiment: instrument price displayed vs charged per storefront. Report 52: 2018–2020 billing defects (261, 83.5% in those years: purchases that spin forever, double charges, ¥12 shown but ¥31 charged); a gb 'lifetime' purchase billed as £12.99/month (2023); a tw buyer of the NT$390 lifetime unlock charged NT$220 when the concurrent trial converted (Aug 2026); an SMS login that subscribed a user to ¥55/month of carrier services (single report, legal exposure). Report 53: unexpected charges PAY_CHARGE 34 (mean 1.38, 85.3% 1★); a one-week trial billed for a year (kr); an accidental purchase on first open. Report 54: a purchase that never unlocked ('I paid for the app and absolutely nothing. It's exactly as it was before', AU; 'Still telling me Become a habit pro!', KR) — 6, mean 1.17. Report 55: 'BEEN TRYING FOR MONTHS TO CANCEL MY SUBSCRIPTION'; auto-renewal on an account the user can't log in to; charged after a trial (PAY_CHARGE 7). Report 57: listed ₩29,000 but the card was charged ₩44,000; ₩3,994 charged after a redeem code. Report 59 (Tappsk): U_BILLING 485 (3.20%, mean 2.30★) is the largest negative that is neither a price objection nor a product defect; even the reviewer's own missed cancellation ('забыла отменить подписку', 5★) lands as a support ticket in the reviews, and refunds are reported both granted ('Все вернули! Оперативно') and refused ('Деньги, естественно, никто не возвращает'). Report 60 (Mindway): billing operations failing is 'a store-risk problem, not a pricing problem' — 11 of 216 (5.09%, mean 1.27, 10 of 11 US): charged for a year without subscribing ('this needs to be reported and i want my money back'), charged after cancelling with screenshots of inactive status, a $0.99 'free trial' billed $39.99 within hours, a 3-day trial that billed a week after cancelling on day two, monthly implied but the whole year drafted; the corpus cannot prove the charges were unauthorized, but eleven users could not tell what they had agreed to or how to get out, and seven of them used a public review as their support channel; all 13 confirmed payers are the only source of every refund, cancellation and surprise-charge report — 'the corpus contains no post-purchase success story at all'. Report 64 (Critique AI): 'On the website it said cancel anytime but it immediately billed me'; 'They say that they give a three day trial but charge you for the full year upfront'; reinstall charged again — PAY_BILLING 8 (1.91%, mean 1.50), 6 of 13 self-stated payers. Report 65 (Rabit): billing_failure 28 (5.62%, mean 1.75) nearly all payers; PAY_REFUND 8 at mean 1.12 — the lowest of any theme — for crashes after an annual subscription, reminders not working after Plus, ads despite paying, a post-trial charge, and two unanswered refund emails. Report 67 (Habio): U_BILLING_HARM 878 (42.81%, mean 1.04; 60.05% of non-seeded) — charged after cancelling 351, trial conversion 173, workbook 189, charged with no subscription 164, duplicate charges 157, amount above shown 55; U_ESCALATION 196 (9.56%): bank / card / PayPal disputes 118 and regulator / police / legal threats 94 (BBB, FTC, ACCC, state attorneys general, OCU, Sernac, Verbraucherzentrale — 'Abofalle'); a card statement under the company name the customer had to research ('Tuve que investigar que aplicaciones tenía GOTOTOP LTD'). Report 68 (Ultiself): MON_EXTRA_CHARGE 632 (14.01%, 2021-02-28 → 2026-09-06, every era), MON_SCAM 747 (16.56%); MON_ESCALATE 189 (4.19%) — card blocks, chargebacks, reports to Apple, police, regulators and lawyers; reviewers teach each other to block the payment in their bank app (REV_TIP 5); 'Leaving is rarely the story; being unable to leave is' (deletion 8 vs escalation 189).

title: Sync must work — and prove it
statement: The paid feature that breaks most; sync failure is ×12.8 over-represented among buyers. Report 13: iCloud sync complaints rose 10× from 2015 to 2021 and ran at 8.9% of 3★ reviews — the fastest-worsening dimension and the defect most likely costing renewals. Report 23: sync is the single largest reliability finding — 348 mentions (4.79%), 223 complaint-framed (3.07%, mean 3.08, 23.3% 1★), only 22 positive; the 2022 migration produced a spike (25 → 60 → 40 → 24 by year) with visible recoveries within weeks and a tail still visible in 2026 — a migration with a long, damaging tail; Germany 10.0%, Spain 10.1%, Sweden 9.7%. Report 25: cross-device sync not updating 14 (1.07%, mean 3.29), flat across eras. Report 27: sync that works but cannot be seen produces data-loss anxiety (4) and sync requests (3 — iPad; 'wish my goals were synced across my devices') in a corpus where the listing says iCloud sync already exists. Report 31: sync / backup / restore fails in 83 reviews ('Manual syncing is so 2010'); real-time iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Watch is requested with the iPad layout, concentrated in the 4★ band. Report 33: account-only (Firebase) sync replaced personal iCloud sync ('Original Habitify was able to sync … over personal iCloud. This has been removed'), with repeated logouts; sync failures 119 (3.02%), 7.9% of E4 — offer iCloud sync as an option alongside the account backend. Report 36: private sync is the resolution of the privacy-vs-sync tension — local-only praised ('not harvesting your data') while sync is the top request. Report 41: cross-device iCloud sync with no account is praised by 90 (11.04%) and fails for 13 (1.60%, mean 3.08) — four of them payers, because sync is the promise the app is bought on. Report 43: iCloud is simultaneously the advertised backup, an undismissable error banner ('iCloud Sign in Error - I can't turn off this message'; 'Constant iCloud Error… Sloppy code') and a backup that did not restore for a payer ('lost everything even though it was backed up to iCloud') — 5 reviews, mean 1.40, none after Aug 2022. Report 46: cross-device sync is a paid trigger ('I did upgrade so the data could be shown and updated on my watch') and a failure surface — sync 15 (mean 3.13), Watch and Mac disagreeing with the phone ('I paid a hefty price to sync with all my devices', subscriber 2★). Report 47: December 2019 sync hanging at 0% (7 reviews in 9 days); a crash loop after logging in to the free backup 6 (Feb 2024 – May 2025, log-out the workaround); registration / login failures 8, six of them from mainland China ('好像需要vpn'). Report 48: sync failure is the only reliability theme that never improved — 48 (1.09%, 2.65), flat at 11–13 per era since 2015, now the most common reliability complaint; the 2015 v3.0 sync rewrite shipped with crash-on-launch (29.55% of the era), duplicated trackers (20) and data loss (25). Report 52: sync is iCloud-only and fails across iPhone and iPad (147 reviews, 0.71%); reviewers ask for account-based sync (132). Report 55: partial, silent or 'only half' sync, a buried manual sync button; multi-device users pay for sync, open the iPad and see partial or no data — 'habitbull is a one device app only. And i have paid for pro. Unacceptable'. Report 56: 'the recent update about sync made my habits disappear, is there anyway I can get them back??' — six days after a sync request; F1: a local pre-sync snapshot and a visible restore path. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_SYNC 61 (5.71× among purchasers — sync is Premium-only) — 'На iphone не работает синхронизация'; the 2.6.2 release notes lead with 'iCloud sync more reliable'; a paid user lost everything and the account ('все записи удалились и больше не могу авторизоваться'). Report 69 (TheFor): an account system exists but habit data does not follow it — 'i've tried logging on and off and deleting and reinstalling the app but nothing works :/'; 'не могу синхронизировать… iPhone и iPad' (BUG_SYNC 3, mean 3.67). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): iCloud sync with no sign-in — only 3 mention sync, none negatively; 'nobody is fighting with it'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): 7 say sync does not work, one Korean reviewer says iCloud sync links her devices, the listing claims cross-device restore — 'Determine which is true, then fix the capability or the discoverability'.

title: Crashes / launch failures
statement: Largest complaint by volume; a two-day launch crash produced more 1★ than years of minor bugs. Report 23: crashes 46 (0.63%, mean 2.80, 34.8% 1★) on three dated bugs — iPhone X freeze-on-close 2017–18, an iOS 14-era freeze, a stuck splash screen 2023–26 — plus Watch-app crashes on each watchOS generation. Report 24: crash / freeze / won't load 944 (2.17%, mean 2.367) — the recurring shape is freezing on the 'first mountain' / Journeys screen on day one. Report 25: a post-onboarding freeze — the main screen stops responding to touch — is the fastest-rising negative theme (51, 3.90%, mean 1.63; 1.3% → 2.9% → 5.8%; 27 of 34 E3 reports in May–Jul 2026; Colombia 18%, Germany 7.8%, GB 0%); iPhone 11 and iOS 26.x named, reinstalling does not fix it, one reviewer says it survived two updates; every one of these users got zero value. Report 26: crash/launch failure fell 3.37% (2021–22) → 0.13% (2024) after a visible engineering turnaround, then a 2026 cluster (n=4, three Russian, two paying — a premium subscriber crashing on the onboarding screen after reinstall) flagged for telemetry. Report 27: a September–November 2025 update-and-iOS-26 launch crash ('Ever since I updated to iOS 26 the app immediately crashes when I try to open') accounts for almost every bad rating the app ever received — all 4 1★, the only 2★ and 4 of 6 3★ fall in a five-week window (window mean 4.162 vs 4.822 elsewhere); fixed by Feb 2026 (mean 4.829, zero 1★); a solo-developer app with no support channel pays for an OS-transition break entirely in public rating. Report 28: launch failure / crash 15 (1.83%, mean 2.40) concentrated in 2022 (orange-screen failure), then a 2026 uptick ('freezing every time I open the app, I think it needs an update to keep up with ios') consistent with OS drift on a build last updated Nov 2025. Report 29: one 2026 launch failure ('Lässt sich nichtmal öffnen'); overall bug reporting fell by two-thirds (22.3% → 6.5%). Report 30: two launch-week crashes (Jul 2025, 'It just doesn't open… on iOS 18.5 and on the iOS 26 beta') and none in the following 13 months. Report 31: the app would not open in 1,052 reviews (20.29%, mean 1.30) in five waves — launch season 2016, intro freeze Oct–Dec 2021, v1.19.0 crash on launch 22 Dec 2021 → ~8 Jan 2022 (918 in the window), a post-update white-screen hang May–Jun 2022, freezes after subscribing 2022–23; devices from iPhone 6 to 12 Pro Max, so not an old-device issue; 1★ in E3 is 66.4% launch failures; the fix did not recur at scale. Report 33: an 11 Sep 2025 'Liquid glass' update crashed on launch on iOS 18 and was fixed in ~1–3 days with no lasting rating shift; in Oct–Nov 2019 Brazilian users could not open the app after purchase. Report 34: the 10–11 Apr 2024 update crashed on launch and was fixed a day later (E4 reliability 6.7% → E5 2.6%); in Feb 2026 a reviewer needed 20–30 launches to load. Report 42: a launch-blocking regression 4 Dec 2024 – 11 Jan 2025 — 7 'won't open' reviews (mean 1.71), 5 Russian inside 40 days, one a payer three months into an annual subscription ('Give my money back, crooks'). Report 43: crash / won't open is the largest single defect (20, 3.13%, mean 2.15; 18 of 20 US) with a persistent won't-open cluster Dec 2021 → Feb 2023 recurring Dec 2025 → Apr 2026; 'after purchasing, the app crashed every single time I opened it'; 'Crashes if you have less than 500MB free'. Report 47: crashes arrive as dated incidents — 19 crash reviews in January 2021 (10 of them attaching a photo, 9–24 Jan), a white screen when typing a custom habit name Oct 2020 → Jan 2024 (13, all JP, mean 1.54), 4 in January 2026 — 64 crash / cannot-open (10.87%, mean 2.84), 13 of 51 crash reviews still 5★. Report 48: two crash crises — iOS 8 / iPhone 6 (late 2014, crash on adding a tracker and on the back button, 20 reviews Sep–Dec 2014) and the v3.0 release (81 crash-on-launch reviews in 2015) — then a 2020 iOS 13 / 14 freeze (25 reviews) that vanished; the crash union fell from 37.3% of E2 to 2.9% of E5 — 'fixed, and stayed fixed… defended, not revisited'; crash / won't open is 23.3% of all 1★. Report 49: a launch-crash cluster (Oct 2024, 37.5% of the window), a 22 May 2025 update that stopped the app opening for users 20–39 days into a 66-day programme (37.8% of the fortnight), a June 2026 crash-on-task-completion wave (32.1% of the month); crash on launch fell 10.2% → 0.0% by E4 while unspecified bugs rose to 7.9% in the new game layer. Report 50: reliability flat and thin (21, 10.24%, no defect above 4 reviews in 31 months) — 'a well-built app and it has stayed well-built… the rating risk… cannot be engineered away'; 4 of 20 one-stars never used the product (crash, would not initialise, login failed). Report 52: crashes arrive in release waves — 175 of 412 crash reviews (42.5%) in six of 110 months (Jul 2018, Oct 2019, May 2023, Sep 2024, Apr 2025, Sep 2025), roughly every 12–18 months, three of them destroying data; a launch crash on iOS 14.x for 20+ days despite a stated iOS 14 floor. Report 53: crash waves at launch (Nov 2017, fixed within days), on iOS 11.3 and iOS 13, an app that quit on open for several days (Mar 2022), and the 2024–26 statistics-view crash (BUG_CRASH 133, 7.63%, 2.82). Report 55: four crash waves each tied to an update and concentrated in one storefront — Jul 2017 (all 12 UK), Jan 2018 purchase and registration (US), Nov 2018 iOS 12 (23 of 24 Brazil), Oct 2020 – Feb 2021 (26 of 30 UK) — BUG_CRASH 197 (9.73%, 2.04, 107 at 1★); the written-vs-public gap tracks incident exposure (gb 1.07★, br 1.18★ vs ca 0.30★, au 0.14★). Report 59 (Tappsk): four dated regression clusters in three years — 2021-10-22→25 an iOS-15-era update left iPhone 6/6+/7 on iOS 12–14 unable to open the app (33 crash reports in four days); 2023-06→10 completing a recurring task closed the app (trigger isolated by a reviewer to the 'show completed tasks' setting, build 2.5.397 named, 'no progress on this bug in three months'); 2023-08→12 the calendar opened on the same month of 2022; 2023-10 freezes after one action — the regression era carries the highest crash rate after launch (2.6%) and U_REGRESSION 296 'produced most of the product's 1–3★ reviews outside billing'; a launch-crash cluster in 2026-05; a locale-specific crash when setting a habit reminder appears almost only in Turkey (BUG_HABITS 19.99×, BUG_REMINDER 11.80×, BUG_CRASH 8.43×; 1–2★ 15.7% vs 5.9% global) with two Korean reports — test reminder flows under each locale. Report 60 (Mindway): only 2 of 216 (0.93%) report a crash, both within five days in 2024-10 and never again — consistent with one bad build; 'the product is barely reported as broken', which is what makes the monetization findings unambiguous. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a 1–2 June 2026 build with broken hit-testing — taps did not register (six reviewers; one found that a swipe still worked) — produced 8 reviews in 39 hours across six storefronts (17.78% of the app's entire written history, 40% of all its 1★, −0.32 on the mean), caught a premium buyer and a $10 buyer one week after purchase, and blocked first-run habit creation ('I couldn't get past the start creating a habit step, the button won't press'); fixed within days (16 reviews from 3 Jun average 3.875, zero tap reports) but 'the regression is closed; the reviews it produced are not'. Report 64 (Critique AI): the one repeated defect is a freeze during AI plan generation (May 2025 and Apr 2026, independently), then on every launch for one reviewer; crashes on every AI review and on the coach tab 'after the update' ('I expect better from an app which costs like 30 dollars'). Report 65 (Rabit): stability union 73 (14.66%, mean 2.04) in release-tied waves — a first-run block (Jul 2021, 46.2% of its fortnight), a crash-on-launch wave (Apr–Nov 2022, eight of 13 from payers: 'Paguei o premium a toa, pq já tem mais de 7 dias que não consigo usar o app'); an unexplained crying-woman sound on every launch ('c'est effrayant') kept as an asset-integrity issue. Report 68 (Ultiself): on 2023-01-04, 13 reviews in one day, 12 saying the app would not load ('App won't even open'; 'the app support link on the App Store also doesn't work'); BUG_LAUNCH 10.7% of that era. Report 75 (Habit Streak): a crash on launch four weeks after release from a user who had 'really loved the simple, easy design' — the only blocking defect; no later crash report; defects 1 → 3 → 1 by era, none since 2026-01-08. Report 76 (Way of Life): BUG_CRASH 39 (0.50%, mean 2.08★) in two waves — 11 on cn in one week of 2015-01 immediately after buying premium, 10 in 2016-05 after an update; BUG_LAUNCH 4; 10.50% of 1★. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): DEF_CRASH_LAUNCH 2 (1.50★) — one a lifetime buyer, one 'the new update, where the app can't even open without crashing' that opened the 70-day one-star window; the last defect report is 2025-08-26 and the 37 reviews since contain none. Report 82 (Lasting Change): zero crash or freeze reports in 175 reviews — the reliability complaint is login and account state; §8.9 do not prioritise stability work. Report 83 (Roubit): U:cant_use_app 88 (17.60%, 3.23★) — blank tabs 40, launch/load 26, login/sign-up 16 (Google and Facebook login, lost items), crash 11, update loop 7; 46 of 62 one- and two-star reviews describe a defect or being blocked; an earlier launch cluster March–April 2023 ('it breaks every like 3-4 days'). Report 84 (HabitGrid): one launch failure 12 days after release ('worked pretty well for the first 7 days and then just stopped opening', the only 3★), never repeated; zero crash or freeze vocabulary since; §8.8 no stability overhaul. Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_CRASH 415 (12.05%, 2015 → 2026) in dated waves after updates; 'The latest 2 versions of the app have ceased to work at all for me. They crash on startup' (1★); crash share 16.2% of reviews in 2015–16 → 2.1% from 2024. Report 86 (Today): BUG_CRASH 126 (7.06%, 2.71★), BUG_LAUNCH 58 (3.25%, 2.26★ — the lowest defect mean); the launch crash under an Editors' Choice feature pinned 228 reviews (12.77% of the whole corpus) at 3.25★ to the listing; a black-screen build shipped and was never fixed for 1,030 days.

title: New Year peak-season robustness — year-end report and January onboarding
statement: The year-end report crashed five New Years in six; never ship risk or lock features in late December. The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). Report 31: v1.19.0 shipped a crash on launch on 22 Dec 2021, into the New Year and a TikTok-driven install surge — 1,135 reviews in 25 days (21.89% of the corpus, 79.4% 1★, 51% non-US), 35% of lifetime 1★; 47 reviewers never got to use the app; collateral data loss ('Lost more than 2 years of data'); the 2022 mean of 1.74 is a release-engineering outcome — stage rollouts and freeze releases before acquisition or seasonal peaks. Report 58: the history view shows only 2026 and a reviewer worries 'I hope all of my 2026 is not removed' — the corpus ends 118 days before the app's first year boundary while 5 reviewers adopted it for unrestricted history; fix 1: verify and publicise year-rollover behaviour before 1 Jan 2027.

merged_from.title: Harden onboarding before January
merged_from.note: C146 (harden onboarding before January) is the same rule as C032 (never ship risk into late December) on a different surface

title: Restore purchase and entitlements must work immediately
statement: Charging and not delivering is the second-fastest route to 1★ (×13.9). Lifetime buyers told to subscribe, subscribers who cannot find their tier, premium members still upsold. Report 11: 3 of 3 paid reviewers lost purchased access — a lifetime non-consumable expired, a subscription re-locked after a week and reinstall did not restore, an active annual term was re-charged — and two titled their reviews 'scam' and 'Purchase fraud'. Report 12: 40% of self-identified payers reported that payment did not grant access (paywall re-appears, 'no subscription found', Restore Purchase redirecting to the privacy policy, HTTP 400 at login, re-purchase demanded on a new device) — rising to 12.6% of all 2025 reviews. Report 18: 25 entitlement failures (mean 2.44★; 9.94% of confirmed payers; every Japanese instance 1★) — lifetime buyers denied Pro, a PayPay lifetime never applied, a subscription active in iOS settings with premium unusable, and a lifetime holder whose entitlement was deleted when they cancelled an accidental annual plan. The worst case: a power cut reset a lifetime buyer to onboarding, wiped every routine, then demanded a subscription. Report 19: 5 of 105 paid and could not use the product — 'I can log in on my laptop but no apps'; iPhone login error 300 with no message while iPad worked; account access lost once cancellation was started. Report 20: legacy lifetime entitlements often did not survive a device change; restore-purchase failures (91, mean 1.59) recurred for years after the 2021 revocation, and 75.8% of them came from confirmed payers. Report 25: 'already paid, asked to pay again' — 8 reviews across a 16-month window (Mar 2025 → Jul 2026), including a lifetime purchase that restore does not recognise ('every time I enter the app it tells me to remove them or to buy the subscription to keep my habits'); emerging by rate, severe by kind, and the persistence argues against a one-off outage. Report 26: purchase lost or not delivered is the top paid-user failure (24, 0.63%; 12 of 72 explicit payers = 16.7%) by three mechanisms — the 2022 repricing withdrew a purchased unlock, restore-purchases fails or the button is dead, payment succeeded but premium never activated. Report 28: 10 of 24 identifiable payers (41.7%) report a purchase not delivered or not restorable — a $9.99 pack that never appeared with 'no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; restore failing on a new device with the same account; a purchased cosmetic that reverted; consumables cannot be restored the way non-consumables can. Report 30: 'Списаны деньги за подписку, премиум функция не открылась' — charged with premium never unlocked — 'unambiguously a bug and should be treated as a P0 incident, not a review'; both billing failures are Russian, the only market with continuous purchase attempts. Report 31: 468 reviews (9.02%, mean 1.23; 304 explicit payers) say Premium they paid for was not granted — 2023 200, 2024 200 — including 295 'lifetime' buyers who stayed on Basic (mean 1.14, 89.5% 1★): the post-purchase 'gift' / Growth-Bundle screen appears to drop the entitlement when dismissed ('by not finishing this flow and purchasing the upsell, I think it doesn't recognize I purchased it'); one clean success ('I was successful at purchasing and using a lifetime premium upgrade') suggests a code-path defect that ran at least 16 months — make the entitlement grant atomic with the purchase and show any cross-sell after. Report 33: entitlement failure is small (69, 1.75%) and mostly portability — web (Paddle) purchases not unlocking the iPhone, a lifetime tied to one e-mail and paid twice, guest → account, a new or stolen phone, 18 days without activation, 6+ weeks and 20+ e-mails to resolve, a lifetime holder asked to subscribe on the Watch — plus a Jan 2018 wave (21, 11 in Japan) fixed within two weeks; the report asks for one entitlement per person recognised on every platform, with guest and account purchases merged automatically. Report 36: entitlements don't travel — skins 'unlocking them on each device'; a payer who cannot find out whether the subscription covers one device. Report 41: premium bought on iPhone never reached the iPad (2022) and premium intermittently reverted to free with Restore Purchases failing (2025) — 'a paying customer being shown a paywall is the most damaging possible bug'. Report 46: entitlement not recognised across devices or after a trial — 4 payers ('App does not recognize it… even after refreshing the subscription with the provided link'; '明明都在pad己開通高級版，Iphone上卻不給用'; one resolved only by refund and re-purchase); the report's #3 fix is one entitlement across iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac and web with a visible subscription-status screen. Report 47: premium status reverted to free with ads reappearing (3 payers, January 2021); a 'purchase failed' loop on every open (Jul 2026); the report's fix #3 is entitlement recognition. Report 49: restore purchase fails 5 — every one a paying customer locked out of what they bought, all 1★ — 'the most severe five-review theme in the corpus'. Report 52: PAY_RESTORE 190 (0.92%, 2.61; payer lift ×3.21) — an iPhone membership not recognised on iPad, memberships lost after reinstall, and a reinstall path where restoring one's own data asks for a membership that does not restore. Report 53: PAY_RESTORE carries the highest payer lift (6.32); a lifetime buyer about to post a bait-and-switch review tapped Restore Purchase and 'the app went back to normal and no more pop ups' — so part of the 2026 legacy cluster is a restore failure the app could fix by restoring on launch (F2). Report 54: 'for a one-time-purchase product, restore-purchases is not a feature, it is the product's warranty' — 7 restore failures (every one 1★) across BR, ES, GR, TH, UA×2, US, 2021 → 2026, P3 rate 4.2% (five-fold rise), 6× more concentrated outside high-spend storefronts; F1: a visible, labelled Restore button — the single largest source of one-star reviews. Report 55: premium gone after a new phone or reinstall (PAY_RESTORE 18, 1.11, lift 10.22) because premium was tied to an e-mail account; F1: restore-purchase tied to Apple ID. Report 57: 8 restore failures, all from 2024 ('I changed phones and my Premium purchase is gone'; 'after reinstalling I get ads again'); 3 whose entitlement never applied; a July 2026 release (3.1.0) broke Premium activation and restore — 8 reviews in 5 days, six 1★, one still broken on 3.1.1, externally corroborated by the release notes. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_PURCHASE 142 (0.94%, 2.81★, 8.43× among purchasers) — 'оплачено 990руб за подписку, но работать в этой программе нельзя пока ещё 1499 руб не заплатите' (990 ₽ paid but you cannot work until you pay another 1,499 ₽); a lifetime unlock listed in the phone's subscriptions as 'for a year'; the fix: restore the lifetime unlock from any receipt, on any device, on the Mac, after a reinstall, with no annual charge in between. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'I paid for subscription monthly but still not working. Is this scam?' (BR, 1★) — two of six self-identified payers had an entitlement failure, 'the worst ratio in this report'; I2: audit the purchase-unlock path end to end, including a charged subscription that still behaves as free. Report 64 (Critique AI): paid but still gated — the paywall popup persists after purchase (age 15), restore fails ('I can't restore my purchase so basically I can't do anything now'), reinstall demands payment again, and a second device refuses login ('you have to pay for each device') — 4 of 13 payers (30.8%), 3 of 13 fully gated (23.1%) — 'converts a completed sale into a 1★ and a fraud accusation'; F4. Report 65 (Rabit): PAY_ENTITLE 9 (1.81%, mean 1.56) — 100% payers, Sep 2021 → Mar 2026: 'Fiz a assinatura do plano plus anual e o app não reconhece!'; a subscriber still capped at five habits; a buyer's to-do list locked; lifetime charged but 'O app consta como se eu não tivesse o pacote'; ads and 'upgrade to premium' prompts after paying; a new phone offered only a new plan; an account 'não existe' after reinstall; F2: audit fresh install, new device, reinstall and Android→iOS, and make Restore Purchases reachable. Report 67 (Habio): U_ACCESS_FAIL 97 (4.73%, mean 1.02) — cannot log in / email not found 52, paid but no premium or restore fails 43, purchased PDF not delivered 10; 'even i payed for subscription 350 kr but everything is locked'; §8.4: link web purchases to app accounts automatically. Report 68 (Ultiself): paid access never unlocked (BUG_PURCHASE 18) and login failures often after a web purchase (BUG_LOGIN 41). Report 69 (TheFor): 3 of 4 self-stated payers describe a failure (mean 2.75 vs 4.62 for non-payers) — 'I payed for an annual subscription but the app is still prompting me to pay. Hitting restore purchase does not help'; a reinstall that lost the purchase — 22 months apart on two storefronts, 'a persistent weakness in the receipt-validation / restore path'; F1: validate the receipt on launch, never paywall a Pro owner, show entitlement state in-app. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): an accidental sale-pop-up purchase not recognised after delete-and-reinstall — 'still asking me to purchase the thing I already accidentally purchased' — §8.1 #6 restore after reinstall, findable. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): both restore failures had paid — a tablet upgrade that did not appear on the phone (no support contact found) and 'Doesn't let you transfer purchases from one OS to another. Waste of money' (1★) — 'the most costly review type there is'. Report 76 (Way of Life): BUG_PURCHASE 54 (0.70%, mean 2.69★) runs the whole 16 years and is 9.48× over-represented among purchasers and 11.60% of 1★; 'money were taken but nothing had changed' (ru 1★); 'es gebe nichts zum wiederherstellen' (de 1★); rose after the model change (0.91% → 1.55%); ru over-indexes 3.29×. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): U:paid_broken 4 (2.33%), mean 1.00★ — the only theme where every review is one star, and 4 of 11 1★ overall: 'I paid for the pro features but still features are not unlocked. Restore purchase is also not working' (2024-11); 'Lifetime purchase doesn't work. Restore purchases doesn't work. Developer doesn't respond' (2026-01); 'Estafa — Pagué por la versión premium pero no puedo usarla en mis dos celulares' (2026-06); a recurring class over 19 months, not one build; 3 of 9 stated payers; §8.8 #1 'make purchases and restores work, everywhere, including offline'. Report 83 (Roubit): PAID_NOT_UNLOCKED 4 — 'I was stuck with only 8 even after paying' with no support reply (us 1★); 'despite paying for the ¥6,000 annual plan, none of the paid features applied… 詐欺に近い対応です' (jp 1★, refund requested); membership 'sometimes drops'; one fixed by support via Restore Subscription; SCAM_LANGUAGE is otherwise absent (2 in 500). Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_IAP 9 — subscription benefits and gems not credited after payment; §8.4 restore/credit checks and a preview of paid backgrounds. Report 86 (Today): MON_RESTORE 18 (2016-03-28 → 2021-02-12), a nine-year unresolved defect — 'I bought it last year — why does it charge again after reinstalling?' (cn 5★); 'I delete the app, now I install it again (on the same phone) and I have to buy the features again' (nl 4★); '¿Es una estafa?' (es 1★); 'I paid for the Premium twice' (2★); China carries 8 of the 18; one reviewer found Settings → Restore Purchases himself — 'the function exists and is undiscoverable'; MON_IAP_FAIL 11 incl. a March 2018 cluster where the product showed as 'no longer available' ('I am trying to give you $4.99… It keeps failing. I wrote for help and no response', 1★); §8.2 'surface restore at the paywall, not buried in Settings'.

title: Data must never be lost on update, reinstall or phone change
statement: Data loss is ×10.6 over-represented among buyers; local-only storage is the cause. Report 10: from 2025 the dominant story became app-initiated — 'it told me my pet data got corrupted' — with no automatic backup to fall back on. Report 14: data lost on update was the only theme with a perfect 1★ record and the corpus's only 'stay away' review; it recurred 5.5 years later ('backdate all my progress by memory (again)'). Report 18: data loss sat between 6% and 8% in every era after the first, five years running — the single most durable defect in a 2,048-review corpus — and hit 12.42% of confirmed payers; 'if I'd known records could all disappear I wouldn't have paid.' Report 20: update 1.41.0 (13 Mar 2025) erased habit histories globally — 126 of 161 reviews in the following seven weeks (78.3%) reported losing 2–5 years; the advertised fix did not work, a second bug wiped prior progress on the next check-off, iCloud backup was itself a paid, manual feature ('Why should a premium subscriber even have to think about whether a backup was created?'), and there was no communication. The same migration-bug class had fired in Jan 2021. Report 23: data loss 81 (1.11%, mean 2.17, 45.7% 1★), 60 of them after the 2022 sync rewrite (3.38% of post-2022 reviews, mean 2.03; 2024 peak 22) — the only theme that destroys a long-tenure customer outright ('my 3+ years record to null'; 'It's like I'm a brand new user'); an in-app backup existed and was discovered by support, not the user. Report 24: progress lost on device change with no restore (257, mean 2.693) is the most-cited reason a multi-year user stops. Report 25: data loss / reset to zero 12 (0.92%), flat ~1%; archive/delete destroys history (4) — 'archive losing history defeats the point of archiving'. Report 26: with no account or sync, a support-recommended reinstall deleted 'all the lovely growth you have achieved' along with the purchase. Report 27: the one observed churn — 'It doesnt open with the update, ive lost all my progress, guess its time for a new app' — is reliability plus data loss, not price. Report 28: 12 data/progress-loss reports (1.46%, mean 2.42) entangled with the game's intentional decay — 'on challenge mode… run out of health it resets ALL of your progress… level 278… resets you to level 1'; 'My Account is gone, I was at a high Level'; an intentional decay mechanic and an unintentional data-loss bug are indistinguishable to the user. Report 29: 9 data-loss reports (mean 2.11, the lowest-rated theme) came from the calendar bug plus a workaround users taught each other — reinstall — which wiped local-only history ('just sad I lost my data from uninstalling it'); 'the bug fix alone does not close this loop — an export or backup path does'. Report 31: data / streaks lost or reset in 94 reviews (a 109-day no-wine streak; sobriety 40 → 16 days; 200+ day streaks to 0); counts corrupted by v2.7.1/2.7.2 in 107 (58,720 — 'Do not download 2.7.2!!!'); a habit tracker's only durable asset is the user's history, which users treat as health data — gate releases on data-migration tests and stage every rollout. Report 33: v2.0 (Nov 2016) wiped history and Premium for many ('30 routines gone'); Habitify X erased 4 months of time logs; data lost 55 reviews (mean 2.25). Report 34: local-only storage lost data on reinstall, factory reset or 'for no reason' (4; 'thought this app supports iCloud sync and re-installed app … lost all data as this app needs backup file'). Report 36: 'everything you save and track is reset when the app is deleted … I do not recommend' (1★); DATALOSS 3 (mean 1.67); a new phone met the new cap ('5 habits on the old phone, 1 on the new'). Report 41: 6 data-loss reports (0.74%, mean 3.33) — 'After 215 days of tracking… everything… deleted, all history lost! No chance to restore'; 'deleted from BOTH old and new device' on migration; one recovered only by the developer by hand; a 6-month total loss filed at 5★. Report 42: data loss 6 (mean 1.33, acted on regardless of share) — 'last night it updated… All my data and tracking… is gone'; 'I had 90 days of progress on every habit, now it's all gone and became 9 days'; 'I used it for many years… After the last update progress isn't visible… looking for a replacement' — the update → restart → history-truncated pattern recurs, four of six Russian. Report 43: data loss is the most severe and accelerating defect — 12 (1.88%, mean 2.08), 0 in 2016–18 → 7 in 2022–26 (4.55%); in July 2026 two German users four days apart lost four years of locally stored history when the UI changed ('I used HabitHub for four years and after an update my locally stored data was gone'), got immediate support replies, and had already migrated — 'If I could change anything, I would sync my data to the iCloud to be sure'. Report 46: data loss 24 (1.10%, mean 2.12), doubling across halves and 8 from payers — checked squares, streaks and history silently rewritten ('marks from a couple of days or even a week ago disappear'; 'the results for habit one are somehow already displayed for habit three'; 'suddenly reset and lost all my data. What am I paying $29.99/year for'); all four 2026 cases from the Russian storefront in 23 days — 'for an app whose entire value is an unbroken visual record, silently rewritten history is the highest-severity failure possible'; the fix asked for is a per-habit change history with 'undo last 7 days' and conflict resolution that never deletes a completed mark. Report 47: data loss 16 (2.72%, mean 1.94), all Japanese, 8 of them in 3–20 August 2026 after an update — '7年間使った結果がこれ… アプリ更新したら勝手にデータ上書きされて今までの記録消えた' (seven years overwritten); '2022年から毎日つけていたトピックが消えていました'; '登録していたメアドに復旧のための確認メールは来ない' (no recovery mail); one user stopped writing memos because losing them hurts too much; the data-integrity union rose from 1.1% of reviews (2019–21) to 13.0% (2025–26) while crashes fell 13.8% → 4.8% — 'more stable to open and less trustworthy to rely on'; the report's fix #1: run it as an incident, restore server-side, guard sync against overwrite, ship a visible restore path. Report 48: data loss 58 (1.32%, 1.67), 25 in the 2015 sync rewrite; 36 of the 484 one-stars; Australia over-indexes (3.23%). Report 49: progress reset or lost 36 (14.15% of payers vs 2.92%) — an update or logout restarts a 66-day programme at day 1: 46 of 66 days lost, a 177-day streak lost, six accounts lost within 48 hours in June 2025 (window mean 1.92) — 'destroys the exact asset the product is selling'. Report 50: 'the app just pushed an update and erased all my data without any warning or options to save' (1★, May 2026); a Premium user's to-do entries lost and unrecoverable (Apr 2026) — no reviewer in 205 mentions a backup; fix F6: visible backup / restore and no destructive migrations. Report 52: DATA_LOSS 229 (1.11%, 2.73; 37.1% 1★) persistent every year; 56 tie loss to an update or crash — 'four years of to-do records all gone… I bought lifetime membership for this'; payers with data loss average 1.73. Report 55: 'now I lost my account including years worth of data' (BUG_DATA 35, mean 1.31); 'I'm a premium user and have already lost all my data twice' (br); reinstalling to escape a crash often wiped data. Report 56: a sync update deleted a user's habits (4★, the only severe defect) — the history is the asset outcome reviewers keep the app for. Report 57: 12 data-loss reports (8 since 2024, 6 at 1★) — 'today's update wiped all my previous data. If recovery is impossible, shouldn't you warn people before the update?'; 'I adjusted the count on one habit, saved, and every other habit's check-ins collapsed to one'. Report 59 (Tappsk): U_DATA_RISK 104 (0.69%) — 'но все мои задачи пропали' (all my tasks disappeared); 'Нигде не указано, что задачу надо обязательно сохранить' (nowhere does it say a task must be saved) — an unsaved-edit loss reads as data loss. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'After several months of usage all my habits disappeared upon app launch' (UA, 1★); a repeating last-week wipe on update (KZ) — two reviews (4.44%) promoted under the severe-data-loss rule. Report 65 (Rabit): 'it continuously wipes all my habits, tasks, everything and I have to start over. I have the paid version!'; 50 list items saved one by one and 'simplesmente sumiu tudo!'; 'não restaura o que tinha antes' (DATA_LOSS 10, mean 1.70; data_continuity 21, 4.22%). Report 69 (TheFor): 'Eu comprei o app. Desinstalei e na hora que fui instalar novamente, sumiu tudo o q estava lá e pediu novamente para comprar' — data and entitlement lost on reinstall (2★); F2: never lose local data on reinstall. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'my five minutes of effort couldn't be recorded and went to waste' (1★) — a lost check-in is lost data in a streak product. Report 71 (MyStreaks): the streak record is the asset users protect — 'I depend on it to keep track of my Streaks…that record is extremely important to me!'; streaks of 823 and 900+ days; zero data-loss, crash or login complaints in six years (thin but genuine). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'Всё сбросилось в бесплатной версии спустя месяц. Подскажите, так и должно быть?' — a month of free-tier tracking gone and the user cannot tell bug from policy; §8.2 #10 'Either answer is a product decision; silence is the only wrong one'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): three data-loss reports inside 48 hours after an October 2022 update, never recurring — yet in January 2024 a buyer withheld a star purely because of them: 'Old data-loss reviews keep costing stars long after the bug is gone'. Report 76 (Way of Life): local-only storage with manual backup — U_DATA_RISK 123 (1.58%, mean 3.04★): BUG_DATA_LOSS 38, NEG_BACKUP_MANUAL 13, BUG_BACKUP 10; long histories gone on update or phone change ('using Way of Life daily for over four years… I downloaded an update and all of my data disappeared', 2★; 'for the third time, I've lost my data because I forgot to backup my data', 3★; 'I lost all my habits when I got a new phone even though I paid for the app', 5★); a 2017-07 release wiped some histories; 12 of 181 1★ are data loss. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): DEF_DATA_LOSS 3 (1.74%, mean 2.00★), all in the last seven months — 'All data gone after updating to ios 18.4' (1★; later recovered by iCloud sync), 'Han borrado los datos previos de antes del cambio de nombre' (1★, attributing the loss to the rename), 'My old boards got taken down in an update… Is there anyway I can get them back? I had a nice streak going' (4★, matching a v2.6.2 stability fix for year-old builds); 'for a habit tracker, whose entire value is an unbroken record, this is the most damaging defect class'; an archive/restore feature shipped in v2.3.0 and nothing suggests users know it exists. Report 83 (Roubit): the diary holds years of personal writing and was unreachable for weeks in two waves — DATA_LOSS 11 (2.20%, 2.91★): 'this app holds two years of my memories' (5★); 'I'd at least like to see the diary I wrote for a year, but I can't'; 'after updating, all my diary entries disappeared' (1★); 'It lost all my fragments. I had dozens.'; §8.1 treat the diary as irreplaceable data — release gate, fallback read-only view, export. Report 84 (HabitGrid): no actual data loss in 86 reviews; one warning it could happen on a phone change (4★) and one request for an optional account for backup — for a local-only app the fear itself costs a star. Report 86 (Today): U:dataloss_any 55 (3.08%, 2.67★): BUG_DATALOSS 33, BUG_BACKUP 28, BUG_ICLOUD 17 ('iCloud was clearly on but there was no automatic backup — all the data is gone', cn 1★), BUG_SAVE 12; 'these people have lost ALL my information on 2 occasions' (pe 1★); §8.4 restore must never destroy the backup it is reading, a failed restore must leave existing data intact, covers must survive a restore; REQ_ACCOUNT 3 want a login so history is not hostage to one device — but on-device data is praised, so 'optional account-based sync, not mandatory'.

title: Account system from day one
statement: Root cause of lost purchases, lost data and failed sync; requests rise as users change phones. Report 20: 'no account, no signup' was praised — and was the root cause of the 2025 data loss; the account/backup layer must exist even if signup stays optional. Report 26: no account system anywhere in the corpus — a device change, a reinstall, or support's own advice to reinstall destroys both progress and entitlement ('It also deletes the purchase price of the app if you bought it as there is no account to sign into'); absent accounts every other entitlement bug is unrecoverable — the root cause behind the top paid-user complaint. Report 27 (counter-evidence on the signup side, not the durability side): no account is praised — but iCloud sync exists and is invisible, so three reviewers fear data loss and one churned after an update lost progress; the account layer's job here is legible backup, not signup. Report 28: an account with e-mail verification exists (29 mentions, mean 3.66, mixed); a verification reset by support turned a 1★ into a 5★. Report 29 (counter-evidence): no account, no email, no login is named as the reason to choose the app; the report's rule is backup yes, account no — local-first. Report 33: guest mode is a data trap — 26 users who never created an account lost everything on update, reinstall or Mac sign-in ('Never use guest mode'; a ¥6,000 lifetime bought as a guest) — while forced login since 2016 is itself a privacy complaint. Report 36: no account at all; Chinese-market users ask for login specifically ('希望可以登陆', 17 helpful votes, third most-voted). Report 41 (counter-evidence): no account is praised (privacy / no account 10, all 5★: 'Pas de compte à créer, pas de données collectées'), and the report lists 'do not require an account' among what not to change. Report 43 (counter-evidence): no account required is listed among reasons to buy ('No subscription · Very reasonable one-time purchase price · Great data privacy (no data collected) · No ads'). Report 46: an account was required 2018–2022 (8 complaints, mean 1.50; the first review in the corpus could not sign up; login failures mean 1.89) and optional by 2024 — the complaint stopped when the requirement did. Report 48 (counter-evidence on mandatory accounts): forcing an account and online sync on a local tracker in Jan 2015 drew 39 reviews at mean 1.64 — 'a privacy objection, distinct from price' — strongest in Germany (5.04%, the largest over-index of any theme in any storefront; one review invokes German consumer law); iCloud sync later replaced the account; login / account failures 21 (1.86). Report 50 (counter-evidence): a mandatory account limited to Sign in with Apple or Google before first use lost two GB users at the gate — 'Why would I want to expose every aspect of my life to data mining in this way? Stay clear.' and 'unable to login with apple' — 'a conversion risk and a single point of failure'; S6: consider a local-first trial mode. Report 52: WeChat login cannot be bound on the Mac build for five years (12 reviews, among the most-upvoted) and QQ vs WeChat logins split Android and iOS memberships. Report 55: an optional account (e-mail, Facebook; later Apple, Google) whose January 2018 registration spinner, 'email invalid' and reset e-mails that never arrive (ACCT_BUG 57, 1.68; US 34 of 57) broke premium; F6: registration optional and robust, never block first use. Report 58: no account and no e-mail sign-up named as adoption reasons by 2 ('It makes it quick and easy to start using'). Report 76 (Way of Life): a counter-example — no account, no sync, local-only for 16 years at 4.62★; the cost shows as data loss on phone change (U_DATA_RISK 123, 1.58%) and REQ_SYNC 139 in every era, not as a sign-up complaint; PR_PRIVACY 12 praise the absence. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the account system is the product's one reliability defect class — DEF_LOGIN 14 (8.00%), no crash reports at all; a paid web account must be linked to the app login by the purchase email with creation and recovery paths on the sign-in screen. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the no-account counter-case — 'No sign-in. No servers. No cloud.' is a headed section of the listing, praised for privacy, and the cost is one 4★ who believes data dies with the phone and one request for an optional account; the website mentions opt-in authentication and cloud backups that appear nowhere else.

title: A support channel that exists, is reachable outside the app, and answers
statement: 'No support channel' is ×34.7 over-represented among buyers and the second-worst-rated complaint. Report 5: the only support link was inside an app that would not launch; email went unanswered while public review replies were same-day. Report 10: AI and canned support replies; paying users 13× over-represented among support complaints. Report 11: 'there is no way in app to talk with developer or team' — with no support queue, billing bugs were filed as public 1★ fraud accusations instead. Report 12: five reviewers said the listed support email does not exist; refund and support failures were twice as prevalent in small storefronts, where users are charged and stranded. Report 18: support silence (32, mean 2.72★) landed hardest on payers — a week of silence on a lifetime account with purchase screenshots; the Japanese in-app feedback form rejected every valid e-mail and its text was invisible in dark mode, so Japanese users could only file bugs through the App Store; KakaoTalk was the only Korean channel and closed at weekends; a Canadian found the in-app support link resolved to an ad. Report 20: support went from answering reviews and fixing bugs same-day in 2019–2020 to a dead 'Contact Us' e-mail with an autoresponder and a dormant Instagram account (0.05% → 13.0% of reviews by era); among 148 support-silence reviews the mean was 1.33 versus 3.63 for the 30 who were restored or fixed — the same defect produced either rating depending only on whether anyone answered, worth ~+2.3 stars per recoverable incident. Report 23: support praised (49, 0.67%) with fixes bringing edited upgrades, but genuine silences recur and one reviewer says support implied they don't own an Apple Watch for testing. Report 24: 947 (2.18%, mean 1.528) automated-only support; the refund path works when reached — several 1★ → 4★ edits after a refund — so the failure is reaching it. Report 25: a solo developer answering within a day ('feature requests implemented in less than 24hrs'; 'I can't believe one developer made this') is a purchase trigger — 'After testing the app and interacting with the developer… I've decided to pay without any hesitation' — but support praise thinned 3.0% → 1.6% → 0.9% and one 1★ says the developer 'preferred to argue about what I could see on my end'. Report 26: support unreachable 13 (mean 2.77), support praised 10 (all 5★); support's own advice to reinstall destroyed a paying user's progress and purchase; a premium subscriber's crash went unanswered for months. Report 27: not one review in four years mentions contacting support or a developer reply; the website link in Settings leads to an inactive domain, so the support path is broken — and a solo-developer app with no support channel absorbs an OS-transition break entirely through its public rating. Report 28: 'There is no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; 'no matter how many emails you send, they don't reply'; yet the four who reached the developer got excellent service — a 1★ converted to 5★ after a verification reset 'within an hour… on a Sunday, on a 3 day holiday weekend'; support quality is not the problem, discoverability is — an in-app 'Contact support' and 'Restore purchases' entry point is the cheapest rating intervention available. Report 29: support effectively unreachable — 'I contacted the dev twice but got no response'; a support link that 'takes you to a super-sketch website, circumventing Apple's privacy settings'; with no account and no backup the review page is the only support channel, which is why bugs arrive as public 1★. Report 31: 460 reviews (8.87%, mean 1.32) say support never replied or the contact path was broken (dead typeform links, a Mail-app-only link), rising 0.6% (E1) → 20.3% (E4) → 20.8% (E5); in E1 support was praised (11 of 18 support-praise reviews) — staff a single working contact path with a published response time and resolve by receipt, not by argument.
