Report 33: support is two-sided — praised 103 (mean 4.73; 'Hana … sent me a video'; 'within one minute') vs support failure 131 (1.70; 5 weeks without reply then the review deleted); English-only replies frustrate Japanese and Chinese users; AI-only support is an emerging negative (8 reviews, 7 in 2025–26: 'Their support is AI'; the chatbot 'stops answering'). Report 34: a single 'Support doesn't respond to emails' in an app whose main asset is a named, responsive solo developer. Report 36: both support-failure records are payers ('contacted the developer twice … I waited too long for a reply and I have now paid. Service matters'; 'a small company and cannot solve problems in mainland China'). Report 41: the only support channel is a mailto: link that dead-ends users without the Mail app ('forcing me to add a mail account'; a trial user 'likely will cancel'), in an app where support closes sales and is the only data-recovery path; support praise collapsed to 1.7% in 2025 as volume tripled, then recovered. Report 42: a paying customer with data loss had no route to a human — 'it says mail isn't connected, but there's no section in the app to connect it' — and replies are canned ('they just reply the same thing to everyone', a 10-vote review). Report 43: support is bimodal because the intake is broken — praised by 24 (mean 4.67; a 2★ raised to 5★ after the exact fix shipped; 'requested a small new feature… added a few days later') vs 7 with no response (mean 1.29, the lowest theme) and 4 reporting the in-app feedback form itself fails ('Feedback email can not send'; 'They have a report bug feature, but that also doesn't work'); 'no response' rose 0.57% → 2.60% by era while praise stayed flat. Report 46: 7 unanswered (mean 1.57; 'sent 3 different email… Not a single reply'), four of them 2024–26 and two paying customers with unresolved data loss or an unrecognised subscription; support praise 53 (4.94) is falling 4.30% → 1.82% as volume grew. Report 47: no findable support route — unresponsive 7 (mean 2.57): '問い合わせ先もわからない'; 'サポートサイトにも窓口がない'; a feedback form that crashes; account-deletion messages unanswered — while 12 reviews (mean 4.42) acknowledge a fix: the gap is the channel, not responsiveness. Report 48: support is reachable only inside the app, so users whose app will not open have no route — 14 reviews (1.08% of 2022–26 and growing) are 1★ reviews written as support tickets, nine from payers; the report's fix #3: publish a support e-mail on the website and the listing; separately 29 got no response (1.55). Report 49: 'contact support' is not a button (3), App Support resolves to a 404, multi-day silence — 21 unreachable (1.43), 10 of them payers; when support does answer it is outstanding (9 at 4.89 — a refund plus a free year) — 'The capability exists; the routing and the staffing do not.' Report 50: in-app support chat praised by 8 (5.00) and developer responsiveness by 11 (4.91) — 17 unique; one negative ('sometimes customer service give is not very caring'); support re-sent a lost discount offer and closed the sale — 'an asset to protect… not a cost centre to optimise'. Report 52: support silence rises with each crash wave (SUP_BAD 184, 2.33; payers ×4.53 at 1.92) across e-mail, WeChat, Weibo and Xiaohongshu; a support address that bounces; fast fixes are among the strongest praise (SUP_GOOD 148 at 4.93: a purchase crash fixed the next day, a request shipped within days). Report 53: support went from praised to silent — SUP_GOOD 31 (4.71) all Nov 2017 → Mar 2022 (a proactive follow-up, an icon idea shipped in days, VoiceOver added on request) and SUP_BAD 64 (1.58), 41 in 2023–26; the in-app contact needed a configured Mail account and later 'the support email it opens does not send'; payers with silent support average 1.17; F4: a contact that works without Mail, an auto-acknowledgement and a known-issues note. Report 54: support unresponsive 6 (1.50), rising to 4.2% of 2023–26; 'Your support pages and email are down' (GR, Aug 2026); 'there's no app support to write any of this to… which I feel like should be a thing if you have to pay for an app'. Report 55: support silence from Jan 2016 to Apr 2026 (SUP_BAD 83, 1.45, 66 at 1★; payer lift 6.21) — a developer site returning errors, a contact form that won't send, ticket numbers with no reply, canned answers; 'will update my review based upon their response'. Report 56: four in-review support questions (data recovery, widget transparency in Korean, language reset, back-dating) left unanswered, each answerable in one sentence. Report 57: Korean users write support tickets in the review box — 50 direct questions to the developer (49 Korean, 8.10% vs 0.57%), mostly 5★ about existing features; support praised 2019–24 for fast KakaoTalk replies ('got a reply the moment 9am hit') then silent ('they just read it and never replied. What a waste of money'); 'the support link goes to some Asian industrial company'; the in-app bug-report form crashes on Submit; F6: a support link and FAQ where users are already asking. Report 59 (Tappsk): reviewers praise Telegram and condemn e-mail — 'пишу на почту уже 2 раза, ответа нет' (e-mailed twice, no reply); 'На почту пишешь не отвечают, в тг пишешь бот' (e-mail unanswered; on Telegram you get a bot); SUP_NONE 64 (6.09× among purchasers), SUP_CONTACT 31, both more frequent in the latest eras; fix: route billing and sync tickets to the channel that answers and acknowledge bug reports with a status. Report 60 (Mindway): seven reviewers (3.24%, mean 1.43) used a 1★ public review as a help desk — 'the absence of a visible support path', six of the seven about money; the one who tried the proper route ('asked this question of the developer and awaiting the reply') rated 3★ where the other six went straight to 1★ — 'the one payer who found a support route rated the app two stars higher than the ones who didn't'; F3: put an in-app support route in front of the review prompt, and answer it — seven support tickets became permanent public 1★ reviews. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): no reviewer — including three paying customers with a broken app — reports contacting the developer; the reviews are the support channel by default. Report 64 (Critique AI): three 1★ reviews are unanswered, resolvable tickets — a parent's three emails on a login issue got one 'please clarify' then silence ('My son was so excited to use this app, but now it's just taking up space'); billing; a frozen paid app — F5: 'low rate, 100% conversion to 1★'. Report 65 (Rabit): SUP_SILENT 5 — every one 1★ and every one a payer ('Mandei dois e-mails solicitando o estorno da compra, mas até o momento não deram retorno'; 'ninguém responde… Um descaso total!') — each a problem one reply would have converted; F3: 'the cheapest rating repair available'. Report 67 (Habio): U_SUPPORT_FAIL 425 (20.72%, mean 1.04) — no reply 213, slow 78, templated 59, evasive 46; 'Funny how when it's public your response is timely'; retention questions in reply to cancellation requests; 37.7% of reviewers whose money left their account report a support failure. Report 68 (Ultiself): SUP_NONE 352 (7.80%; 20.8% of the Dec 2024 → Mar 2025 era); replies that seem automated ('the bot responds with nonsense'); in 2026 fast named replies with refunds lifted PR_SUPPORT to 5.0% of reviews — refunds reported in 1★ reviews stayed 1★. Report 69 (TheFor): the developer answers but cannot be found — 'Unable to contact developer on their website'; 'Let me know if I can email the suggestions'; a 1★ 'Phishing spam scam' demanding cancellation in public — 'a support-surface problem, not a support-quality problem'; F7: an email link in settings and a Manage-subscription row deep-linking to Apple. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 5 reviewers used the public review as a support ticket (mean 3.00) though the developer answers email fast — E4: an in-app 'suggest a feature' route. Report 76 (Way of Life): support silence arrives from 2016 and peaks in the subscription era (SUP_NONE 20 at mean 2.05★, 9 of them in E6) alongside restore failures; the website contact section did not work ('secção de Contact no website não funciona', pt 1★); 'received no response at all' (1★); §8.3 a working in-app contact form and an auto-reply with restore steps; reviewers excuse a solo developer ('I think they are just one person, so be patient') until money is involved. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): zero customer-support-failure mentions in 71 reviews; the schema has no developer-reply field. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the single support-silence report is the worst case — a lifetime buyer whose restore failed: 'Developer doesn't respond. Waste of time' (1★); §8.1.1 a visible support path from the entitlement-failure screen. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the App Store listing prints a support address at a domain that does not exist — hello@lastingchange.app returns NXDOMAIN with no MX record, while the same page links the working domain thelastingchange.com; a reviewer hit it ('I tried to email hello@ and was told this was invalid'); email is the only cancellation route, so a dead address is a structural failure; the one satisfied payer used the working help@ address and was confirmed within a quarter of an hour; SUP_UNFINDABLE 5, SUP_CANNED 8 ('Your feedback has been taken into consideration…'), SUP_RESPONSE_FACADE 4. Report 83 (Roubit): the in-app support form sits inside the Settings tab that blanked in two bug waves, so the corpus became the support desk (SUPPORT_QUESTION 43, 8.60%; 31 of 33 rating/text contradictions are high-star bug reports); support_negative 15 (3.00%, 2.53★): unanswered email ('I emailed the person in charge twice with no reply'), unread KakaoTalk, a promised same-day fix then three days of silence, 'it's starting to feel like the app is being neglected'; where support worked it raised ratings ('The support helped me fix the ad issue by using the Restore Subscription button' → 5★; 'sorted within 24 hours'). Report 86 (Today): SUP_ASK 54 (3.03%) ask the developer a question in a review — 'a signal that the in-app support path is not obvious'; the embedded support address is misspelled (toda@neybox.com) and the corrected one got no reply; §8.11 'the cheapest fix in this report'.

title: Family plan
statement: Demand exists (people bought it); report 1's failed only through discoverability (Apple Family Sharing with no in-app affordance). Report 23: Family Sharing is supported on the one-time purchase; a few want to track a child's chores alongside their own inside one account. Report 33: a paid family plan (2025) whose sharing is described as not working (7, mean 2.00). Report 46: no Family Sharing — 'for that, €29 a year is too expensive' (DE, 1★); 'too expensive to have 5 subscriptions so my entire family could use the tool'; the report: offer it on annual and lifetime. Report 53: the listing claimed Family Sharing that the in-app purchases did not support (PAY_FAMILY 8; refund requests in kr). Report 57: Family Sharing advertised on the listing and not working for a buyer ('I do not think it is right that they lie', MX). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_FAMILY_SHARE 13; 'написано, что поддерживается семейный доступ' (it says Family Sharing is supported) is a paid-twice complaint. Report 76 (Way of Life): MON_FAMILY_SHARING 3 (family sharing / gifting, 2015 → 2025). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): a $17.99 'Powerpack Family' SKU and Family Sharing support — no review mentions Family Sharing at all.

title: Dates, streaks and statistics correct on every surface — month boundaries, week starts, DST and timezones
statement: Miscounts are ×10.2 over-represented among buyers. Off-by-one dates across app/widget/Watch were report 2's longest-lived bug. Night routines that cross midnight must log to the day they started, honouring a user 'day ends at' setting. Report 23: un-pausing a task marks paused days as missed and resets the streak; a completion 'un-completes' seconds later under sync conflict. Report 25: over-achievement carries into the next day (exceeding a goal pre-completes tomorrow) and logging a bad habit at 200% is rewarded as success (7, 0.53%). Report 29: a month-rollover and weekday-header-offset bug was the dominant defect — 37 reviews (10.11%, mean 2.95 vs 4.73), 78.4% filed on days 28–3 against a 27.6% baseline ('On the last day of every month the app has no idea what day it is… April 30 defaulted to Feb 28'); 62.5% of all 3★; users taught each other to reinstall, which wiped local-only data. Test every date surface at month end, leap day and both week starts. Report 31: time-zone travel rewrote 600- and 1,500-day streaks (13); the week-start setting was ignored and weeks reset on Sunday, including in widgets (30; a 3-year premium user 'begging'); store completions against the local calendar day, not a UTC timestamp. Report 47: calendar weekdays off by one day for reviewers outside the Japan / Korea time zone — 14 (2.38%), 13 from China, Italy, France, Spain and Australia, 2019 → April 2021 ('4 January 2021 is a Monday and it says Tuesday'; 'it lost 29 February'); habit order scrambling (5, 2022), counts displayed wrong (5, 2025–26), late-night check-ins leaving a gap (fixed); a Sunday week start added on request. Report 48: timezone / date bugs 26 (3.35, 2014–22); wrong counts / stats 85 (2.59) across every era; day-boundary 2. Report 49: the day counter advances wrongly — 20 reviews, flat Oct 2024 – Jun 2026, never fixed; the daily recap closes scoring at a fixed ~9pm (10). Report 54: the paid calendar rings show the wrong completion — two reviewers on two continents tie it to the long-press undo not propagating to the calendar (9, 2.56, 5 payers). Report 55: 'not more than' goals saved as 'at least' — inverting success for quit-smoking and drinking goals ('Smoke not more than 10 cigarettes… they actually show as requiring you to do the task at least that many times'); streaks reset at the year change in 2018 and 2020; editing a frequency rewrites history; a traveller's completions shift days; a July 2020 update marked taps on the wrong day. Report 56: 'the calendar is a day out so when you complete a dot on the Monday it highlights the Sunday before' (GB, rated 5★) — F2: verify week-start and timezone handling (Europe/London vs UTC feed); the UI switched to Chinese unprompted. Report 57: 'Display on' per-weekday filter shipped and silently ignores selections for 8 users over five years ('I set Tue/Thu/Sat and it shows every day'). Report 65 (Rabit): completed habits reported as missed — 'Tengo un hábito cumplido todos los días y mi planta sale muerta y con 0 días de racha' (BUG_STREAK 7, mean 2.43); week start offered only as Friday or Saturday, never Monday (3); a calendar mapping dates to the wrong weekday; F7, F9. Report 69 (TheFor): 'Even though I completed around 75% of my test, only 20%. Why?' (3★, 2026 — the only open bug that year); F4: verify the completion percentage before deepening analytics — 'Deepening a view that computes the wrong number is the wrong order'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): no date is shown on the ring — 'because no dates are shown, from about day 3 I lost track of whether I'd recorded or not, got confused and uninstalled'; 'unrecorded' flags on unscheduled weekdays; §8.1: show the date being recorded on the ring. Report 75 (Habit Streak): 'Have a 6 day streak and it says day 4. Best streak says 5, current streak says 4… it just frustrates you instead of encourages you' (2★) — three mutually inconsistent numbers on the one metric the product exists to show, the highest-severity open defect; with the no-backfill 0% case: 'the app's record of what the user did disagrees with the user's own record, and the app wins'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): DEF_DATE_LOGIC 2, the only defect reported twice — a tick on Saturday or Sunday 'fills in/unfills both days'; a widget increment lands on the following day; both week/day-boundary errors; 1.0.19 'Custom week start' touches week boundaries and whether it fixes either is not established; §8.2 test completion writes across the week boundary, across time zones, and from widgets. Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_RESET 93 (2.70%) — 'the app will tell me it started a new day, but it hasn't cleared out my dailies' (3★); NEG_DAYSTART 16; in the latest era day-rollover failures rank fourth among defects; §8.1 make 'start new day' (cron) idempotent and visible and never let a failed rollover block ticking tasks. Report 86 (Today): a time-zone check-in bug first reported Feb 2019 was fixed Oct 2025 — six and a half years later; a day-start-time setting was in a 2016 twenty-item request list.

merged_from.title: Date arithmetic must survive month boundaries and week-start conventions
merged_from.note: C243 (report 29: a month-rollover / weekday-offset bug) is a specific failure of C038's rule, not a separate decision

title: Reminders fire reliably, once
statement: Reminders that work are a top praise item; not firing or spamming is a 1★ driver. Report 23: 97 (1.33%, mean 3.48, 18.6% 1★) — reminders that don't fire (Thailand 4 of 22, 18.2%, limited evidence), fire for already-completed tasks, fire all at once at night, ignore Do Not Disturb, or interrupt a meditation to say meditate; the 'smart' auto-timing algorithm is widely disliked. Report 24: notification volume/control 744 (1.71%, mean 2.437) — users turn all notifications off, which disables the product; give per-notification-type control. Report 27: the reminder fires for a goal already marked complete today — 'a notification that contradicts app state actively trains users to ignore notifications'. Report 28: notification annoyance 5 (0.61%, mean 2.80) — decay-guilt pushes ('YOUR BUNNY'S LOSING HEALTH'). Report 29: reminders that never fire, deleted reminders that keep firing (surviving delete-and-reinstall), and changed times that don't take (6, mean 3.17) — one problem: the notification schedule is written once and never reconciled against the habit's state; cancel scheduled notifications on delete and stop the day's reminders on check-off. Report 30: a user wants an alarm, not just a notification — 'receives an alarm from the app itself and doesn't need another alarm on the phone'. Report 33: reminders praised by 91 (repeat every 30 min until done) and broken in 68, notably when iOS 13 broke notifications. Report 34: the reminder time picker broke for a paying user ('I payed for this app … I might just cancel my membership', Dec 2025) and again Mar 2026; a 2019 buyer got no notifications and returned the purchase. Report 43: an iOS 15 notification regression ran five public weeks (13 Oct – 10 Nov 2021: firing after completion, double notifications, 'I don't think the solution is to have us individually email tech support. It's clearly a bug'; a payer 'over a month and a half… no bug fix'); ghost habits — deleted habits still firing at midnight after reinstall and a new phone (2); notification bugs 15 (2.35%, mean 2.60) on the app's signature feature. Report 46: a deleted habit's notification kept firing (the most-voted review in the corpus, 25 votes); reminders not firing 7; finer reminder control (per day, stop once done) requested by 9. Report 47: reminder time-setting buggy Jan–Feb 2021; non-scheduled weekdays notified until fixed by June 2026 — notification bugs 11 (1.87%). Report 48: notification bugs 78 (1.77%, 2.64) at a stable ratio against 224 reminder praise; notification overload 12 (2.33). Report 52: reminders were why people installed (and in 2017 what they reviewed to unlock), so REM_FAIL carries a 3.62× payer lift — silent mode kills the sound, reminders keep firing after the habit is done (23 votes), archived habits still remind, changed sounds revert. Report 53: in an app named HabitMinder reminders are tied to a time-of-day section, not a clock time — an evening habit reminds at 8 am ('the only reminder that can be set is for 8am'), a 30-reminder list hits iOS's scheduled-notification cap so some habits are never reminded, and reminders fire for habits already done (REM_CONTROL 56, 2.88; REM_ANNOY 28; REM_FAIL 13). Report 54: notification defects — no badge, nagging after completion, wrong sound (6, 2.50). Report 55: medication reminders that fail; push instead of sound-only in silent mode. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_REMINDER 96 (0.63%, 2.78★) in every era — 'unless you open the app every other day, the reminders you set will stop working'; 'за весь день дай бог словить хотя бы 2 уведомления' (lucky to catch two notifications a day); PR_REMINDERS 401 shows the same feature is a top praise when it works. Report 65 (Rabit): the ledger's clearest reminder regression — REM_FAIL 66 (13.25%, mean 2.91), 10.8% of launch-era reviews, 0.8% for the next 25 months, then 45.7% of everything written from Nov 2023 to Sep 2026 and still open at the last review; 14 reviewers (2.81%) report the app is absent from iOS Settings → Notifications altogether, across iPhone and iPad, seven storefronts and five languages, after reinstalls — 'almost certainly a missing or failing UNUserNotificationCenter authorization request'; 'Qual o sentido de fazer um app de habitos e nao ter notificação?'; 15 of 66 are 4★ and 9 are 5★; REM_GOOD (a perfect 5.00) fell 8.1% → 0.8%; the loop a reviewer described — cue (notification), routine, reward (the tree) — loses its first step; three abandoned lifetime / subscription purchases, 10 of 49 payers, three refunds; F1: confirm the authorization request on a current device before anything else. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): missing, duplicated and phantom reminders across 2017 → 2026 (BUG_NOTIF 38) against 203 reviews crediting the reminder (PR_NOTIF, 4.84) — 'The second notification arrived at a moment as if it had seen through my laziness'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'приходят не все уведомления о привычках' (3★ — the only rating reduction from a plain defect); a 5★ titled 'Notification bug' resolved individually by support — handled per-user rather than systemically (§8.2 #11). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): multiple reminders — asked by three reviewers in 2024 — shipped in v2.2.0 (2026-03-01) and generated two reliability complaints five and six weeks later (DEF_NOTIF_FAIL 2, 3.50★: 'maybe is a bug I would like a anwser') — a newly shipped requested feature created its own defect class. Report 86 (Today): BUG_NOTIF 63 (3.53%, 2.57★), 2016-04-04 → 2025-02-10 — ten years never fully fixed ('notifications are straight up not working for habits. I have 3 set up and they never go off'; 'out of ten habits it notifies one or two, and for days no notification is delivered', br); 10 of 63 say it makes the app unusable; a specific reproducible behaviour reported independently in 2017 and 2021 — 'if I don't check in every single day, the reminders stop all together'; 'surely this is the most important time to have a reminder?' — §8.3 'a habit app that goes quiet precisely when the user lapses has inverted its own purpose'.

title: Widgets must not go blank, stale or disagree with the app
statement: Broken widget is ×7.8 on 2★. Report 10: the widget rendered as a grey box for five years (117 reviews) — reported mostly by fans, so it never generated pressure. Report 18: the widget went from the top request (31 reviews at 4.77★ before launch) to the top defect surface (214 mentions, 10.45%) — blank, missing from the picker, wrong weekday, false 'all done', check-off opening the app, routine widget rendering to-dos. Report 20: the widget was the top defect surface for five years and the 2★ band's peak theme (13.0%). Report 23: widgets rendering blank or losing configuration (57 explicit widget-bug reviews, mean 3.16; 20 blank/config reports) alongside the interactive-widget regression. Report 25: widget stopped working / not interactive / font fixed (6, 0.46%). Report 27: the widget is the most consistently under-delivering surface and the only one to produce a 1★ on its own ('Widget does and shows absolutely nothing… Just says 0% ALL the time'); 9 gap/defect reviews (6.52%, high-priority) across every one of five years vs 5 praising it. Report 28: no widget at all — 14 requests (1.71%), mean 4.64, zero negative ratings, continuous April 2022 → September 2026, 'i want to be able to click on the widget and shortcut to check a habit as done'; the clearest uncontested gap in the corpus. Report 29: no widget at all — 16 requests (4.37%), the only absent feature with demonstrated substitution (a user on 'Check Me' because it has one) and the one explicit payment offer ('add widget support happy to pay for a lifetime'); three withhold a star for it. Report 30: the Home Screen widget is paywalled and a documented switch followed — 'I downloaded it only for the widget. Turned out it's a paid feature… competitors include it free — I went there'; the widget shown in the store screenshots is not the widget the app provides; the one user who has it is the happiest reviewer. Report 31: widget mentions 195 (3.76%) — positive in E1, demand in E2, complaint after the Oct 2021 downgrade; the widget ignored the week-start setting. Report 34: widget rendering broke with the iOS 18 tinted home screen (white), two of six widgets didn't show days, 'keeps getting disabled' — 5 reviews, 3.0% of E4, one payer 'waste money'. Report 46: widgets blank, stale or wrong — 21 (mean 3.33): 'I deleted the Dry January task but the widget still shows it'; 'every day the home-screen widget colour blocks get scrambled'; 'The widget is the heart of the application' (1★ after contact); interactive widgets also record accidental taps ('marks the completion of that day by mistake… Not great for a paid app') — the report: keep it, add a lock / view-only mode. Report 47: the 2025 widget gets stuck at 0 or goes blank (5, all 2025–26: 'ある日突然ウィジェットがずっと0表示になってしまいました'); the report's fix #2 pairs it with wrong month-view counts. Report 49: the same blank / stuck-on-day-1 widget reported in Mar 2025, May 2025, Nov 2025, Dec 2025 and the final week of the corpus (8). Report 50: widget lag (1, 5★). Report 52: widget defects 454 (2.20%), 62.8% in 2020–21; a widget renders blank on iOS 26 Clear / Tinted home screens. Report 53: widgets blank on tinted home screens and no longer interactive on iOS 18/26 (WIDGET_BUG 5.1% of 2025, 7.5% of 2026). Report 56: a widget tap that opens the app instead of progressing the habit (BE, 4★). Report 57: the widget is both the most-loved feature and the largest defect surface — 129 (16.56%) raise a problem: 50 won't appear or go blank (rising 3.89% → 6.67% → 10.80% by era), 25 don't reflect check-ins, 9 show a live group as 'deleted' (Apr 2024 – Dec 2025), 6 clip items; 58 of 90 defect reviews are 4–5★; 'every single update breaks the widget'; 'I have to reinstall five or six times a month'; 23 of 99 payers affected; a Premium payer considering switching over three widget layouts. Report 58: widget habit icons render as white boxes in iOS clear / tinted icon mode — the only functional defect in 91 reviews, with a stated repro. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_WIDGET 100 (0.66%) — widgets blank or stale after updates and not changing at day change ('при переключении дня задачи на виджете не меняются'; 'каждый раз обещают направить разработчикам, но проблема остается' — each time they promise to pass it on, the problem remains); fix: widgets that refresh at day change without opening the app; the 2.6.2 release notes list 'faster widgets'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): the widget is the paid hook, so its gaps are voiced by the highest-LTV buyer — no dark theme, 'so basic' — from a lifetime purchaser. Report 69 (TheFor): widget won't launch the app unless it is already backgrounded, and doesn't show already-completed tasks (BUG_WIDGET 2) — refresh / state bugs on an asset praised at 5.00. Report 83 (Roubit): BUG_WIDGET 15 (3.00%; KR 4.9%) — routine order reversed in the widget (developer promised a fix for October 2024); in July 2025 'with this update the iPhone widget seems to be unsupported' for a paying user; REQ_WIDGET 9. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 'incrementing a counter through the widget doesn't increase the count, or increases the count for the following day (possibly a time zone mismatch?)' (4★) — the most detailed bug report in the corpus, from a reviewer who calls widgets 'a huge plus'; 'can't add several widgets with different habits — it only gives one… please tell me how' (5★); widget praise stops in the final era (8 → 0). Report 85 (Habitica): widgets arrived and became a defect source — BUG_WIDGET 22 (all from 2021), 15 of them in the latest era where widget failures rank sixth among defects; REQ_WIDGET 68 (1.97%). Report 86 (Today): BUG_WIDGET 35 (1.96%) — 'the widget has a bug on iOS 10; purple blocks keep appearing' (5★); the 3D Touch widget reveals the habit list past the paid lock.

title: Editing a habit never wipes its history
statement: Multi-year bug; fixing it brought reviewers back to raise their rating. Report 25: archiving or deleting a habit destroys its history (4); preserve history through archive and restore. Report 30: the only way to stop a finished habit is to delete it, which destroys its history. Report 71 (MyStreaks): a streak's cadence (daily / weekly / monthly) cannot be changed after creation — the reviewer had to retire a 6-day streak and start over, and retired streaks cannot be viewed; 'Forcing a user to destroy the exact thing the product tells them never to break is a design contradiction' (open after 25 releases).

title: Aim at ADHD / neurodivergent users, students, medication & chronic-illness trackers
statement: Highest-fit, highest-satisfaction audiences (ADHD 7% of US at 4.79; students 4.87). Report 10: 7.36% of 70,041 reviewers self-identify as ADHD/autistic/ND; Australia's base is 11.4%. Report 18: ADHD/ASD/depression/burnout reviewers were the highest-rated audience (36 at 4.53★; 5.95% of US reviews) and the developer put 'ADHD' in the Korean store title — but the same population is most damaged by streak mechanics and excluded by a 9-to-5 onboarding; the positioning ran ahead of the product. Report 23: self-identified ADHD/autism/executive-dysfunction users are a growing, high-satisfaction segment (73, 1.00%, mean 4.45; 0.66% → 0.70% → 1.90% across eras) the app never marketed to; 28 arrived on a therapist/coach/doctor recommendation (mean 4.50); several of them are the strongest capacity complaints because task decomposition is what executive-function support requires, and one calls the help-page wording ableist. Report 24: ADHD/autism/executive-dysfunction users are 933 (2.15%) and grew 30× across eras to 6.01% of 2024–26 reviews — but they are the angriest segment (mean 2.747, 54.2% 1–2★) because the interface overstimulates and the cancel flow exploits executive function; depression/anxiety/PTSD/grief context is 1,256 (2.89%, mean 3.938); clinicians review it and recommend it (24 + 9). Report 25: ADHD/autism/OCD self-identified users are the highest-satisfaction segment (41, 3.13%, mean 4.44, 32 5★; plus 24 at mean 4.67 describing executive difficulty without a diagnosis; three arrive via a clinician including a psychologist recommending it to clients) — and they supply the sharpest paywall anger ('just another app trying to profit off of your disability'); ADHD vocabulary is 4.8× more common in high-spend markets, a diagnosis-prevalence difference not a needs difference. Report 26: ADHD/neurodivergent users (81, 2.11%, mean 3.84 — the lowest of any positively-framed segment) succeed because of simplicity and are hit hardest by the 5-habit cap; mental-health users (32, mean 4.66) are the highest-affect reviews; teens and students (25, ages 10–21, mean 4.16) cannot pay. Report 28: ADHD/autism users (15, mean 4.33) say the reward loop 'works so well for my brain' — and produce the harshest ad verdicts ('whenever I click to complete a habit, it shows me an advert'; 'Bad for ADHD — Has Potential'): interruption cost is not evenly distributed; kids and students are 40 (4.87%), several aged 8–10. Report 31: ADHD / autism / OCD users 33 (mean 4.09 — 'every other app overcomplicates… this app is BEAUTIFUL and simple'), medication and body-care tracking 36 (3.42), mental-health context 38; coaches, clinicians and therapists recommend it — they are the most loyal and the most hurt by regressions (monthly frequency, streak display, medication streaks). Report 33: ADHD, neurodivergent and health users praise the structure ('as an adult with ADHD'; 'I'm neurodivergent and I really hate routine'; medication) and object most clearly to guilt copy and unclosable banners ('I have adhd … huge banner … you CAN NOT CLOSE'). Report 34: ADHD users (5) prefer the simple general tracker — 'apps designed specifically for ADHD … too detailed … This app is simple with just the right amount of detail'; 'MUST. FILL. BOXES.' Report 43: ADHD (18, mean 4.61) and other accessibility accounts (12, 4.75; autism, depression, chronic illness, head injury, ASD, anxiety) are the fastest-growing theme (0.00% → 4.22% → 7.79% by era) and almost entirely US (24 of 25) — 'severe ADHD… complete tasks that would otherwise take hours on end — cooking, cleaning, and even applying makeup'; 'motivated me to shower for the first time in a week'; 'when I don't have the brain power to think it just tells me what to do next'; the mechanics are the multi-step timer and the widget; the listing's 'ADHD-friendly interface' claim is earned without targeting. Report 46: neurodivergent and chronically ill users (30, mean 4.83, 23 US, growing 0.54% → 1.70%) name the forgiving skip ('one off day doesn't kill your streak'; 'neutral data instead of a personal failing'), the widget ('if I don't see something I forget it exists') and minimal input ('a simple yes/no input, which is perfect for me and my ADHD because I've quickly become burnt out by decision fatigue on other apps'; 'Literally 3 click options'). Report 47: study / learning users 9 (mean 4.78; 'ピアノ練習100日目'), neuro / focus 2; fitness / diet 24 (4.08; a high-schooler's diet log with 14 votes). Report 48: ADHD is the lowest-rated segment (13, mean 3.77) in a corpus where every other segment averages 4.6+; students 24, mental health 23 (4.78), health / medical 24. Report 50: ADHD users 7 (3.41%, 4.29; 5 US at 4.80 — 'ADHD life saver ❤️'; 'the best app to help me with my crazy ADHD'; 'ADD/ADHD/OCD me Loves You!!!'); the one 1★ is an ADHD user whose household tasks no longer fit in 3 free habits; mental health 4 (5.00 — depression, bipolar 1, memory loss, low mood). Report 52: medication and chronic-illness logging named in reminder praise (an IVF medication schedule; a chronic-illness patient agitated by ads); the ADHD subtitle has only 6 supporting reviews (0.03%) in a 20,634-review Chinese corpus. Report 53: medication, stroke, bariatric care, alcohol recovery and brain-injury users ('I haven't missed a dose since I started using this app') — a small set of older, disabled or recovering users most exposed to confusing billing. Report 54: 7 self-identified ADHD, autistic or anxious reviewers all at 4–5★ discovered the fit themselves though the subtitle names ADHD; 'with my adhd, once it's closed i never use it' (widget). Report 56: one ADHD reviewer — 'tried countless apps that claim to help neurodivergent people… They end up being made for quick cash grabs or having a wildly confusing interface… With Dots, you get exactly what you download' — the report advises earning the audience by staying simple, not claiming it (n=1). Report 57: two US ADHD reviewers disagree — one left over the ad at first setup, one calls colour coding and views 'amazingly functional for my ADHD'; a medication user asked for multiple stamps per day in 2019. Report 58: 8 of 91 self-identify as ADHD or neurodivergent, unprompted, across 6 storefronts, all 5★, 5 tying it to simplicity ('ADHD HEAVEN… Not overwhelming or complicated… my brain is happy'; 'Setting up is simple. No extras') while the listing does not target ADHD — 'produced by users, not by marketing'; one wants more celebration for dopamine. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'As an ADHD person'; 'keeps me together with my bad ADHD'; 'Я очень забывчивая, и это приложение буквально спасает меня' (very forgetful; this app literally saves me) — OUT_MEMORY 326 (2.15%), USE_HEALTH distinctive in the US (6.89×) and UK (8.76×), OUT_MEMORY in France (3.34×) and Sweden (5.01×); these users are the most exposed to the missing task time; students (USE_STUDY 90 — 'made a student's life five times easier') and managers (USE_WORK 163 — 'the flow of tasks is endless') are the other named contexts. Report 60 (Mindway): an app named for ADHD — 4 of 216 (1.85%) mention it, 3 praise the fit at 5.00 with zero ADHD-related complaints, across US, TR and CH: 'This app helps me a lot since I was suffering from ADHD from my childhood. It helps me organize my day'; 'As someone with ADHD. This helps me stay on task instead of getting distracted'; 'Parfait pour un TDAH'; and 'I don't think I have ADHD but it really helps' — the positioning reaching beyond its target rather than narrowing the market; D4: commit to the ADHD positioning and say so in the listing — the only differentiated claim the corpus supports and one Reminders / Notes / Calendar cannot match. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an Arabic reviewer became consistent with morning adhkār, dhikr and daily Qur'an reading ('even if just a page') and advises others to include remembrance of God in their habit — a religious-practice use case the 'Atomic Goals & Accountability' positioning does not address, already running 3+ habits, i.e. over the free cap. Report 65 (Rabit): subtitled 'ADHD Help' but only 2 of 498 reviewers name ADHD or autism — one ADHD user: 'Esse App é tudo que eu sempre quis', one autistic user uncomfortable with the icon; medication adherence and depression use cases rely on reminders that stopped firing; §9.4: re-examine the positioning before spending further on it. Report 67 (Habio): the ADHD audience the ads target is the most harmed segment (97, mean 1.25) and finds the product 'way too overwhelming' for ADHD; §8.9: a short path to the first tracked habit, skippable pop-ups, the quiz after first value. Report 69 (TheFor): one ADHD reviewer ('Finding this app though CHANGED the game') on an app whose listing never mentions ADHD — 'do not build an ADHD strategy on a single review'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 5 name ADHD, ADD or hypersensitivity as why the visual approach works where others failed — 'Ich (ADHS) habe schon so viel ausprobiert… Nichts hat funktioniert. Diese App macht mich froh.'; mental health / anxiety 7 ('a space where you want to be yourself and grow without pressure or shame'). Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): health uses 9 (medication 5, diet 4, ADHD / rehab 2), all Japanese. Report 76 (Way of Life): USE_ADHD 23 (4.91★), USE_MENTAL 27 ('someone who lives with a mood disorder'; 'I used this to get me out of a rough depression'), USE_ADDICTION 46 (4.96★), USE_COACH 20 (4.95★) — all above the corpus mean. Report 83 (Roubit): ADHD 4, autism 1 ('I am autistic and find it very hard to manage routines', 5★), depression 2, anxiety 2 — USE_MENTAL_HEALTH 16 at 4.75★; 3 of 27 payers name a condition. Report 85 (Habitica): USE_ADHD 71 (2.06%, 4.41★) is the fastest-growing audience — 6.0% of E5 vs ≤1.3% in E1–E3; the instant reward of XP and gold is the mechanism they name ('The first app that helps me with my ADD'; 'I have ADHD and find it hard to do tasks, but this app has been a game changer'); the same audience names the failure modes: pop-ups that derail the task, punishments that feel arbitrary or absent ('ADHD, autism, and executive dysfunction, not helpful', 2★), too much stimulus ('Demasiados impulsos texto y provoca que te distraigas', 2★), and the loss of a guild that worked as a support group; USE_MENTAL 51; professionals recommend it (SEG_PRO 16: a psychotherapist, a life coach, an autism/ADHD support worker).

title: Flexible / custom frequency — N times per week, specific weekdays, counts — with non-scheduled days neutral in the statistics
statement: Every X days, specific weekdays, bi-weekly, quarterly, yearly, total-over-a-window — the #1 unmet functional need and highest 4★ lift. Report 12: weekday-only repeats were asked for in Jul 2022 and still missing in May 2026 — three years and ten months. Report 20: frequency was 'N times in M days' only — specific weekdays ('Gym Mon/Wed/Fri') were never expressible in seven years (22 requests) and drove a share of the notification complaints. Report 23: times-per-week, per-day, per-month and every-N-days shipped incrementally; still absent after eleven years — yearly goals, arbitrary intervals (every 6 weeks, quarterly, a shift worker's 4–5-day rotation) and specific dates of the month (101 requests, 1.39%); a non-daily habit also consumes a daily slot under the cap. Report 24: per-weekday / shift-work scheduling requested by 31, 51.6% of them 4–5★. Report 25: flexible scheduling primitives are a stated reason to choose the app — an every-N-days reminder ('the ONLY APP I've found'), N×/week, skip, vacation mode, a custom day-start for shift workers (capped at 11:45); a weekly habit cannot be pinned to a chosen day. Report 26: flexible recurrence ('3× per week') and a vacation/pause mode ('exception periods' while travelling) requested by 12 (0.31%); only per-habit day-of-week scheduling exists. Report 27: flexible weekly frequency shipped ~2025 and is praised ('tasks that can be completed a few times a week rather than everyday'); per-weekday scheduling ('run 1 mile per day during the week, and skip Saturday + Sunday') remains a request; a Monday week-start setting was asked twice in early 2024 and never again. Report 28: a weekly-target-only model — monthly, every-other-week, multiple-times-per-day and specific-weekday scheduling requested by 15 (1.83%), one explicitly blocking a purchase: 'I can't see myself purchasing without being able to make these distinctions'. Report 29: weekday checkboxes only — x times per week without naming days ('practice golf 3 times a week but it doesn't matter on which days'), every other week ('My off days Fri, Sat, Sun every other week… its frustrating' — the only feature-driven 1★), monthly and custom intervals (14, 3.83%) — the one structural gap persisting across all five half-years. Report 30: non-daily scheduling (days of week, x per week, weekly, monthly) is the only feature gap with multi-market evidence — 4 storefronts, 4 languages — and the only build item the report supports. Report 31: 'N times per period' with no fixed days is praised by 81 (a monthly view prevents 'feel bad' spirals); removing monthly and yearly frequencies (Dec 2022 – Jan 2023) drew 58 requests still arriving in 2026 ('This was the ONE reason I used to love this app'; contact lenses monthly, weight loss yearly; 'call friend once a month or take a vacation three times a year'; deep-clean the oven monthly). Report 33: 'N times a week' and every-N-days frequency are named differentiators (flexible scheduling praised 79, mean 4.80); 'N per week' was removed in Habitify X and restored; monthly nth-weekday and end dates are still requested (82; haircut, bills on the 15th, can't end a 30-day challenge). Report 34: x-days-per-week added on request (Apr 2019), flexible frequency praised by 13 (mean 4.92); every-other-day and monthly targets still requested (7). Report 36: flexible schedules (every N days, N×/week or month) requested by 7 in E1–E3 and not since Dec 2024 (probably addressed); habits shown on unscheduled days (3, all 4–5★). Report 41: 'X times per week, any days' / 'every N days' (13) and seeing which day a weekly habit was done (9) — one request asked twice, every year 2021–2026, 8 of 13 at 4★: 'I would like the option of doing something 3 times a week, not necessarily on the same day'; the app models which-days and how-many-times as alternatives. Report 42: setting which days, dates and repetition is Premium ('task repetition is paid-plan only', JP 1★); 'Tue & Thu' and shifting a habit to another day requested. Report 43: scheduling flexibility is the longest-running unaddressed request (29, 4.55%, mean 3.38; Jan 2017 → Jan 2025) — intervals beyond one month ('Wish I'd known that before I paid for it'), Nth weekday ('1st Tuesday of each month'), 'X times per week' without fixed days, every other week, a due date rolling from last completion; a redesign regression made 'every 2/3 weeks' habits show every week. Report 46: every-N-days, X-per-week without fixed days and monthly schedules are the longest-running functional request (34, mean 4.09, every era Sep 2019 → Jul 2026) — 'a medicine I must use every other day and I can't put it on this app'; a shift worker on trial calling it 'potentially a deal breaker'; 'most of my habit are repeated every 3 days… Apple reminders is WAY more efficient' (churned). Report 47: X-per-week and monthly habits requested by 8 (mean 4.12) — absent, and a 5★ requester withdrew the request to protect simplicity. Report 48: arbitrary cadences such as every-other-day requested by 35 (3.97); weekday scheduling — weekly goals that still demand a daily answer — 21 (3.57). Report 50: 'at least N per week' goals missing (2, 5.00 — a weekly goal marked complete at Mon–Thu cannot record Friday and Sunday); every-other-day, future start date and 15-minute increments requested (4). Report 52: monthly, every-other-day and N-per-week rules (299); weekly-N habits spoil a '100% day'. Report 53: '3 times a week, any day', every other day, a day of the month (CORE_FREQ 54, 3.76); a 3×/week habit fails Monday and Tuesday and support's Skip 'skips that task for the week'; '2 times weekly' must be done twice in one day. Report 54: 'X times a week without naming the days' — 24 (6.50%, 3.79); two call the scheduling model 'unusable' ('I don't care or know when those days will be but this app makes you designate them'; shift workers, DE). Report 55: 'You set your own standards (every day, certain days a week, or a number of days in a week/month)… it doesn't disqualify you if you don't do each habit every single day' (CORE_FLEX 148, 4.82 — the named differentiator); gaps: weekly totals, monthly periods, custom week start, optional end dates. Report 56: non-daily scheduling is the oldest request (day one) and the only one with a rating penalty — the corpus's only 3★: 'Great daily but no weekly… I love the daily tracking for free with no premium version, but I feel like we need a weekly/monthly/select days option!'; five of six forms reduce to 'this habit is not daily' (x per week, weekly, monthly, select days); a deadline request is a different product (D1). Report 57: every-N-days, monthly, yearly and month-end scheduling requested (7). Report 58: times per day, per weekday ('only make habits show up on specific days for my gym sessions'), biweekly and monthly — 4 reviewers, 4 storefronts, one gap in a weekly-goal model. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_HABIT_OPTIONS 113 (0.74%) and REQ_RECURRENCE 51 — habit scheduling and count options are a steady request beside REQ_CUSTOMIZE 234, the largest single request (80 of the 4★ reviews). Report 60 (Mindway): recurrence limited to daily / weekly / monthly is the largest functional request — R_REPEAT_OPTIONS 3 and R_CUSTOM_TASKS 4 of only 10 requests: 'I don't need to flip my mattress every month, but that's the only option I'm given'; hourly hydration, every 2 weeks, every 6 months, haircuts; plus fixed 28/38-day programme pacing the user cannot control ('neden tüm planları kendimiz hemen o gün yapamıyoruz'); D5: fix the recurrence model before adding anything else — four of ten requesters ask for flexibility in different words. Report 65 (Rabit): CORE_FREQ 9 (1.81%, mean 4.11), all Brazilian over five years — 'Preciso estudar música 3x por semana (0/3)… (1/3), (2/3) e (3/3)'; 'minha rotina não permite sempre me exercitar nos mesmo dias'; 'Sem isso a assinatura não vale a pena' (a conditional purchase); with skip, partial multi-per-day, reset time and week start, 15 reviews (3.01%) describe one model limitation — fixed weekdays; S2; research: why only Brazilians ask. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): strength-training users — rest days are part of training, so a daily rule does not fit (REQ_FREQ 8). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): more repeat intervals — 'cada 15 días … o una vez al mes'; 'add monthly as a repeat option' (2). Report 76 (Way of Life): the one structural request for fifteen years — U_FLEX_REQ 347 (4.47%, mean 4.13★) = REQ_FREQUENCY 214 (weekdays, N times a week, weekly/monthly) + REQ_COUNT 129 (quantities) + NEG_YESNO 36 (a partial state); present in 15 of 16 calendar years and in every era (1.8–4.5%); the most frequent code in 4★ after generic praise (96 of 1,281) and 2.39× more common among purchasers than the corpus; a 2016 reviewer was 'waiting for the promised weekly/monthly options' and they never came (NEG_DEV_PROMISE); users emulate it with skip, which distorts the percentages they value (NEG_CHART 38); §8.4 schedule on weekdays or N/week with non-scheduled days neutral and excluded from percentages, counts as a separate journal type, yes/no as the default, guarding against bloat (PR_KEEP_SIMPLE 64). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'x times per week' scheduling is the only feature requested twice by otherwise-happy 4★ users, 11 months apart ('3 veces a la semana o 2 veces al mes'; ''x-mal pro Woche' zu definieren anstatt 'a Tag x und y'… Mich verwundert, dass es das nicht gibt'); scheduling is weekday-only; the use case is 'go to the gym three times a week, any three days'; 'an app built on missing a day is fine still forces users to name the days' — a scheduling-model gap that contradicts the product's own thesis; §8.8 one of the three things to do. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_WEEKLY_SCHEDULE 3 (4.67★, 2024-10 → 2026-07), partial only (v2.4.0 lets you disable streak/consistency; no weekly target): 'a gym habit done 3×/week can never build a streak, so the app's core feedback loop breaks for non-daily habits'; 'Wenn ich einzelne Tage skippen könnte, oder ein Wochenziel festlegen… Das wäre der 5. Stern für mich' (4★) — one of only two pre-committed-star requests in the corpus. Report 83 (Roubit): REQ_FLEX_SCHEDULE 10 (2.00%) — every N days, weekly counts, reps ('if it's 10 planks a day'), recurring deadlines, a pomodoro timer. (Consolidation after report 83: title widened from 'Flexible / custom frequency' to name the three shapes and the statistics rule; the earlier evidence stays in the statement.) Report 84 (HabitGrid): REQ_FREQUENCY 5 (5.81%), the only recurring request, in five variants (N per week without fixed days, specific weekdays, every N days, monthly, custom interval), one attaching rating elasticity ('if it appears, this app will have no equal'); all five predate 1.0.15 'Smarter habit goals' and none of the 27 reviews after repeats it; §8.5 check each variant against the shipped goals — where present, the fix is discoverability. Report 85 (Habitica): REQ_FREQ 45 (1.31%) — '3 times a week'; 'there being no option for truly weekly tasks' (1★); REQ_DUE 12; REQ_REPEAT_TODO 9; §8.6 'N times per week' Dailies. Report 86 (Today): scheduling covers daily / weekdays / N per week (max 6) or month (max 25) / multiple check-ins a day — the most complete in the series — yet REQ_FREQ 27 still ask for every-N-days ('If the app had this capability, I would rate it 5 stars and purchase the full version') and weekday-only reminders ('add weekday-only reminders and I'll pay immediately', cn).

merged_from.note: reports 76, 77, 79 and 83 attached the shape of the request and its cost: the one structural request for fifteen years, in 15 of 16 calendar years, the most frequent 4★ reason and 2.39× over-represented among purchasers (report 76); the only feature requested twice by otherwise-happy 4★ users, and thesis-inconsistent for a forgiving tracker (report 77); a gym habit done 3×/week can never build a streak and a pre-committed fifth star (report 79); every-N-days, weekly counts and reps (report 83); reports 76 and 77 both specify that non-scheduled days must be neutral and excluded from percentages because users emulate frequency with skip and corrupt their own stats

title: Mac / desktop / web app
statement: Strongest 3★ driver; users volunteer to pay extra for it. Report 23: the Mac app was a separate purchase in 2020–21, then included in the universal purchase from late 2021 (≥8 reviews, a classifier miss at 1); one unverified report of the Mac app creating millions of files and locking the user out. Report 25: a Mac app is part of the included platform surface (8 mentions, mean 4.00). Report 27: a macOS app requested once, 5★. Report 31: iPad / Mac / landscape / web / Android wanted by 98 (1.89%, mean 3.49), peaking in the 4★ band (7.5%) and in E1 (5.3%), falling to ~1% after 2021 as those users left. Report 33: a Mac app (sold separately in 2018), a menu-bar mini app, web, Android and Windows exist; the Mac app could not sign in or sync through 2021–22 (Mac/web 18.5% of 2022, Russia 10.1%) until macOS 13.0.1. Report 34: no iPad / Mac / web app (8) — 'The only reason i'm going with a competitor … is because I don't always want to use my phone'; 'I'd even pay for separate versions as long as they synced'. Report 43: a macOS / desktop app requested by 3 (mean 4.67); the listing claims Mac (M1+) — possibly discoverability. Report 46: a web app and Chrome new-tab extension pre-dated the iPhone app and held the early community ('I have it as my default Chrome tab page'; 'I am not allowed my phone at work'), fading 2.15% → 0.23%; the Mac build is criticised as slow. Report 48: a Mac app from ~March 2022 was welcomed by long-term users and lifted multi-platform praise to 3.13%; the web app (2015 – ~2019) was discontinued and its removal is still resented — 17 want it or Android back (0.84% of 2022–26), Windows users in particular lost access. Report 49: iPad and Mac builds exist but layouts are broken (device incompatibility 15, mean 1.27). Report 50: Mac and iPad companion with one account (praised). Report 52: a Mac build exists but cannot bind the WeChat account the membership lives on. Report 55: no Mac or web app (PLATFORM_WANT 24). Report 57: Mac requested by 8 (all Korean). Report 59 (Tappsk): U_PLATFORM_REQ 385 (2.54%) — REQ_DESKTOP 208, REQ_WEB 104, REQ_ANDROID 28; desktop requests fall from 6.0% of the launch year to 0.6% after the Mac app and hold near 1% since, shifting to Windows and the browser ('Сделайте версию для ПК на WINDOWS 10'; 'нужна веб версия, товарищи'); the report's experiment is a read-mostly web view priced into Premium to test demand before a full client; REQ_WATCH fell from 4.7% to 0.0% after the Watch app shipped. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_MAC 23 (4.52★), REQ_WEB 14 (4.43★), REQ_ANDROID 3 — the highest-rated requests in the list, from users who already love it. Report 86 (Today): REQ_MAC 14 (2016 → 2021) — never; Momentum's desktop sync envied ('I like their desktop sync, wink!').

title: Grouping / folders / categories / tags
statement: #2 feature request in report 1; the highest-mean request in report 3 (zero 1–2★, power users tracking 20–100 counters); named in report 8's only subscription-price statement. Report 20: categories/folders (58) and a compact row option (26) co-occur — both are what happens when a power user exceeds ~8 habits. Report 23: extra capacity is wanted for time-of-day pages (morning / work / evening / bedtime) and life-domain segmentation (health / work / relationships / creative). Report 25: groups and sub-groups are a praised paid feature (customisation 65, mean 4.49); group creation reported locked on free. Report 26: per-habit gardens or categories requested (18). Report 27: tags exist but existing tags cannot be selected and duplicates don't group — two storefronts, two months apart, same bug, both cost stars. Report 31: groups/categories (added Mar 2018) were paid and valued by buyers; forced daily/weekly grouping and order resets in v3.0 (22) drew complaints. Report 33: areas / folders (Dec 2019) are free and mixed (31). Report 41: lists / tags with per-list rings and widget filtering (2022). Report 46: folders / habit groups shipped Aug 2025 after 10 requests ('The new habit folder feature is — chef's kiss'). Report 48: tags / filters / a Today list are premium; requested by 26 (4.12). Report 50: journal notes filterable by activity or category. Report 53: 'so close to perfect… ability to group activities' (4★). Report 56: separate lists / habit groups requested once. Report 58: user-defined sections requested once — test as an opt-in invisible until the first section is created. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_PROJECTS 33, REQ_TAGS 24, REQ_CHECKLIST 21; PR_LISTS 185 and hidden lists (books, films, shopping) 29 are praised. Report 60 (Mindway): 'There is no folder system. I can't categorize my reminders' (one 3★ request). Report 65 (Rabit): routine grouping caps at two even for subscribers, or duplicates habits and empties tabs. Report 76 (Way of Life): tags shipped (PR_TAGS 35, 4.77★, from 2014-06) and REQ_CATEGORIES 37 (0.48%) still ask for groups / sections; REQ_TAG_FILTER 1. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_CATEGORIES 1 (4★, a user with many boards); UX_LIST_SCALE 2 — the one-page list stops scaling for heavy users. Report 84 (HabitGrid): categories shipped in 1.0.14 and were praised 21 days later ('great that there are categories'); archiving shipped in 1.0.13 unmentioned. Report 86 (Today): REQ_CATEGORY 11 (2016 → 2023) never; REQ_SORT 11 added but slow.

title: Shortcuts / Siri / URL scheme / API
statement: Power users who evangelise. Report 23: Siri Shortcuts, URL actions and NFC triggers are a power-user favourite (72, 0.99%, mean 3.94). Report 25: Siri Shortcuts exist; a Mac app and formerly Vision Pro; Shortcuts gaps 1. Report 31: Siri Shortcuts were removed in the Mar 2022 rebuild and automations broke (14). Report 33: x-callback / Shortcuts, Zapier / IFTTT, a public API, calendar sync and NFC habits serve power users (47, rising to 2.5% of E5; API 'unbeatable'; 'Pairs nicely with agentic workflows'); Siri Shortcuts broke in Habitify X. Report 41: Siri Shortcuts with near-full app control praised by 36 ('I was able to automate 80% of habits tracking'); public API / Zapier / IFTTT requested by 5. Report 43: Siri / Shortcuts praised by 5 (all US); one asks for Shortcuts integration. Report 48: Siri Shortcuts praised (17 with Health); an API or IFTTT / Zapier automation requested by 11 (4.18). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_INTEGRATIONS 57 (Siri, Reminders, Health), REQ_CALENDAR_SYNC 56, REQ_NOTIF_ACTIONS 28, REQ_QUICK_ACTIONS 21. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_INTEGRATION 14 (4.29★; ru 5.78×); the listing ships Siri & Shortcuts. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): Siri Shortcuts / automation incl. NFC tags praised by five ('set it [on] one of my nfc tags'); the v2.1.0 overhaul required custom shortcuts to be re-configured. Report 83 (Roubit): NFC tag check-ins (Korea) — PRAISE_NFC 2; a user paid for the plan and bought stickers and the tag did not work; stickers out of stock. Report 86 (Today): REQ_INTEGRATION 34 (Shortcuts / third-party, 2016 → 2026) — a URL scheme only; 'any plans on giving us an update for iOS 14. Widgets, Shortcuts integration… The silence is a little concerning' (2020).

title: Cumulative totals and total-days counter
statement: '47 hours read this year'; total days instead of consecutive to reduce streak anxiety. Report 47: totals and statistics requested by 11 (mean 4.55); cumulative total shipped by 2025; a payer wants average and total study time. Report 50: stats praised by 23 (4.83) — weekly / monthly / yearly reports, grid map, success percentage, 'consistency (not only streaks)'; payers name statistics depth as the value. Report 53: totals and trends in units, not only completion % — 'a total of 1000 push ups'; a 7-hour sleep against an 8-hour goal shows 0% (R6).

title: Flexible units / partial progress
statement: Drag to 60% instead of a binary tick — a named reason for choosing over competitors. Report 23: 77 reviews (1.06%) in seven languages ask to record effort beyond the goal or short of it — over-achievement is discarded ('goal 30 minutes, read 90, it stops at 30') and partial progress renders as failure ('6 of 8 glasses shows an ✗'); the two most-upvoted reviews in the 7,270-review corpus (313 and 126 votes) are this request; 'do 30 push-ups' breaks on a 25 day where 'push-ups per day' would record 25 and preserve momentum. Ship floor-without-ceiling goals and a partial-progress calendar state without changing the streak rule. Report 25: measurement units — count, minutes, distance, custom steps — and track-only habits with no goal number. Report 29: quantity/unit tracking (steps, litres, reps; one proposes a slider) requested by 4 — only as an optional habit type outside the default flow. Report 31: unit tracking with custom increments (dollar amounts for business referrals) is praised; a custom-count input bug added an extra unit ('I type in 50 pages … it counts 55', 16). Report 33: goals with units and multiple check-ins per day shipped in Aug 2020; custom units (kg, kcal, metric) and icons still requested (56). Report 34: quantity / partial completion requested by 11 — 'I Drank 80oz … I wanna be able to track that'; '8 of 10 glasses counts as progress'. Report 36: multiple completions per day / quantity targets (water in ounces) requested by 5. Report 43: multiple completions per day with 0/2, 0/4 counters (water, reps) exist free and are a purchase trigger ('the 0/2, 0/4 etc feature that visually shows you how far behind you are… it made me buy it'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 46: several completions per day (12) and numeric targets — glasses, steps, pages (9, mean 4.56) — requested. Report 48: numeric Target and rolling Average trackers are the reason 485 reviewers chose the app; flexible units requested by 13 and true time-duration HH:MM by 8 — see [[C265]]. Report 53: US units only for water, weight and distance ('Stuck with Dopey American units'; 'In Europe we have no idea what a US Fl Oz is!'; notifications in ounces with litres selected — DES_UNITS 47, 20 storefronts); log beyond the goal (CORE_OVER 10). Report 55: numeric habits with 'at least', 'exactly' or 'not more than' success rules alongside yes/no — 'counting habits like 8 glasses of water a day'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'store a value or note per day (walked 5k, then 7k) and see it over time' (ZA, 4★) — the same data-model change as within-day counting (P5). Report 69 (TheFor): a numeric goal set by a scroll wheel capped at 10,000 — 'I want to be able to type the number for my goal instead of having to scroll for a minute'; 'Хотела выставить цель:12000 шагов - максимально выдает 10000' — two independent users two years apart; F6: 'a one-afternoon fix'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): enter numbers, counts or durations instead of a check (2) and more than one check a day (2). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_COUNT 129 (1.66%, 4.22★) quantities / several times a day, in every era (0.8–2.9%); NEG_YESNO 36 want a partial or 'yellow' state; §8.4 test an optional count per day as a separate journal type, keeping yes/no as the default. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): check-in of amounts with custom units (PRAISE_FLEXIBLE 7, 4.71★: 'a task with a completely open schedule'); notes + custom units were the roadmap items one buyer waited for.

title: Mood tracker
statement: Meaningful praise where shipped; mentions rose after launch (report 1); asked for only by 5★ users (report 8); an automatic mood prompt is a memory aid and moving it behind a button destroyed users' mood datasets (report 10). Report 24: a daily mood check-in exists inside the routine app. Report 25: a Russian lifetime buyer with ADHD proposes a mood/energy tracker so the statistics screen can answer why a habit failed. Report 28: a mood tracker with limited free moods (paid moods 10 complaints, mean 3.90; mood entry mandatory on open 2); journal/mood used by 38 (4.63%, mean 4.29). Report 33: a mood log (Aug 2021) with multiple moods per day as Premium — 14 mentions, mixed. Report 41: mood tracking added via Apple Health (Sep 2024, 'I'm very happy to see mood tracking added'); 5 wanted it inside the app's own history. Report 50: a mood tracker and body-weight tracker bundled in. Report 58: themed mood, gratitude and day-rating logging proposed in a 1,030-character review. Report 65 (Rabit): a mood / feelings diary and wellness prompts (REQ_MOOD 3, mean 5.00).

title: One-off to-dos alongside habits
statement: Emerging request. Report 18: routines and one-off to-dos interleaved in one time-ordered list was a named purchase trigger and 'MyRoutine's one advantage' over to-do apps; to-do parity (carry-over, subtasks, tags, priority, undated, recurring) was requested ~30 times. Report 25: one-off, non-repeating tasks in a separate list or tab requested by 10 (7 of them 4★) alongside the time-of-day request. Report 28: a to-do checklist exists separately from habits and users want it to earn carrots (9, mean 4.44 — 'the more irksome and time consuming tasks that you procrastinate on'). Report 31: one-off tasks / today-only items requested by 28 (mean 2.86). Report 33: one-off tasks requested by 10. Report 50: tasks / to-dos and 'Lista' sections alongside habits (requested May 2024, shipped); the list section reported broken (MX, Aug 2026). Report 52: to-dos (小事) shipped ~2024 and rose to 3.0% of that year's reviews — welcomed, then sorting and hiding regressions. Report 59 (Tappsk): the strongest evidence yet for the hybrid — a daily to-do list with a habit row on the same screen is what 15,176 reviewers praise: PR_ALLINONE 293 (1.93%), PR_HABITS 445, and the most-voted review in the corpus (156 votes) is 'Задачи и привычки в одном приложении - гениально' (tasks and habits in one app — genius); switchers come from Notes/Reminders, Todoist, Trello, Notion and Things. The to-do half brings its own design decisions: today / tomorrow / this week / later buckets (PR_SECTIONS 134, PR_ONE_SCREEN 82; Germany praises the one screen at 8.92×), automatic carry-over of unfinished tasks (PR_AUTO_CARRY 69 — 'all your unfinished today's tasks move to tomorrow') which the report says to keep as the default but with a per-task opt-out because recurring tasks carrying over is unwanted by 28 and recurring tasks invisible on future dates by 32; and the missing event time ([[C276]]). Report 65 (Rabit): a separately paid to-do list — 'só o todo-list que não é [gratuito], achei meio injusto' — that vanished for a payer and has no reminders ('die sinnlose Aufgabenliste ohne Erinnerungsfunktion… Total sinnfrei'). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_SUBTASKS 6 (to-dos / subtasks, 2014 → 2018).

title: Android version
statement: Requested; cross-platform continuity matters to switchers. Report 26: Android asked about repeatedly (CN, FR, SE). Report 31: Android and web appear in the 98 platform requests. Report 47: an Android version exists; Apple ↔ Samsung sync is why some users chose it and why 2022 sync failures hurt. Report 52: Android build exists but membership, price and login differ (PLAT_ANDROID 195, 3.53). Report 57: Android requested by 13 (all Korean) — 'please release this on Play Store so Galaxy users can use it too'. Report 65 (Rabit): an Android build exists but cannot restore to iPhone. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_ANDROID 3 in 7,764 reviews.

title: Points / rewards / wish list
statement: Weak request; one proposes a cash-stake mode. Report 48: gamified rewards requested by 17 (4.47); the 2013–14 points system drew 10 complaints and was dropped. Report 52: 光芒值 'sunshine points' earned per check-in and exchanged for self-set wishes — 312 (1.51%, 4.65), rising from under 1% before 2021 to 1.9–3.1% after; praised as a way to delay spending and curb impulse buying; requests for separate point currencies and for multi-check habits to earn points. Report 58: points redeemable for self-chosen real-world rewards requested once.

title: Custom time-of-day segments
statement: Beyond morning/afternoon/evening — shift workers. Report 23: one page per time of day — morning, work, evening, bedtime — is the top reason people ask for more capacity. Report 33: time-of-day sections (morning / afternoon / evening / anytime) are a named differentiator — 'no other app does as well'; 'the best thing about Habitify' — and paired with flexible frequency form 'a winning core'; a hidden time-of-day filter also produced false bug reports. Report 54: time-of-day grouping named as a differentiator by 10 (2.71%). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): morning / afternoon / evening grouping — evening habits render above morning ones despite the configured order, and a habit added to all three slots lands only on evening (§8.2 #8). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_DAY_ROLLOVER 9 — a custom day end.

title: Never run incentivised / review-for-premium campaigns
statement: Bought rank and a fake average, 0.86% purchase signal, reputational backlash, unreadable data. Report 26: a review-for-cosmetic-unlock reward produced reviewers who volunteer they have not used the app; the ≤25-char 5★ tier doubled to ~35% of the corpus. Report 33: review solicitation — a founder-named 5★ burst (12 Oct – 1 Nov 2018: 110 reviews at mean 4.64 vs 3.30 before), 'a strange email … asking for a rating', a free-lifetime link after reviewing, contests awarding Premium, and a CEO asking for 5★ — 'Who the hell is peter?'; the burst left no durable effect and the report's last cheapest win is to stop it. Report 34: a free-lifetime giveaway (~29 Jun 2023) produced 27 short, mostly 5★ reviews in three days (55.6% ≤ 25 characters) and moved the mean by ~0.01. Report 42: six US 5★ reviews in three days (Aug 2020) with 13–30 helpful votes each and nonsense titles ('Hgfgg', 'Bdbdbd'), and eleven of Canada's twelve reviews 5★ generic praise in 13 days (May 2021) — 17 reviews (8.25%) that inflate the mean from 2.968 to 3.136 and leave Canada unmeasurable. Report 43: a launch-week burst of 13 seeded 5★ reviews inside 24 minutes moved a ten-year corpus by 0.02. Report 46: an aggressive in-app rating prompt produced 297 reviews (13.64%) in 44 days in May–June 2023 at mean 4.58 vs 4.29 — permitted by Apple, not fake, but it tripled volume with contentless 5★, diluted every later negative rate and 'made the post-2023 corpus less informative per review'; 17 reviews say they are writing only to make it stop. Report 52: a 2017 review-to-unlock gate (reminders unlocked by writing a review, with a length check) produced 462 unlock reviews, 427 in 2017, all 15 busiest days of nine years, keyboard-mash filler and 5★ reviews reading 'please stop forcing people to write reviews' — the launch year is unusable as a baseline. Report 68 (Ultiself): in 2026 named support agents ('Nick', 'Emma', 'Michael', 'Sam') resolved complaints with refunds and free lifetime access and asked for reviews — 14 of 45 E6 named-agent reviews report a refund or gift ('He canceled my subscription, issued a refund, and even upgraded me to lifetime access'); 'My feedback goes to Michael who asked me to write it'; 'Please post one review per day' inside a 5★; PR_SUPPORT rose from 9 reviews before 2025-10 to 62 of 1,238 after; §8.4: stop asking support contacts for reviews. Report 83 (Roubit): four reviews from January–March 2022 were written during a developer survey or for an in-app 'review-writing mission', and three post invite codes for in-app rewards — U:solicited_signal 7 (1.40%), all 5.00★; kept at the star given.

title: Never gate or delete reviews
statement: Users catch it and call it a ToS violation. Report 33: one unverified claim that the developer deleted a review after 5 weeks without support.

title: Don't build AI features on demand grounds
statement: 0.011% demand; users ask for the opposite. Report 23: exactly one review mentions the 'Break It Down' AI feature (May 2026) — and asks for it to be removed. Report 24: an AI chat/coach bubble added ~2025 is an unwanted addition for long-tenure users, and AI-generated art/copy is the worst-rated non-billing theme (64, mean 1.156, 90.6% 1★) — the theme did not exist before 2024. Report 28: zero of 821 reviews request AI features; the only AI mention is a complaint about AI homework-cheating ads served inside the app — 'no evidence of AI demand in this audience'. Report 33: AI 'smart fill' and AI / chatbot support (2025–26) drew mostly negative reviews — 'Stop shoving AI everywhere'. Report 34: across 743 reviews over eight years, no review mentions AI, ChatGPT or an AI feature. Report 36: exactly one review mentions AI — as a substitute after uninstalling over the cap ('doing it with AI daily tasks until I find an alternative'). Report 41: Apple Intelligence habit suggestions shipped (Sep 2025) drew one light positive ('I like the apple AI to help with ideas'), while 'an AI coach' is on the report's do-not-add list. Report 46: 'I'm really sick of apps with a million features and AI just to convolute things' (Apr 2026, 5★). Report 47 (counter-evidence): an AI coach replying to each check-in is the first premium feature reviewers praise unprompted (13, mean 4.69) — see [[C263]]; the objections are silent stops and a toggle bug, not the feature. Report 64 (Critique AI): the AI is the brand ('AI Coach' in the name) and 'among people who used it, the weakest part' — 19 AI reviews at mean 2.21 vs outcomes 4.92 and gamification 4.00; a paying 5★ splits the product: 'for the AI plan? No. For speaking coaching and challenges to improve overall? Yes'; the substitute named for the AI half is ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini. Report 65 (Rabit): zero AI mentions in 498 reviews spanning 2020–2026 — 'worth knowing before assuming AI features are table stakes in this category'. Report 68 (Ultiself): 'I don't really see where the AI is supposed to be working' — personalisation that feels generic (NEG_AI_POOR 23); PR_AI 20 (15 in E6) against NEG_AI_CONTENT 8 (all E6); §8.7: test a demonstrably personal plan against the library. Report 69 (TheFor): a $2.99 'Routine AI' purchase is listed and zero reviews in 3.5 years mention AI in any form. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_AI 1 (kr 3★) raises AI features as an expectation — single voice.

title: Offer a non-pastel / premium design option
statement: Recurring critique from men and users wanting a premium look. Report 25: native Apple design language reads as premium — ''Apple' design all over it'. Report 26: reviewers convert on beauty within minutes of install ('I bought premium within the first couple minutes of downloading'; 'as soon as I saw the visuals and music I bought premium') — aesthetic is the mechanism, not decoration, and 'It's not just an app it's a piece of art'. Report 29: UI/visual design praised by 45 (12.30%, mean 4.64); a font complaint (1); more colours / custom colours requested (4). Report 48: 62 call the UI dated (3.63, rising to 1.68% of E5) while 14 praise its plainness ('does not include "cute" graphics') — the report: do not redesign for novelty; the tap-count lesson is the larger risk.

title: Discovery runs through social video, Reddit, therapists (US) and Xiaohongshu / Bilibili (CN)
statement: Plan marketing around where users say they found the app. Report 10: 381 reviews involve a clinician recommending the app; two clinicians publicly withdrew the recommendation over data loss. Report 19 (negative case): paid Instagram/YouTube ads → web quiz → web checkout → a checklist; six reviewers named the channel and the funnel, not the software, generated the corpus. Report 23: therapists and psychologists recommending it to ADHD clients (28, mean 4.50), Atomic Habits and habit literature (14, mean 4.79), podcasts and blogs (Daring Fireball, MacBreak Weekly, Do By Friday, Diary of a CEO; 12, mean ~4.6); Apple editorial / Design Award traffic was the worst channel (17, mean 2.53). Report 24: acquisition runs through Instagram / Facebook / X ads into a web questionnaire; credibility signals (Duke/Stanford framing, Atomic Habits adjacency) and 'the trial produced a result in days' are the conversion stories. Report 25: Instagram / TikTok / Reels ads are a stated acquisition channel for buyers; three arrive via a clinician. Report 31: TikTok / Instagram / YouTube / press named by 117 (mean 1.72), 81 of 98 TikTok mentions in 2022 — the channel that brought the largest audience arrived during a launch crash. Report 34: launched via Reddit (Jul 2018); 6 reviewers (mean 5.00) say they found it via Reddit, social or reviews; early Reddit adopters wrote long, personal reviews to the developer by name. Report 36: an App Store Awards / Apple Design Award feature drove discovery at launch (Jun 2022); a professional coach prescribes the app to clients. Report 55: a Reddit launch post with the developer answering in the thread produced 21 reviews on day two (4.71 for 2015), and BuzzFeed plus a TV review produced 105 in January 2016 (4.77); a Korean rapper's recommendation in 2019–20; therapists and a clinical psychologist recommend it to clients. Report 57: the only AI-discovery attribution in the corpus — 'I found it by asking GPT to recommend an app with the features I wanted' (KR, 2025); Korean word of mouth (24 advocacy). Report 58: founder TikTok is the only named channel — 8 of 91 ('I saw the creator talking about her app on TikTok'; 'thanks to that tik tok girl'), no reviewer names search, friends or ads; single-channel, founder-dependent acquisition that also inflates the mean via audience selection; attribution fell 13.3% → 4.3% between halves. Report 59 (Tappsk): Russian-language acquisition — the founder's vc.ru article (MKT_PRESS 13), bloggers (MKT_BLOGGER 19: 'посмотрел видео у Маргулана'; 'я смотрела тик ток'), word of mouth (MKT_WOM 41), ads only 9. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): new acquisition routes in 2025–26 — a YouTube appearance and an AI assistant's recommendation ('I asked an AI to recommend apps like this and picked from those'); the developer's book appears alongside the app. Report 71 (MyStreaks): a founder-led content channel — a book, a podcast and the founders (Jeff & Jami) — appears in 8 reviews (25.0%), every one 5★, from the first review (Feb 2021) to the last era: 'This concept, the book, and the app have done a 180 in how I see habits'; 'it wasn't until I found this App + Podcast…' — users 'already bought into the method before they open the app'; 'a durable acquisition advantage no habit-tracker competitor can replicate by shipping features'. Report 76 (Way of Life): press and podcasts are the named acquisition source — MKT_PRESS 51 (0.66%, mean 4.94★), 26 in E4 (Tim Ferriss's podcast with Kevin Rose, Ezra Klein), later Atomic Habits, and in ru/kz Margulan Seisembay ('Спасибо Маргулану Сейсембаю'); 6 purchasers cite press ('Used for one day then upgraded to the paid'); coaches and clinicians recommend it to clients (USE_COACH 20, 4.95★); gb 2.20×, au 3.11×. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): seven reviews name YouTube or Reddit as the acquisition channel ('The dev took feedback from me on Reddit and released my requested feature within a couple of weeks'); PRAISE_INDIE 9 (5.00★) with no entry after 2025-02-28 and CH_YOUTUBE none after 2025-11-25 — 'the early corpus is full of people who followed a developer; the recent corpus is full of people who found an app'; §8.4.4 rebuild the acquisition story or accept a harsher audience. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the funnel is Instagram → quiz → personalised-book checkout with a forced app bundle; every documented path to payment runs through the book, none through the app; U:acquisition_any 12 (6.86%, 1.33★).
