Report 31: Apple Health counts wrong or doubled in 37 (2.7.1 added a year of steps; sleep 14 h; 26,000 vs 5,000 steps) — de-duplicate imports and show the source value alongside the app's value. Report 33: Health sleep double-counting and data wiped when switching tracking mode — de-duplicate, allow manual override. Report 53: reading, meditation and relaxation timers written to Apple Health as exercise minutes or active calories ('One hour of reading in HabitMinder gave me 60 active minutes'); stand counted while asleep; doubled Health statistics (HK_WRITE 8, HK_BUG 61); F7: stop, or make write-back explicit per habit.

title: Manual reordering, renaming and editing of habits/tasks — free
statement: Trivial, requested for years by 5★ users; best effort-to-goodwill ratio. In report 4 rename/reorder was gated and it was the top complaint among paying users. Report 25: habit/group order resets itself (11, 0.84%) — two long-term users left over it; make reordering a drag gesture. Report 26: reorder habits / per-habit gardens / categories requested by 18 (0.47%). Report 27: habit reordering shipped (between Sept 2024 and Aug 2025) and the order does not stick ('they keep getting jumbled up and going back to the wrong spots'); one user avoids reordering for fear of data loss; another wants grouping by the time a habit is set for. Report 29: 'This could be my perfect habit tracker if I could only reorder the list of tasks… Without it the app is virtually useless' (2★); two of four ask to sort by reminder time, which needs no new data model. Report 31: custom order and forced grouping (22) and an edited habit jumping to the top of the list drew complaints — restore custom ordering and stop moving edited habits. Report 33: custom ordering that sticks requested / broken in 47 (90 routines; broken in v10.7.4–10.7.5 and again in 2026). Report 36: cannot delete or rename a habit easily (10, mean 3.00) and a habit-name character limit (3). Report 43: drag-to-reorder within time windows requested by 7 and shipped Nov 2025 ('The ability to program your day windows and reorder items in time windows is fantastic'); bulk edit across a group 1. Report 46: cannot reorder habits (10, mean 4.10); a limited history view (9). Report 47: reorder / sort habits requested by 6 (all JP, mean 4.33); habit order scrambled by an update in 2022 (5). Report 48: can't edit / delete a log entry 32 (3.22); backfill history praised by 13. Report 50: an August 2026 update removed editing or deleting a single occurrence of a recurring habit ('I love this but I was really disappointed in the update that took away ability to modify time or delete single reoccurring events in a day') — fix F5: a straight revert. Report 54: reorder / drag habits (13, 4.54; 5 payers). Report 55: in 2026 habits cannot be deleted or deactivated. Report 56: reorder requests (4) stopped dead once reordering shipped, because it is visible in the list. Report 57: 27 could not find how to delete or edit a habit though the function exists ('How on earth can you make a habit app and not be able to delete the habits'; 'I got angry and deleted the app'; 'I almost threw my phone') — a user documented it publicly; 'it should be a clear option when viewing the habit detailed view'. Report 68 (Ultiself): 'sort those habits chronologically' — REQ_REORDER 7. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): row reordering (4) named as the thing blocking one purchase — possibly already available via long-press. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_REORDER 16 (0.21%, 2011 → 2025) and NEG_EDIT_NAME 3 ('cannot edit items', 2012 → 2015) — both long since fixed but they recur for years. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_SORT 1 (5★) — sort or organise habits. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_REORDER 1 shipped in v2.4.2/2.5.0 and is still reported broken by the corpus's final reviewer; editing an existing board reported as paid by one 2★ ('You don t let me modifie my habits whitout paying'). Report 86 (Today): reorder/sort was added but 'slow' (two reports); parent/child habits requested in a 2016 twenty-item list.

title: Customisable, louder reminder sounds
statement: Asked by happy users; the cheapest 5★ upgrade. Report 20: one reminder per habit with user-written message text — 'small feature, outsized affection' (25 reviews, mean 4.60). Report 65 (Rabit): an audible alarm rather than a silent banner (REQ_SOUND 3, mean 3.00).

title: Skippable, replayable onboarding tour and an in-app help screen — searchable FAQ and per-setting explanations for anything richer than the daily check-in
statement: Hidden gestures (swipe-to-complete, mode toggles) confuse new users; a US-specific 6% complaint in report 2. Report 12: an unskippable narrated intro drew 21 complaints peaking at 16% of 2024 reviews, then fell to one review after a skip control landed — the corpus's clearest fix — while the same intro is praised as a conversion asset. Report 17: a product with its own vocabulary ('what is a sequence? What is a block? What is an activity?') asked for 'a day of experimenting'; users who got through the first day gave 5★, those who didn't quit at 30 minutes — while the paywall demanded payment before that day. Report 18: a five-year vocabulary muddle (습관 vs 루틴 vs 모드) and an onboarding that re-ran on existing and paying accounts with no skip button — a restore-purchase loop returned users to the questionnaire. Report 23: an icon-only first run left new users unable to delete, edit or undo — 63 of 650 1★ reviews; a 66-upvote review asks for plain-language in-app instructions; replace it with a short text-labelled walkthrough covering add / complete / edit / delete / undo / pages. Report 25: confusing/no-guidance 27 (2.06%, mean 2.70); two Brazilian reviewers ask for a tutorial video; comprehension failures worth designing against — how to structure a bad habit ('smoked' or 'didn't smoke'), pinning a weekly habit to a day, stopping a repeat, whether the app is iOS-only. Report 27: a real first-run comprehension cost — four of five confused reviewers got past it and stayed ('a lil hard to figure out at first but now super easy'), the fifth gave 1★; a 30-second skippable explainer is a low-risk fix that does not compromise minimalism. Report 28: 38 onboarding complaints (4.63%, mean 3.24) with one unchanged content for four and a half years — the tutorial teaches the fiction (bunny, mess, carrots) but not how to add, edit or delete a habit ('The tutorial is pointless as they don't show you how to create a task'; 'a steep learning curve with all the unlabeled icons'); 11 more report the add/edit controls genuinely broken and the app cannot tell which it is receiving; the fix is a labelled, skippable tutorial that demonstrates habit CRUD. Report 36: onboarding complaints 16 (mean 1.81, 12 of 16 1–2★), 7.9% of E1 → 1.9% of E5 — 'Is there no manual? Or user guide? I see no way to add new items like a + sign'; 'Is it a game or some kind of something else?' Report 41: onboarding 8 (mean 2.88, lowest non-monetisation) — 'How to use this app🤡 :: Is there a tutorial?'; could not find how to edit a habit; a paying user never started because the skip / miss / stats model was opaque; the report proposes a one-screen 'how this app models habits' card. Report 42: 'Endless screens asking unnecessary questions with no option to skip. I deleted the app after about 15 non-shippable screens, never got to use it'; '~30 questions before I gave up' (both 1★). Report 43: 20 reviews over nine years say there is no tutorial, FAQ or help (see C259). Report 46: onboarding confusion 19 (mean 3.95); the skip-symbol legend is missed at first run and cannot be found again ('I missed the intro and can't find it again'). Report 47: onboarding confusion 9 (mean 2.44) — two could not find back-dating after reading it existed in the update notes, a third the hidden start-date options; today's done / not-done status unclear 5. Report 48: confusing setup 118 (2.68%, 3.11) has sat at 2–3% in E1, E3, E4 and E5 — 'a decade of onboarding friction that no redesign has removed', concentrated on choosing between Habit / Target / Average / Project and on where deletion lives; the existing goal-setting course (credited by 27) could be surfaced at first run. Report 49: onboarding too long 29 (1.55), rising every era to 4.1% — some abandon during the questionnaire before any price is shown. Report 50: onboarding bimodal — confusion 4 (2.75) vs 'The onboarding and habit creation are straight to the point' 3 (5.00). [Merged from C259: Report 43: no guide / tutorial / FAQ / help (9, mean 2.78) plus a learning curve (14, 3.36) — 20 reviews (3.13%) requested continuously from Feb 2017 ('There must be some tips or suggestions in start') to Aug 2026 ('I don't understand nothing') and never addressed: 'There is no help option in settings which makes at least one action I want to take impossible… I can't find instructions for this in the app, on YouTube, or through a Google search'; 'I have had to contact support twice on things that could have explained up front'; 'it took me an hour or so to figure out how to make it work… I'd pay for this if it had some adjustments in usability'. Roughly a tenth of the 29 scheduling-gap reviews ask for capabilities the app already has (custom days, timers, untimed tasks) and land as 1★ / 2★. The same product draws 123 'simple' reviews — daily use is simple, setup is not — so a help screen targets a different surface from the praised simplicity.] Report 52: time-of-day scenes are loved and confusing ('two + buttons'). Report 54: onboarding_confusion 10 (2.71%, 3.70) — the water jar, 'repot' ('Will it restart all my progress?') and where to add a second habit are unexplained. Report 57: onboarding_no_guidance 23 (18 KR, 4 JP) and 65 Korean reviewers (10.74%) asking for help rather than reviewing — an in-app FAQ answering the five most-asked review questions. Report 59 (Tappsk): NEG_ONBOARDING 78 (0.51%, 3.27★) — hidden gestures and an unexplained score make first use confusing even in an app praised for simplicity. Report 60 (Mindway): 'It is overwhelming to set up tasks in the beginning' — a first-run 'pick one of three ready-made days' is the proposed fix (E6); a how-to for bulk-removing unwanted preset tasks is requested by a payer. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'Explain what the options actually do' (PY, 4★) — the cheapest item in the report. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): three could not find how to start (the '+'); onboarding complaints are about absent guidance, never complexity. Report 76 (Way of Life): the interactive walkthrough is praised (PR_ONBOARDING 48, 4.79★; au 4.95×) and the app is 'confusing on first use, simple once learned' — NEG_UI_CONFUSING 81 (1.04%, 3.36★, 12.50% of 2★), NEG_LEARNING_CURVE 17 (4.65★); 'depois do excelente porém extenso tutorial, a gente pega a manha' (after the excellent but long tutorial you get the hang of it, br 4★); BUG_ONBOARDING_LOOP 3 (tutorial stuck). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): UX_LEARNING_CURVE 1 — 'At first I had some trouble following the points logic, but now that I've grasped it, I'm thrilled' (5★); PRAISE_ONBOARDING 1. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): UX_ONBOARDING 1 ('I can't find any directions on what to do', 1★); v2.3.1 later shipped 'Simplified onboarding for first-time users'. Report 85 (Habitica): NEG_LEARNING_CURVE 73 — newcomers struggle to tell Habits, Dailies and To-Dos apart ('Why are there 3 sections. Doesn't make sense', 2★); NEG_HOWTO 8 in Japan (6.5× lift: how to get the Orb of Rebirth, how quests start); France 4.0×; the three task types are also the structural feature praised most (PR_TASKTYPES 91). Report 86 (Today): UX_CONFUSE 74 (4.15%), UX_ONBOARD 20 — people cannot find check-in ('I could never figure out how to check in', 2★), cannot understand the custom chart or counter, cannot tell skipped from missed, cannot find the statistics ('I only stumbled on the charts in the profile section by accident!'); the cost stated plainly: 'The statistics are in the profile. You can't start the app with the list of goals… So I deleted it; otherwise I'd have bought it' (ch 1★).

merged_from.title: An in-app help screen — first-run tour, searchable FAQ, per-setting explanations — for any product whose setup is richer than its daily use
merged_from.note: C259 (report 43: no guide, tutorial or FAQ for eleven years) is the help-screen half of the same need C075 covers (hidden gestures and product vocabulary that new users cannot decode); one learnability requirement

title: Never seed the launch rating — templated or bought reviews decay and leave the markets they cover unmeasurable
statement: Users spot it in week one and say so; it contaminates the analytics baseline permanently. Report 16: a reviewer alleged the beta list was asked to 'overcome outdated reviews'; 23 self-identified beta testers were strongly bimodal and the launch rating was spent within six weeks. Report 19: all eight 5★ reviews in a 441-day corpus landed in one nine-day December window, all US, 44–74 characters, morning-UTC, generic register, one containing a homoglyph ('recọmmend') — the report treats them as unable to bear analytical weight and states every positive figure with and without them. Report 30: two dated phrase-bank campaigns seeded 50% of all reviews; when they stopped the rating fell toward 3.0★ and the organic 1★ rate tripled. Report 30: 83 of 166 reviews (50%) came from a five-phrase list in several languages, all 5★, in two dated campaigns; when they stopped the half-year mean fell 4.65 → 3.00, the organic 1★ rate rose 12.5% → 44.4%, and the US and GB storefronts were left commercially unmeasured (the high-spend group yielded 8 substantive reviews at 3.50 against a 4.79 headline). Report 43: 13 US 5★ reviews within 24 minutes on 10 Oct 2016 ('Use!!', 'Best!!', 'Helful'), three days after the first review — lifted 2016's mean 4.45 → 4.58 and the ten-year mean by 0.02; detected by timestamp clustering, not votes. Report 48: 3 reviews claim fake reviews (1.33); no burst or brigading pattern found — the Jan 2015 spike spans 20 storefronts with unrelated texts. Report 49: 27 reviews invert their stars as a signalling channel ('THIS is actually a one star review. I just wanted you to see it'; 'Gunna remove the one Star as soon as I know you got the message'). Report 60 (Mindway): a 45% two-month burst of very short, very positive, mostly non-English reviews with no duplicated authors or bodies — read as a paid acquisition push plus a first-session rating prompt rather than a farm — is disclosed as 'the single most distorting structural fact in the dataset'; the mean it bought decayed to 3.21 within weeks of the push ending. Report 67 (Habio): SUS_SEED 589 (28.72%, mean 4.91, 2024-03-11 → 2025-02-18) — 94.2% on the US storefront, 33.6% Cyrillic author names vs ~1% elsewhere, 3.1% with any helpfulness vote vs 28.3% of other 4–5★, zero mentions of charges or support; a developer reply pasted into a 5★ body, one paragraph split across three accounts in the same hour, six bodies posted twice by different accounts, referral spam, praise aimed at the complaint ('Cancelled my subscription with no issues at all'), praise for frequent updates while the current build dated from 2024-05-15; they supply 545 of 668 praise codes and coincide with a 4.28 US public rating against a non-seeded mean of 1.31; genuine reviewers cite the gap as proof of fraud ('These scammers pay to have their ratings boosted'); §8.7: stop any programme that sources, incentivises or scripts reviews. Report 68 (Ultiself): E5 (Apr–Sep 2025) holds 2,363 of 4,511 reviews (394 a month vs ~100 either side, mean 4.03 vs 2.23 before) with 230 of 238 generated author names ('nashayla*mogenot@1987qmnp'), 59 of 60 bodies using a look-alike letter 'ọ' to evade duplicate detection, most cross-author duplicate bodies (identical one-liners the same day in Mexico and Uzbekistan) and 1,544 of 1,885 very short 5★; Hebrew, Kazakh, Uzbek, Lithuanian and Latvian reviews almost all E5 one-liners; without E5 the corpus is 41.8% billing complaint and 47.3% praise (mean 3.02) — 'the public rating is not evidence of satisfaction'; earlier, three pairs of long identical US 5★ under different names in 2022-10 → 2023-01. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the soft form — six of the first 13 reviews come from the developer's home region (Romania 4, Hungary 2), two authors carry the developer's surname, none from either storefront appears after month five, and the website's testimonials ('John Harris', 'Maria Smith') match no App Store reviewer; disclosed not adjudicated; excluding the six moves the corpus mean 0.005★; §8.7 'the earliest ratings are the least independent… store rules on reviews from the developer's own circle should be checked, and the website testimonials should be real or removed'.

merged_from.title: Never seed the launch rating with templated or bought reviews — the rating decays and the markets they cover become unmeasurable
merged_from.note: C244 (report 30: two phrase-bank 5★ campaigns, 50% of the corpus) is the strongest instance of C076, not a separate rule

title: Purchase and signup flow must not leak buyers
statement: People who try to pay and cannot (errors, rejected emails, promos that fail to apply) leave 2–4★ and money on the table. Report 14: two willing buyers in 2020 could not complete the purchase ('When I click upgrade button, it only appears an orange screen and then disappears') — the checkout broke in the app's final months. Report 53: an accidental purchase on first open (kr) and a crash right after paying ₩19,000. Report 55: the purchase button crashed in January 2018 — 'I want to give you money! I want more habits! But you're app crashes whenever I try to upgrade' (PAY_IAP_FAIL 14, 10 that month). Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a 5★ Russian user cannot find how to pay — 「Кааак оплатить???????」 — 'Full intent, zero friction tolerance, no sale'. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'money were taken but nothing had changed' (ru 1★); BUG_PURCHASE 9.48× among purchasers. Report 82 (Lasting Change): DEF_LOGIN 14 (8.00%, all but one 1★) — people who paid on the web and could not get into the app: 'we recognise your email adress but the account registration is not complete — you took all the fee in öne min'; 'it says my account doesn't exist'; no create-account option on the sign-in screen; 'my email is not even registered. Then why was I even charged'; present in the first review of the corpus (15 days after release) and still in the last year; §8.7 every successful web payment must end in a usable app account linked by the purchase email. Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_SIGNUP 139 (4.03%, mean 1.55★ — the harshest code: 'people who never got in have nothing else to say'; 'they haven't been able to program a functional login screen in two years'), BUG_ACCOUNT 85: the onboarding Finish button, Google sign-in returning to the same screen, prefilled usernames that cannot be changed; the 2018-02-26 App Store feature day brought new users who could not reach the servers to register (22 reviews that day, 2018 the lowest-rated year at 3.32★); §8.2 'sign-up and login that never dead-ends'.

title: Ship the paid feature working before you sell it — the purchase trigger must never be the broken feature
statement: Paid features carry a higher reliability bar; selling broken sync/calendar/stats put payers a full star below free users. Report 20: the widget was by a wide margin the most-named purchase trigger and the feature that most often didn't work — 182 reviews (mean 1.94), 113 from confirmed payers, broken for five years with an in-app FAQ offering 'restart your phone'; even when present it was a Today-view widget while screenshots implied Home Screen. Ship it properly or remove it from the paywall copy and refund on request. Report 23: the Apple Watch is a purchase driver, not a feature — ≥15 reviews name it as the reason to buy and the explicit-bug subset runs at mean 2.57; if you ship a Watch app its reliability budget is your main reliability budget. Report 41: four of ten post-purchase failures bought for one named capability that then failed (backfill, widget ×2, Health sync) — any single-feature failure is a total failure of the purchase. Report 43: 'purchase not delivered' is the most damaging pattern for a one-time product — 4 buyers got nothing ('I paid to upgrade to get the edit function, but no changes happened… Something broken in the backend??'; 'Purchase premium but still getting free trial capabilities'; 'just took my money'), one could not buy, one could not restore. Report 48: the Jan 2015 subscription launch shipped with a broken release — 81 crash-on-launch, 25 data-loss and 20 duplicate-tracker reviews in the same window — and reviewers linked the two: 'they were asked to start paying for an app that had just stopped working'; the 19 Jan – 30 Sep 2015 window averaged 2.06★ with 73.2% 1–2★. Report 53: statistics — a main reason to pay — crashed for paying users from Sep 2024 (STAT_CRASH 28 of 33 since then, 21.7% of all E4 reviews; payer lift 2.95; the 7-day trend view named by 14); a reviewer reset two years of data trying to fix it; F3 'the feature people pay for'. Report 54: the paid tier's named benefit 'Advanced Statistics' is a calendar — 12 value-gap reviews (2.58), 10 payers (22.7% of payers), three quoting the phrase back ('I bought this app bcs it stated advanced statistics for paid version. But I can not call these statistics even basic'); both payers who bought specifically for statistics were disappointed; F4: build it or delete the claim. Report 55: sync and export — the server-dependent parts of the premium bundle — are the two paid features reviewers most often report broken, while 'more habits' costs nothing to deliver. Report 76 (Way of Life): 11 reviews on cn in one week of 2015-01 report the app crashing immediately after buying premium ('钱扣了就开始闪退，无限闪退' — the money was taken and it started crashing, endlessly, 1★).

merged_from.title: Never take a paying user's reason to buy away — the widget sold the upgrade and never worked
merged_from.note: C220 (report 20's widget: the #1 named purchase trigger, non-functional for five years) is the strongest instance of C078, not a separate rule

title: Personal photos as habit icons
statement: Rare, loved, and no competitor in report 2's corpus offers it. Report 86 (Today): the strongest evidence in the series for a personal photo per habit — PR_DESIGN 460 (25.77%, the largest theme) with PR_PHOTOS 97 in a visual union of 523 (29.30%, 4.36★); reviewers treat it as the mechanism: 'I'm a very visual person, so the combination of large pictures and colourful calendars/graphs is great. I really feel motivated to tick things off, more than any other habit app'; 'It sets a craving, when I see the image, I want to accomplish the goal'; custom covers named as the one reason productivity improved most across 15 trackers; custom covers are a named purchase trigger ('I purchased the full thing just because to put my own photo covers'); PR_DESIGN holds at 15.25% even in the abandonment era — 'the app never stopped being beautiful. It stopped working'; §8.12 'copy: the full-screen personal photo per habit'; the costs: one page per habit does not scale ([[C254]]) and the image layer is blamed for slowness; a paid feature later taken away with users' existing covers ('you have to pay to use your own pictures and completely took everything i had on my profile off', 1★).

title: Colour themes / dark mode
statement: 'Only green' draws requests; cheap. Report 10: dark mode requested since 2022 as an accessibility need (migraine, light sensitivity). Report 20: dark mode moved from free-ish to paid in the 2021 conversion (89 reviews, mean 2.69) and was a named purchase trigger. Report 24: dark mode requested by 43, 58.1% of them 4–5★ — cheap and asked for by advocates. Report 29: dark mode absent — 15 requests (4.10%, mean 4.67, the highest-satisfaction request group), India 8.77% (2.9× global), 'it's what's missing for 5 stars'. Report 31: dark mode / themes 18; a German visually impaired reviewer: 'no accessibility features, no dark mode, no localisation … unusable'. Report 33: dark mode and themes were Premium in 2019–20; 48 request themes / colours. Report 43: per-habit colours / icons requested by 4 (mean 4.50); dark mode praised. Report 46: dark mode paywalled (2020, June 2024) — the report's #7 fix returns it to the free tier. Report 47: dark mode must keep every control legible — time-picker digits were unreadable in dark mode (2); more colours requested 3 (2019–20), later unlocked by watching a video. Report 48: dark mode requested by 11 (4.64). Report 50: colour coding, app-wide font, text size, dark mode, week-start day and per-habit units praised (customisation 25, 4.80); hex colours, longer habit titles, hide streak count requested. Report 52: dark mode requested (70, weak). Report 54: dark mode requested (5), once for light sensitivity. Report 55: dark mode shipped mid-2020 with 'black writing on the black background' (BUG_DARK 10, 1.90). Report 56: a dark / OLED design praised ('Cool OLED and Minimal Design'); dark mode (Feb) and light mode (Jul) requested five months apart. Report 57: dark mode Premium-gated (US) against a photosensitive user's accessibility need; white text on a white background with Premium themes. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_DARK (13) ends in 2021-10, consistent with a dark theme shipping; REQ_THEMES 70, REQ_ICON 20, REQ_FONT 21 continue. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): dark mode (2, both 2024–25; nobody since — verify whether it shipped). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_THEMES 54 (0.70%, 4.22★) across the whole span 2011 → 2026; themes shipped 2019-07 (Dark, Serenity, Retro C64, Light, Rose; PR_THEMES 14 at 4.86★) with some sold (MON_BUY_ITEMS 27, 16.48× among purchasers); 'this app keeps its dark mode theme locked behind a paid upgrade' (3★). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_DARKMODE 1 (5★).

title: Ads in the free tier
statement: A mild negative and a minor purchase reason in report 2; 'no ads' is the best-rated topic in report 1. Report 18: an interstitial ad on every check-off (Oct 2022) drew 17+ protests in weeks and was softened by December; the surviving minimal ads were tolerated. Report 25: six reviewers volunteer 'show me ads instead' of a paywall — ads-as-alternative is requested, not complained about; the app has none. Report 26: three teens independently ask for a rewarded-ad path to extra habits ('I will watch ads all day long if I have to') while 7 reviews (mean 5.00) praise having no ads. Report 27: 12 reviews (8.70%, mean 4.83) praise the absence of ads by name; an ad tier is 'contradicted by evidence'. Report 28 (the strongest counter-evidence in the set): an ad-supported free tier whose interstitial fires on every check-off is 19.98% of reviews at mean 2.73 vs 4.35 for the rest, 52.4% of all 1★, and rose from 3.5% (2021H2) to 39.6% (2024H2) before easing to 16.7%; three reports of non-dismissible ads and one of 'decline the rewarded ad, get a forced ad anyway' are store-guideline risks; an app rated 4+ with 40 reviews from or about children (ages 8–10 self-declared) serves untargeted network ads including AI homework-cheating and Temu wigs; 6 reviewers praise the ads as light and rewarded ads for carrots are accepted — the placement, not the existence, is the damage; the CN storefront (12 reviews, zero ad complaints) may be a natural ad-free control. Report 42: zero mentions of ads; upsell interstitials play the role ('the popups for premium are annoying and difficult to click out of'); one would rather see ads than pay €1.99/month (report 34). Report 47: the corpus is its own before-and-after on ad format — top-and-bottom banners were a mild theme (11, 1.87%, mean 3.55, 2019 – Apr 2024) whose reviewers mostly asked to pay to remove them; a video ad per check-in (May–Dec 2024) averaged 1.46 and generated exits ('1アクションに1回結構な長さのゲーム広告'; '元々入力するのに1分もかからないのに広告も1分じゃ'; 'an ad after every single entry is excessive… worse option than the notes app'); rewarded video for cosmetic colours (2022) was reported neutrally in a 14-vote 5★ — placement on the completion action, not ads as such, is what reviewers punish. Report 48: no ads in any era — 33 praise it, zero complain; two reviewers propose ads instead of the paywall, which the report reads as hostility to the cap rather than endorsement of ads. Report 52: the counter-case at scale — a nine-year Chinese tracker ran splash ads (2019–21, AD_NEG 3.4% / 2.8%) and in-flow ads from June 2025 (35.0% of reviews in six months, the lowest month in nine years); a ¥8 one-time ad-free SKU is accepted by those who find it ('but 8 yuan removes ads forever', 5★) and read as the motive for hostile ads by others; recovered to 5.8% in 2026 with complainants possibly churned. See [[C269]]. Report 64 (Critique AI): with no free tier, 12 (2.86%, mean 1.58) propose an ad-supported way in, one proposes an ad-supported base of a three-tier ladder; a 2★ defends the price as the alternative to 'annoying ads'. Report 76 (Way of Life): the free tier carried ads 2011 → ~2018 (NEG_ADS 54, mean 3.06★, 5.03% of 3★); removing them was the #3 purchase trigger ('Worth the upgrade to get rid of the ads', 4.6% of purchasers, 6.59× lift); ads gone from the free version by 2018 ('Now without ads even in free version', 5★) and NEG_ADS is 0.0% of E6; the price objection was highest while the free tier had ads (E2–E3) and fell after. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): no ads; the only ad mention asks for them as a paywall alternative — 'would like to have more freebies or maybe ads instead of the payment wall' (5★). Report 83 (Roubit): a free tier with ads that reviewers praise as generous (PRAISE_FREE_GENEROUS 14: 'literally gives you supportive letters every day FOR FREE'; PRAISE_NO_ADS 6) until 2026 put ads on open, on diary write and on past-day check-off — then ads became a stated churn reason; no reviewer says they paid to remove ads. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the no-ads, no-IAP counter-case — zero price or ad complaints in 86 reviews, all 23 price hits and 9 ad hits are praise.

title: Performance must not degrade with habit count
statement: 5+ second taps for the most engaged (paying) users; lag is a churn cause on its own. Report 30: above ~10 habits the list jumps back to the top after every tick and rows cannot be made denser — a defect that only paying users hit; fix it before raising the cap. Report 31: freeze / lag 404 (7.79%, mean 1.62) rising in every era to 26.6% of 2025–26 — '10 seconds for the sound effect, another 20 seconds for the colour to change'; '20-30 seconds per habit'; 'it now takes several seconds to add a single entry … can't cope with too many entries' (iPhone 15 Pro) — set a tap-to-register budget (<100 ms) and test with multi-year histories; some reviewers infer throttling of non-subscribers (untested). Report 42: lag scales with habit count ('the more goals you add the slower it gets'; hit at 15 habits) — 12 reviews (mean 2.58), 9 Brazilian, 4 payers — 'the users most affected are the ones who bought the app to have more than three habits'. Report 53: slowdown with many habits (24-vote jp review); the statistics crash tested against long histories and 20 habits. Report 56: the bottom menu bar blocks the habit list at 9+ habits — the scale 'unlimited habits' invites. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): UX_LIST_SCALE 2 (4.50★) — users with many boards find the single-page layout hard to manage; DEF_REORDER_BUG 1 after a drag-and-drop rework. Report 86 (Today): the sibling failure — latency growing with accumulated check-ins rather than habit count ([[C303]]); 'as my list of habits gets longer (and my dashboards get more complex), it gets very slow and the list gets very difficult to navigate' (za 3★); a performance fix in Mar/May 2020 was confirmed ('The latest update fixed the lag. I've dealt with that tedious issue every single day for months') and the complaint returned.

title: Address tracking / privacy visibly
statement: One unrebutted 1★: 'a whole lotta tracking going on by the developer'. Report 13: a 2017 privacy-policy revision drew 11 reviews in a month; location prompts with no stated purpose ('No, you don't need it') and disclosure-to-law-enforcement language made long-time users delete. Report 24: privacy / personal data complaints 138 (mean 1.225, 87.7% 1★) — a long questionnaire and web billing that collects card data before install. Report 27: a no-data-collection privacy label and no account are praised as features (4, mean 5.00); data monetisation is contradicted by the evidence and the listing. Report 29: 'I also appreciate that there's no subscription fees or ads. Am I trading off data privacy for this?' — users of free apps look for the hidden price; the listing's privacy label did not obviously cover the bandwidth-sharing prompt that followed. Report 34: on-device data with no account praised as privacy (7): 'my data isn't stored on a server!'; 'hasn't been larded with privacy-invading trackers'. Report 36: 'Does what it's meant to do while respecting your privacy and not harvesting your data'; 'the developers don't collect your data'. Report 41: 'This app doesn't hoard your data'; privacy / no account 10 reviews, all 5★. Report 43: 'Great data privacy (no data collected)' is enumerated among purchase reasons; 'I want to support the excellent privacy and pricing policies!' Report 46: 'Completely functional without paying! No ads!' (chronic pain); no ads praised by 10 (4.90); no account needed by 2024. Report 52: untranslated Chinese UI plus a precise-location request led a US reviewer to title the review 'Malware?? DO NOT INSTALL'; 'still using location after uninstall'; a dead privacy-policy link. Report 53: reviewers who read the privacy policy object to Facebook pixel and Firebase SDKs in a health-adjacent app; unexplained Apple ID prompts on launch (PRIV 7, 1.86); R8: publish and minimise third-party analytics. Report 55: premium required an e-mail account or the purchase was lost; cloud storage of goal data questioned; 'no login needed' praised. Report 56: no data collection named as the primary value by an ES reviewer ('No recopila datos') and corroborated by the listing; adding analytics to learn about churn would contradict it. Report 64 (Critique AI): 'don't put your email in this app' — two German reviewers independently, three months apart; refusal to give card or personal details before seeing the product; a photo demanded before the price; German reviews 28.6% scam and 14.3% privacy (n=14) vs 5.01% / 1.19% globally. Report 68 (Ultiself): PRIV_DATA 18 treat the stored card as the risk — 'must delete your credit card after'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'collects no personal data' named as a reason to trust (PR_PRIVACY 4); §8.9 keep no data collection. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a user objects that cloud backup contradicts the listing's on-device privacy claim. Report 75 (Habit Streak): zero privacy, sync, account or data-loss complaints, consistent with 'stored securely on your device—no sign-ups or cloud storage required'. Report 76 (Way of Life): the same local-only design draws PR_PRIVACY 12 (4.92★, 'Local data, no account') and BUG_DATA_LOSS 38 — privacy praise and data-loss complaints come from one decision; the answer is default backup, not an account. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): zero privacy or data-sharing mentions in 71 reviews across six languages. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 'PRIVATE BY DESIGN' is a headed section of the listing and 'Data Not Linked to You' the privacy label; PRAISE_NO_TRACKING 3, and three reviews volunteer privacy as the reason they chose the app; zero privacy complaints — 'Private by design is working'. Report 83 (Roubit): one tracking objection in 500 ('the app tracks you', 5★); the privacy label lists advertising and analytics uses and precise location; the diary — with crisis content — is sent to an AI and no review asks where it goes. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 'PRIVACY FOCUSED — No sign-in. No servers. No cloud.' is credited by two reviewers ('only anonymized data collection'; 'doesn't collect huge amounts of data') and questioned by none — but the privacy label lists analytics identifiers/usage/diagnostics, the policy is template text naming IP, approximate location, Amplitude and marketing, and the website offers cloud backup; §8.1 make the four sources agree: 'the risk is to a positioning that two reviewers already credit, not to a current complaint'. Report 86 (Today): the label declares no tracking; PR_PRIVACY 4, PR_NOADS 7, PR_SECURITY 3 vs PRIV_CONCERN 4; 'no ads, no account, on-device data — quiet assets that cost nothing and are named unprompted'.

title: Never imply cross-app integration you don't have
statement: Sibling apps raised expectations of integration; the purchases it drove ended in 1★.

title: No rating-prompt or cross-promo spam, especially to payers
statement: Small but consistent complaint.

title: Promos, giveaways and gift codes must work exactly as advertised
statement: Inflate early sentiment; when the promo fails to apply it produces 2–3★ from would-be buyers. Report 5's '1+1' gift code could not be used by the buyer and expired in three months — six years of disputes. Report 9: an advertised 3-month money-back guarantee was not honoured (17 reviews); withdrawing the claim zeroed those complaints and halved refund complaints. Report 26: China App Store shows a ¥38 tier with no in-app purchase path. Report 31: '83–90% off' first-year offers ($8.99–$9.99) checked out at $59.99–$99.99 through 2022–23, and a $19.99 'lifetime' was shown against anchors of $399–CA$499.99 that charged without unlocking. Report 34: the ~29 Jun 2023 free-lifetime giveaway left one reviewer calling it a 'Scam of free life time subscription' (1★) and another asking when the next limited-time free offer comes. Report 42: a promotional R$39.90/year shown, R$99.90 charged at confirm (1★, 'I'm waiting to adjust my rating of the app'). Report 43: a promo-free, ad-free one-time model produced zero unexpected charges, trial traps or chargebacks in 638 reviews. Report 46: a Black Friday €15 price; a December discount honoured after it expired ('Joan still hooked me up with the discounted subscription', 5★). Report 53: a splash screen offering ~90% off the annual plan while the App Store sheet shows the full price, in more than ten currencies ($7.99 → $79.99; €6.99 → €69.99; ¥900 → ¥9,000; 199 → 1,999 TRY) — PAY_PROMO 35 (mean 1.83), Jan 2023 → Feb 2026, 13 with no support reply and 9 asking for refunds; some reviewers did get it, suggesting eligibility rules; the most concentrated trust-destroying pattern in the corpus; F1: show the exact first charge and renewal on the offer screen and never show an offer the viewer can't redeem. Report 68 (Ultiself): a 2022 Sweatcoin promotion for lifetime access brought users who were then asked to pay. Report 76 (Way of Life): MON_SALE 3 (5.00★) — discounts are welcomed; 'only offer a reduced price in the first days after installation' (br 5★) is the complaint about timing. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): an AppAdvice free-lifetime promotion (2025-02-25) that could not be redeemed produced a 1★ (MON_PROMO_FAIL) from a user who also could not find directions; a competition-win giveaway produced a disclosed, neutral 5★ — 'a promo that fails is worse than no promo'. Report 82 (Lasting Change): 'you have the option to buy either the personalized book only… or, at a marginally higher [price], the book plus a 3-month-subscription' — a bundle priced so the subscription is effectively forced (ACQ_BOOK_PRICE_GATE 3: 'they hiked the price of the book if you don't buy a subscription'); a 'free month of membership' that 'will begin charging you monthly many months afterward'.

title: Destructive actions on widgets, quick surfaces and running routines need confirmation or undo
statement: An un-undoable reset button on a Home Screen widget destroyed streaks by mis-tap and read as 'a visual cue to break the streak' — a safety issue in a recovery app.

title: Regional pricing
statement: IN, TR, UA, BR, MX, SA reviewers name price as the only blocker; India likes the product and has not yet been asked a price it can accept. Report 23: price objection concentrates in au (5.7%), de (3.8%), ca (3.6%) against us 1.3%; China's number is ¥25–30. Report 25: price-display confusion is a Mexico-specific repeated issue — three reviewers cannot tell pesos from dollars, others name MXN 500, 40, 300, 599 and 299.99 — a pricing-display problem that is cheap to fix; Argentina's hostility (mean 2.95) warrants a look at its pricing display and trial mechanics. Report 33: regional price objections from Vietnam, Turkey (270 TL), Korea ('I'll buy if it's discounted') and Japan (¥19,000 lifetime, 'unfair to base your pricing on [exchange rates] alone'; 「前に比べて値段が爆上がり」) — regionalise lifetime pricing. Report 36: regional pricing complaints from Turkey and a cheaper local rival in India (₹499/yr vs Dayrise). Report 41: purchasing-power-adjusted lifetime tiers proposed for the 63 sub-50 storefronts, where cap complaints are 2.1× the high-volume markets. Report 46: regional price complaints 8 (all non-US — Turkey ₺179 / ₺30 a month, Saudi 109 SAR, Vietnam, Latin America, Israel cannot buy online, Kazakhstan) while Russia calls its price fair; the report's E2 is regional lifetime pricing. Report 48: China's lifetime objection is cost-of-living framed (a lifetime plan near a quarter of a second-hand iPhone); price sensitivity clusters in CA / AU / DE / CN. Report 49: Canada itemises CA$79.99 plus 14.99% Quebec tax; Türkiye objects to dollar-pegged pricing. Report 54: price objections 3.1× more frequent outside developed storefronts; D2: storefront-tiered pricing for CN/TW/PH/TR/BR/CO. Report 57: price objection 8.05% outside Korea vs 0.99% inside, Japan 26.92% — three reviewers on three continents independently propose a cheaper tier of ad removal + groups + backup (~¥2,000), one a monthly plan. Report 59 (Tappsk): the same lifetime unlock is named at 449 ₽ and 2,500 ₽ and at $14 / €4–10 within a year; regional prices could not be established from the corpus. Report 64 (Critique AI): M6 — price for the actual audience: an age- or region-tiered price as an experiment on a teen-heavy creator audience; volume markets ask for free rather than cheaper (20.0% vs 14.3%). Report 76 (Way of Life): China carries 82 of 306 price objections (26.8%); MON_PRICE is 15.5% of cn reviews (3.94×) and several name the price at which they would buy — '价格太贵了，要是12块我就买了' (at 12 yuan I would buy it, 5★); '30块也是最贵的' (at 30 yuan also the most expensive); East Asia group price objection 16.9% vs 7.5% global; the US sits at 4.8%. Report 86 (Today): a regional price visibly above the US price (CA$7 vs $4.99 at launch) produced Canada's 13.92% MON_FREE1 rate — the highest among eligible markets; US reviewers argue price in public ('just a cup of coffee?… come on people, app devs gotta make a living' vs 'In a market where most apps are $2.99 or less…').

title: No upsell nagging without a 'never ask again' option
statement: Full-screen interstitials, permanent banners and upsells before first value draw complaints even from 5★ users; a subscription launch with nagging cost ~3 points of 1–2★. Report 9: upsell-pressure complaints quintupled (2.16% → 4.84% → 10.23%) as the funnel was tuned harder, becoming the fastest-growing 1★ source. Report 14: the cleanest before/after in the set — rating-and-upsell pop-ups on every launch drew six star-docking reviews in nine weeks ('I docked one star for this'; 'Deleted'), and removing them produced unsolicited 5★ praise ('They removed the pop ups. Nice!!') and a named edge over a rival still 'begging for an upgrade within the first minute'. Report 18: a persistent bottom promo bar and a Dynamic Island discount countdown in 2025–26 were experienced as worse than the 2022 interstitial ads ('Absolutely the worst choice'); upgrade-nag was among the lowest-rated themes (40, mean 2.40★). Report 20: a 'limited time offer' countdown that reset to 60 hours on expiry ran for over four years (Jan 2021 → Mar 2025) beside a full-screen launch interstitial with a low-contrast dismiss — 225 reviews (5.56%, mean 1.80); 'Dark patterns make bad UX!'; 'first the consumer must see the value of the product. And what do you have? Every 2 seconds a subscribe banner.' Report 23: 4 reviews object to ads for the developer's other apps inside a paid app. Report 24: sister-app upsells (308, mean 1.932), referral/share prompts (131) and pop-ups/unskippable steps (182, mean 2.082) inside a paid subscription. Report 25: navigation-blocking upsell sheets — '10 popups in 20 seconds which kills the use'; 'not even my first second on the app 4 ads asking for payment'; a 5-second forced delay on the premium prompt; 'a habit app that starts right away with dark patterns' — 35 reviews (2.67%, mean 1.80); cap the prompt to one dismissible surface per session; a French reviewer notes explosive pop-ups are actively harmful for ADHD users in an app marketed to them. Report 28: forced interstitials on every action ('Ad while you write a habit. Ad while you review habits. Ad while you breathe.') and a rating prompt on open and check-off. Report 31: upsell nag 676 (13.04%, mean 1.72) rising 1.9% (E1) → 22.6% (E4) through a full-screen offer on every launch (2021), a permanent 'Just for you' list cell (2023) and two pop-ups per launch (2024, mean 1.47) — 'the only habit I'm developing is closing the upsell pop up'; a share of E4 purchases were made 'to get rid of the incessant pestering', and when relief did not arrive they produced the angriest reviews; E1 buyers valued 'that they don't prompt you to update every 3 clicks'; cap offers at one dismissible surface per week. Report 34: upgrade nagging 4 (mean 2.00) — 'constantly being nagged to upgrade to premium. I only track one thing'. Report 36: a full-page subscribe screen on every launch — POPUP 24 (mean 2.67), rising to 15.0% of 2026 H2, the only negative theme regularly in 5★ (4 of 24): 'i said no already, please respect that'; 'Can't use the app on my iPhone 13 mini because of a freaking pop up' (5★ titled 'Unusable'); the report calls a once-a-week cap the cheapest change available. Report 42: upsell interstitials 'annoying and difficult to click out of' (3, mean 1.67). Report 43 (counter-case): the in-app upsell is never complained about; the nag is the review prompt. Report 46: the upsell twin of the rating prompt — 'everytiime I try to add a new habit or move between screens the upgrade to premium screen appears and has to be x multiple times' (4, mean 1.50); a paywall on first open for some ('Take a subscription straight away or look at the start screen. That's all'). Report 47: upsell nag 4 (mean 1.25, Jul–Nov 2025) — 'タスクを完了するたびに毎回有料版の導入を進めるページに移るのがうっとうしいから消した' (a paid-version page after every completed task; deleted); the 2024 lesson did not carry over to 2025's upsell screens. Report 48: a full-screen / post-log upgrade prompt introduced around July 2024 drew 6 nag reviews in three months from long-term free users who say it reduced their willingness to pay ('I might even consider paying money for the app. But I darn sure will not… as long as the nag screen is still in place'); one records it being softened and raised their rating — 'the only monetization mechanic in the corpus that users say actively reduced their intent to pay'. Report 53: a 'new year, new me' premium pop-up with a countdown that 'never ends, it just starts over', shown every app open from 2023 (PAY_NAG 42, mean 1.93, 39 of 42 from 2023) — reviewers call the app's own offers 'ads'; M1: once a week at most, never to payers, no resetting countdown. Report 54: upgrade nag including after paying (5, 2.80); 'The paywall is so obtrusive' (GB). Report 55: a full-screen premium pop-up on every launch from July 2020 (PAY_NAG 44, 2.02; still reported Dec 2024) — 'Just ask once and don't make it pop up every time I launch the free app and it gets 5'; M5: one upsell, frequency-capped. See [[C274]]. Report 59 (Tappsk): MON_UPSELL 97 (0.64%, 3.33★) — 'Каждый день по 30 раз пихают мне всплывающее окошко «Купите нашу полную версию»' (thirty times a day the buy-our-full-version pop-up); Germany reports it at 2.36×, purchasers at 2.44×. Report 60 (Mindway): 'every 5 seconds it keeps brining up these Hey pay me now Pop Ups… let me do my activities and move on with my life' (1★); 'It keeps saying do you want a free trial for something'; 'it won't allow me make a plan without showing free trial vip' — an upsell that fires inside the task the user came to do; F5: stop firing the upsell inside an in-progress task — 'a description of a broken interaction, not of a pricing disagreement'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'Get one star for annoying me with pop-ups' (PL, 1★) — one review, a full star, 'a setting, not a build'; M5: cut in-session upsell pop-ups or cap their frequency. Report 67 (Habio): NEG_POPUP 19 ('I just wish it was voluntary'); a 2026 dashboard described as 'a mini Time Square Billboard showcase' of upsells. Report 69 (TheFor): 'Even better - there's no constant barrage of prompts asking you to upgrade!' — the restraint earns 5★. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'if you don't pay at least $10, most of your screen is taken up by a huge ad encouraging you to upgrade the app, and nearly every feature you click brings you back to this ad'; 'I just wish we didn't get an ad to buy premium every time we enter the app' (5★) — in an ad-free app 'the paywall is being experienced as the advertising'; §8.1 #2 take the full-screen upgrade prompt off every app entry. Report 76 (Way of Life): MON_UPSELL 13 (mean 2.85★). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): MON_PROMPT_NAG 1 (1★, title 'annoying'): 'can only add 1 habit then after that this subscription keeps popping up 😑'; §8.4.4 fix the prompt frequency — 'invisible in aggregate metrics until it shows up as churn'.

title: Ask for reviews well — tone converts; cadence and ignoring the OS opt-out backfire
statement: A charming review request produced dozens of reviews; frequent prompts that ignore the iOS opt-out, especially to payers, read as 'scammy'. Cross-promoting the developer's other apps inside the product draws the same complaint (report 2). Cross-promoting the developer's other apps inside the product draws the same complaint (report 2). Report 14: at least three reviews existed only because the app demanded one ('Happy now??'; a body reading 'Review'), polluting the ratings data. Report 20: a review prompt whose decline button read 'let the developers be sad' — 26 reviewers say it is why they wrote (inflating 2019's 5★ count) and two docked stars for the manipulation. Report 23: review-prompt nagging 25 (0.34%, mean 2.72, 40% 1★). Report 24: an in-app review prompt on day 1–3 makes the 5★ band (57.89%, median 105 characters) a first-impression measure — 'they asked me to review it now which I find kind of ridiculous'; the highest-voted reviews are all pre-2024 5★s. Report 25: an onboarding review prompt — 'Why won't it progress without me writing a review?'; 'in the middle of the onboarding questions the app interrupts me to ask me to rate' — pushed ≤25-character reviews from 7.2% to 33.4% of the corpus (150 of 196 5★ in 2026) and median body length from 156 to 53 characters; the all-records mean falls 0.27 while the substantive mean falls 0.73, and 1★ share (16.1% → 26.6%) is the only trustworthy trend line; 43 reviews (mean 4.21) are from people who say they have not used the app yet. A prompt at first launch buys a store rating and costs your own telemetry. Report 26: the app rewards a review with a cosmetic unlock and 13 reviewers say so ('I'm just doing this to get the backgrounds 😋 I haven't even used the app at all'; '(I'm NOT a bot btw)'); ≤25-character reviews rose from 16.5% to 35.0% of the corpus, 83–91% of them 5★; true inflation is unmeasurable and there is App Store policy exposure. Report 27: exactly one reviewer discloses a prompt ('Saw the message and had to rate'), no reward-for-review, and only 12 of 138 reviews are ≤25 characters — the substantive mean (4.594) equals the headline (4.645); a corpus of people who wrote something. Report 28: a rating prompt on open and on check-off shipped in 2026 (5 of 7 complaints are 2026) and already produced a 1★ 'until the rate me notification spam gets fixed'; 134 contentless 5★ records (median 38 chars) suggest the 2026 rating recovery is partly solicited; 'prompting into an ad-frustrated session is actively harvesting negative ratings'. Report 29: a rating prompt fired on the first check-off ('Used the app for 2 minutes then a reminder popped up for me to rate the app. -1 star'; 'so here I am, on day 1') — 39 contentless reviews, all 5★, median 27 characters; the 4.552 mean is partly a prompt-timing artefact that also starves the developer of diagnostic feedback; delay it to day 7 or ~10 completions. Report 30: 83 templated 5★ reviews and a near-absence of 2–3★ (7 of 166) consistent with a prompt routing satisfied users to the store; the public 4.4★ is a decaying artefact. Report 31: no review-prompt inflation — 20 prompt complaints (0.39%) and short reviews ≤7.7% of every era; about 1–2% of 5★ are complaints rated 5 'so people see it'. Report 33: in-app rating prompts 'three in 10 seconds' (Nov 2017 – Jan 2018) made review-nag complaints 3.8% of 2017 before falling to ≤1% every later year; 82 of 88 rating-contradicts-text reviews are 5★ reporting a bug or block; 820 short reviews (20.8%) inflate the positive side. Report 34: a rating prompt during setup ('you want me to rate it before I even finish setting it up'; 'App asks for 5 stars review'); the report recommends prompting after setup and after a 7-day streak. Report 41: 'it asks for a review every day which is needlessly annoying even if you've rated the app' (1★, Aug 2026); 111 of 815 (13.6%) contentless praise at a 69-character median — the signature of prompted reviews. Report 42: a rating prompt inside onboarding — 'Asking for a rating the first time I log in? How could I possibly know. But, since I'm being asked I must give it a one star' — the clearest causal chain to a 1★ in the corpus (2, both 1★). Report 43: the review prompt fires 'every time I open this app', 'every 2 minutes', and to people who already paid ('Paid $3, still kept asking for review. Annoying!') — 4 reviews, mean 2.75, plus a prompt whose Submit stays greyed out; 'a rating-acquisition mechanism actively lowering the rating'. Report 46: the largest self-inflicted problem in a 2,178-review corpus — an in-app rating prompt with no 'don't ask again' (50 complaints, mean 3.22, 10 one-stars; 'App asks me to review 4 times in 10 minutes. I haven't even setup 2 habits yet. Only option is Not now… Think twice before adding dark patterns'; 'you keep asking me for a review? → I'm punishing you'), asked during setup, of subscribers, and across platforms, 'fixed' in June 2023 yet live in August 2026; it capped 11 of 143 three-star ratings; the report's #1 fix: never in the first week, never twice per version, never after a rating or dismissal, never for subscribers. Report 47: rating prompt nag 3 (2023–26, mean 2.33) — a paying user asks it to stop 'せめて課金してる人に対してくらいは' ('at least for people who pay'). Report 48: review-prompt nag 9 (2.22); a prompt existed 2013–15 and ~2021; the prompt-driven share of 379 five-star low-information reviews is unknowable. Report 49: 1★ used as leverage — 'I am enjoying the app and will change the review once they fix it'. Report 50: the review prompt fires during onboarding alongside 'a page of positive reviews less than two minutes after I opened the app' — two 1★ reviews about nothing else ('I don't even star using this app and you ask me for a review'; 'participant reactivity bias plus peer pressure… Absolutely disgusting'); 27 of 142 five-stars ≤ 60 characters — fix F3: move it behind a streak milestone, which also stops inflating the corpus. Report 52: from 2020 a review prompt on the Nth launch ('第500次打开', '第3000次打开') — 40 mentions at 4.50; complaints when it fires before use and when it still insists after the user paid ¥8 to remove ads. Report 53: one jp reviewer nagged to review every time they open the app to log. Report 55: 'You have asked me 4 time within 1 minute to rate your app'; a lock screen and rating dialog that trapped a user (META_PROMPT 9, 2.44); R8: throttle the prompt. Report 58: no review prompt and a 3.30% contentless-praise rate — if a prompt is ever added, gate it behind a real usage milestone so the corpus keeps its value as a discovery instrument. Report 59 (Tappsk): a guilt-trip dismiss button — 'пусть разработчики грустят' (let the developers be sad) — is named in 2.04% of reviews (REV_SOLICITED 309, mean 4.77★, 1.6–2.5% of every era from 2020-01, coinciding with a 10× volume jump); most reviewers quote it fondly ('adorei a estratégia para deixarmos a avaliação'), but 12 of 309 are 1–2★ about the prompt itself ('это манипуляция эмоциями' — emotional manipulation; 'Хватит меня каждую секунду просить оставить отзыв'; 'Saudumme Formulierung') and it feeds distrust of the other reviews (REV_DISTRUST 32: 'начитались купленных отзывов'); the report's experiment: keep the prompt, change the dismiss wording, suppress it after a purchase, a crash or a support ticket. Report 60 (Mindway): a rating prompt fired on first session plus a paid acquisition push produced a 4-month burst — 98 of 216 (45.37%) in 2025-03/04, mean 4.12, 63 at 5★, from 32 storefronts, 52.76% of them content-free — that raised the mean 0.62 stars while adding almost no product evidence; when the push stopped, volume fell from 59 a month to 2 and the mean fell to 3.21, below launch level: 'the burst bought a rating, not a reputation, and it decayed the moment it stopped'; the modal 5★ is nine characters ('Love it') and only 37 of 128 5★ (28.91%) state a reason connected to using the product. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): three of 17 five-star reviews (17.6% of the band) do not endorse the product — 'App doesn't work', a pricing question, a critical entitlement bug — so the public 5★ count overstates satisfaction by roughly that much; seven low-information 5★ ('Good', '👍🏻', 'Excelente') are evenly spread. Report 64 (Critique AI): 11 contradicting reviews, ten at 5★, three explicitly using the star as a message about price ('im only doing 5 star just for you to take the payment subscription away'; 'I only gave 5 stars so you can see this'; 'i'm rating this 5 stars because i support your content bro but just please, please lower that price') — 39.8% of the 5★ band is not a product endorsement. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): an in-app 'rate this app' menu item and milestone-day reviews — the corpus agrees with the public rating (4.73 vs 4.78 on 53,106) and over-represents people for whom it worked. Report 71 (MyStreaks): no 3★ and no 2★ review exists (81.2% 5★), two US 5★ posted 38 seconds apart, an author handle 'Streaking User', a campaign-register review ending '#streakingforthewin' — consistent with in-app prompting after success moments and a founder community asking members to review; removing the 7 flagged reviews changes no headline band. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a 3★ whose entire content is that the app asked for a rating again the day after they rated — 'the review-prompt logic is directly manufacturing mediocre ratings'; §8.1 #5 never re-prompt a user who has rated. Report 76 (Way of Life): 20 days carry 20+ reviews (520, 6.70%, 86.15% 5★) after updates and in-app rating prompts, no campaign marks; the prompt draws resentment when mistimed — 'Quit bugging me with review me review me crap' (1★); 'app solicited a review 3 days in, after I paid for the premium version' (4★); §8.7 suppress the prompt for 30 days after a purchase or a crash-free launch following a failure; REV_SOLICITED 18 (4.06★). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): no burst or solicitation pattern detectable (largest day 2 reviews), though at n=71 'a detectable pattern is not the same as none existing'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): solicitation confirmed by the corpus — two reviewers describe the in-app prompt and both rated 1★ specifically because of it: 'I always leave one star reviews for apps that harass me with 'enjoying the app? Please leave a review' popups. It's gross. Change that behavior and I'll update this to 5 stars'; 'I keep getting the review prompt after every check in. Lowering to 1 stars until fixed' — 18.2% of the app's worst ratings from a growth mechanic; the 83.14% 5★ share is 'what a satisfied user gives when asked at a good moment'; §8.1.4 cap it once per user, never after a check-in, never after a user has already rated. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the star-only rating stream (673 raters, 3.838★) sits two stars above the written reviews in every major market and includes at least one 5★ that is a fraud warning — where and when stars are being asked for is the open question ([[C300]]). Report 83 (Roubit): an in-app 'review-writing mission' and invite-code reviews produced seven 5★ reviews with little product content (1.40%). Report 84 (HabitGrid): an in-app review prompt in every version since 1.0.1 (2025-07-03; 1.0.6 'Love the app? Now it's easier to leave a review') — 83 of 86 reviews postdate it, yet neither prompt release is followed by a rise in review rate; the rise follows localisation: 'the prompt alone does not explain the volume'. Report 85 (Habitica): a 1★ given in protest at a rating prompt (CONTRA_RATING); reviewers use the 5★ field as a contact form for bug reports (44 of 46 contradictions). Report 86 (Today): reviews used as a support desk (SUP_ASK 54) and a bug tracker (40 complaint-only 5★); RATING_LEVERAGE 16 withhold stars until a feature ships ('I'll be sure to change my rating to 5 stars when the updates come out!').

merged_from.title: No rating-prompt or cross-promo spam, especially to payers
merged_from.note: rating-prompt spam to payers was already the negative half of C094; cross-promo spam folded in

title: Neutral, non-judgemental tone on failure
statement: Reset without shame, no motivational pop-ups, keep history — the differentiation against apps that 'talk'. Report 23: a reminder framed as loss — 'You will lose your streak of X days if you don't do this today' — drew requests in four languages to reframe positively ('pedagogy from the early 20th century'); one string change per locale. Report 24: childish / condescending tone 304 (0.70%, mean 2.701); what paying users value includes that missing a day is not punished. Report 25: 'I clicked, paid £29.99 and I don't even know why. It's a list of aims for the day, I get to see all the things I haven't done and feel bad' — a checklist without a forgiving frame reads as guilt. Report 26: 'accountability and motivation without the shame' — gentleness, no streaks and a calm garden metaphor are the moat (25, mean 4.76; mental-health users 32, mean 4.66). Report 33: guilt copy backfires — 'Let's do better tomorrow, shall we?'; 'Yikes'; a Jan 2026 'Are you sure the day is over?' pop-up on fail/skip with no off switch ('infantilizing … Shipping annoying stuff without an off switch is a churn risk') — 43 reviews on unwanted or guilt notifications (mean 2.33). Report 36: 'As an easily discouraged perfectionist, I LOVE that if you miss a day (or a week) that it doesn't become the app of shame' (20 votes); the motivational text is 'encouraging but never guilt inducing' (13, all 5★). Report 46: 'not ticks to check off but areas that fill with beautiful colours — so I don't feel stressed about not managing something'; 'a triangle in that space… feels like neutral data instead of a personal failing'. Report 47: non-punitive framing praised — 'やったところが色が塗られるので加点方式な感じがして好き' ('what you did gets coloured in, so it feels like scoring points, not losing them'); the report: keep filled colour when a streak breaks, any missed-day marker optional. Report 48: non-punitive framing praised by 39 (0.89%, 4.90). Report 53: reminders phrased as questions — 'instead of stating what I'm supposed to do NOW, it asks questions — Have you walked today?' (REM_GOOD 67, 4.85). Report 55: quirky reminder messages liked by most ('I loved being called a tiger') but pet names drove churn ('Deleted when the reminder called me cutie'); R5: offer a neutral message tone. Report 68 (Ultiself): PR_GRACE 75 — 'doesn't make me feel bad when I mess up' — gentler than other trackers. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the jokey voice reads as shaming to some — 'the badge makes me feel blamed all day and weighs on me'; 'The cheerleading energy and jokiness give me goosebumps' — on an audience that includes depression and ADHD recovery.

title: Privacy and discretion stack
statement: Face ID / passcode lock, no account, discreet app name, alternate icons — zero negative reviews in report 3 and category-critical for recovery users on family phones. Report 33: privacy 23 reviews (mean 1.35) — the in-app help showed other customers' support conversations, e-mails and photos; goal-share URLs readable without login with no off switch; sync requiring Apple ID, Google account and e-mail; third-party analytics — audit support-conversation scoping and make sharing opt-in with unguessable, expiring links. Report 48: 25 reviews object to being forced to create an account and go online for a local tracker — a privacy objection distinct from price, strongest in Germany. Report 49: 20 frame the pre-paywall questionnaire as data collection (1.10) — one demands deletion. Report 52: a passcode lock that an ad dismissal bypasses (2025) — security-relevant despite being a single report. Report 56: no ads, no data collection, no account — 'Dots currently monetizes nothing', itself a differentiator and the credibility that makes a donation ask land. Report 76 (Way of Life): passcode / Touch ID / Face ID lock; PR_PRIVACY 12 ('local data, no account', 4.92★); a lock-out is a 1★. Report 86 (Today): the paid passcode / Touch ID / Face ID lock leaks the habit list — via the 3D Touch widget after force-close (ua 4★), on background resume ('no password is required to launch the app'), and for an instant before the fingerprint screen (jp) — three reports in three languages over three years; one reviewer objects on principle to paying for a lock.

title: A tip / donate option
statement: People asking to give money with no mechanism to do so. Report 8: in a completely free app, 7 users asked unprompted for a tip jar (all 5★) and 13 more volunteered to pay — mostly one-time, not subscription. Report 27: exactly two reviewers volunteer money unprompted — 'Keep the free app, consider adding a tip jar for users who are thankful'; 'it would be nice to donate to the dev since it's a free app' — both 5★, both framing payment as gratitude, both pairing it with staying free; with 10 developer-gratitude reviews (all 5★) a tip jar is the only monetisation the corpus positively endorses, and Canada is where the evidence says to start. Report 29: 'love to be able to contribute to use it' — a contribution offered in a free app, alongside a lifetime-purchase offer tied to a widget. Report 56: one unprompted donation request in 67 reviews of a fully free app; E1: an unobtrusive tip jar in Settings — no gating, no prompt, no nag — and watch for any negative review mentioning it. Report 58: a voluntary in-app tip is the only payment surface, received warmly ('there are no ads! But you can leave a tip, which is very nice ✨'), zero objections — unlikely to scale alone. Report 59 (Tappsk): MON_DONATE_WISH 18 — reviewers buy the lifetime unlock explicitly to support or thank the developer. Report 69 (TheFor): intent to buy framed as supporting the developer — 'I'm sure to support you, and I believe it's worth every Thai bath'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a patronage model — 'completely free; in-app purchase is only for people who want to support us' — with 39 framing payment as support and explicit asks for a repeatable small tip ('Please add a way to donate ¥100 at a time, as often as I like'; named thresholds ¥100–300, ¥500), a 'watch an ad' button as non-monetary support, and two buying the developer's book instead; a donation link named in 23 reviews was intermittent (not accepted in 2020); §8.7: a repeatable ¥100–300 tip or one-time pack beside the monthly plan. Report 71 (MyStreaks): a listed tip ladder — Friend $0.99, Ally $1.99, Advocate $2.99, Endorser $4.99 — beside Premium; no reviewer mentions any of it. Report 76 (Way of Life): a tip jar from 2018-11 — MON_TIP 15 (4.60★): 'jumped at the chance to tip the developers' (au 5★); 'supporting the developer' is a named purchase trigger in a corpus that thanks the developer by name (PR_DEV 268). Report 84 (HabitGrid): §8.4 — if revenue is needed, test an optional one-time purchase or tip for unshipped capabilities rather than gating the free core. Report 85 (Habitica): donations were an option 2015–2018 (MON_DONATE 2) and five reviewers ask for a donate button instead of add-ons — for an open-source, free-core product, patronage is the stated purchase motive.

title: Time-unit flexibility for counters (hours → years)
statement: What makes day 1 survivable for a quit-habit user; zero 1–2★. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_DATE_RANGE 22 (other time ranges for charts, 4.23★); REQ_ROLLING_VIEW 1.

title: Countdown / 'days until' mode
statement: Users want one app for count-up and count-down. Report 23: an end-date / countdown / long-term goal is requested by very happy users (17, 0.23%, mean 4.76, 0% 1★). Report 52: countdown / anniversaries among 'everything else' requests (395). Report 56: a deadline (time-bounded goal) requested once — kept out of scheduling as a different product. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_TIMER 5 (3.20★).

title: Money-saved counter
statement: Standard in quit-smoking apps; named as the one thing missing.

title: Milestones, achievements, celebration
statement: The largest positive-intent request in report 3 (2.21%, six years); shipped Aug 2026. Report 23: the gold-theme completion state — the whole screen turns gold when every task is done — is named by 80 5★ reviews; rewards, badges and milestones requested 136 times by happy users. Report 31: celebration on completion requested by 44 (mean 3.98), while achievements/trophies added in Apr 2023 were unwanted by long-time users. Report 46: the colour saturation itself is the reward — no badges needed; a gentler decay on a miss is asked for by 6 (mean 4.67) but must be tested against the neurodivergent segment. Report 50: badges / achievements requested (1). Report 57: a big confetti pop-up on check-off 'gives me ALL the dopamine' with no penalty for missing. Report 58: an ADHD reviewer asks for 'more of celebration for those who like dopamine hits' while 7 of 8 neurodivergent reviewers praise restraint — make it off-by-default and measure. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): reviews are written to mark milestones — streaks of 500 days, 1,000 days, a year or more; OUT_STREAK 617 (26.94%). Report 75 (Habit Streak): streak-milestone visuals requested (background changes at 7, 30, 60, 90 days, citing chess.com) — reinforces the Duolingo mental model users arrive with. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_GAMIFY 16 (rewards / achievements, 4.06★) and REQ_SCORE 4 — small against PR_CHAINS 129; the listing ships a scoreboard. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): Badges & Achievements shipped 2025-09-29 → 2025-11-02 and no reviewer mentions them; UX_NO_ACHIEVEMENT_FEEL 1 ('lacks to give you the feeling of achievement for completing the tasks') predates them.

title: Inverse / 'good habit' mode for a counter
statement: Recovery users want the number up; chore/ADHD users want it low — one counter, two mental models. Report 86 (Today): 'maximum N per period' as a habit type — five reviewers describe it; competitors Done and HabitBull are named as having it.

title: Vulnerable users — recovery, mental-health and minors — are a sensitive surface
statement: Alcohol, nicotine, self-harm (incl. minors), drugs, EDs, no-contact; monetisation moves land as 'preying on the vulnerable'; age rating is load-bearing. In report 4: 455 kid/teen reviews who cannot pay, and 89 shame / diet-framing reviews in a 4+ app. Report 24: a product marketed to people with executive dysfunction and low income priced as a premium wellness subscription; diet-culture / eating-disorder trigger complaints (61, mean 2.918); depression/anxiety users are 2.89% of the corpus. Report 26: users describing severe depression, being bedbound, three years clean and wartime anxiety ('This app helped me return to life') — the gentle, non-punitive frame is what serves them; children as young as 10 review the app. Report 28: an app rated 4+ with 40 reviews (4.87%) from or about children — 'I'm ten'; 'im nine'; 'I am a 8 years old' — serves untargeted network ads (AI homework-cheating apps, Temu wigs) and a 'watch an ad to double carrots' prompt; a brand and compliance exposure independent of the rating damage. Report 29: 'You're doing a great service to students who cannot afford to spend on applications' — free access matters to students; 4 student/budget reviews at mean 5.00. Report 31: sobriety, medication and mood-disorder trackers were hit by streak resets, removed quit-to-zero goals and upsells interrupting tracking. Report 49: the acquired audience is young and emotionally timed — 12 minors, 'I saw it on insta at 2am and got the 2am motivation to change my life so now I have a year of this app', buyers 'at the lowest point in life' or in severe depression; mental-health-benefit reviews carry the taxonomy's highest mean (4.94). Report 64 (Critique AI): the creator audience is young — 20 reviews (4.77%, mean 1.90) are minors or argue for them (ages 12–15 self-stated; 'everyone on it seems to be like 12-15 years old'), 13 of 20 in the US; a ~$40/yr annual-upfront plan needs a payment instrument they do not control; a parent bought it for a 12-year-old and asked for a refund; the most-upvoted review (9 votes) asks for an adult tier and a free teen tier; research: what share of installs are under 13 — 'a compliance question as much as a pricing one'. Report 65 (Rabit): medication adherence ('não estou mais esquecendo de tomar meus remédios') and depression ('m'aide à surmonter ma dépression seulement je ne reçois aucunes notifications') — for these users a reminder failure is not an inconvenience. Report 67 (Habio): USE_ACCESS 18 name vulnerability (disability, low income, student, mental-health crisis) and USE_MENTAL 40 — 'Shame on the developers for scamming people, like me, who are trying to work on their mental health' (the most-voted review, 16 votes). Report 68 (Ultiself): 'my first week of white knuckling sobriety, I found an ad for this app'; 'Instead of helping me to quit drinking it's making me feel like drinking even more' (OUT_HARM 2) — an addiction ad that sells a generic tracker to someone in early recovery. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): depression, ADHD, anxiety, autonomic disorders and binge eating named with recovery stories (USE_WELLBEING 25, 4.92: 'My depression has eased and I've been able to return to work'; 'day 15 since the stress-driven late-night binge eating I'd suffered for about eight years stopped') — the reason a quiet mode matters. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): medication adherence (5) — a dose titrated every two weeks tracked as 20 / 40 / 100 mg rows ('I've safely reached and held the final dose') — makes the tracker 'a clinical-adjacent record'; locking it behind a paywall is 'a materially different act from locking a feature'. Report 76 (Way of Life): USE_ADDICTION 46 (4.96★, 'Today marks 1 month clean'), USE_MENTAL 27, USE_ADHD 23 — the sobriety and mental-health cohorts rate highest in a 4.62★ corpus. Report 82 (Lasting Change): a mental-wellness-framed product (mood and stress check-ins, meditations, 'Contains Health or Wellness Topics', 'Data Linked to You: Health & Fitness') whose users report sobriety and productivity outcomes (OUT_WELLBEING 7 at 4.71★; 'haven't had alcohol for over 60 days') and whose billing is the most-complained-about in the series; one PRIV_CONCERN. Report 83 (Roubit): U:mental_health_any 68 (13.60%, mean 4.84★) — the highest-rated cohort; two suicidal-crisis disclosures credited to the app; a diary sent to an AI with an advertising-and-analytics privacy label and no review asking where the text goes; minors present (SEG_STUDENT_MINOR 13). Report 85 (Habitica): the mental-health cohort (USE_ADHD 71, USE_MENTAL 51) is both the most enthusiastic and the most exposed — a guild used as a support group was removed in 2023, and a punishment mechanic drove a struggling user out for three years; therapists recommend it to clients. Report 86 (Today): 'I started using this app to get a better grip on my depressive phases, and to sort days when I felt bad out of the streak' (de 5★) — a skip/forgiving state as a mental-health tool; accessibility is an evidence gap (2 mentions in 1,785; text over photos has obvious contrast risk, reported in 2016).

title: Never ship a paywall or feature-removal change silently
statement: Undisclosed changes and 'it was a bug' replies that don't match what users see destroy trust for a year. Report 11: the store description still discloses no paywall at all (0 mentions of premium/subscription/free/unlock) after the retrofit; a grandfathering rule for pre-2026 users is the recommended fix. Report 20: the Feb 2021 restoration was never announced — '4 stars after premium was restored, but not 5 because the devs ignored us for so long and have not acknowledged the issue' — and the March 2025 wipe drew 'no communication whatever about this disaster.' Report 29: the bandwidth-sharing prompt arrived with no announcement; the report's first fix is 'decide and publicly disclose the web-indexing policy'. Report 30: the 2 → 3 cap change shipped without the listing being updated. Report 31: monthly/yearly frequency, streak display, swipe, quit-to-zero, Shortcuts, the tappable widget, 'last done' and day-start time were removed across v2 (Mar 2022) and v3.0 (27 Jan 2023) — feature removal 9.4% of E4, an update blamed for a regression 8.4%; the legacy Premium stopped being recognised in Apr 2023 with no notice. Report 33: Habitify X (~27 Aug 2020) removed time logs, yearly stats, CSV export, swipe, 'N per week', Shortcuts and the Watch app with 'no migration path' — 149 reviews in nine weeks, 42 UPDATE-. Report 36: the Oct 2023 widget gate was read as a bug for months ('the widget app has not been working properly … says that I have to unlock it') and the 2026 cap as 'extremely bugged. I cannot add a second habit'. Report 43: 'pause a habit' vanished in the 2026 update (2★) and 'every 2/3 weeks' schedules silently became weekly after the redesign (4★). Report 46: dark mode 'moved behind a paywall' in a June 2024 update ('Immediate deletion'). Report 47: the May 2024 changes arrived unannounced and the word reviewers use is 改悪 ('made worse', 23 reviews at mean 1.39); the listing still says 'unlimited task registration' while reviewers report a cap of 6 — the report cannot resolve which is current. Report 48: the 2015 conversion was announced as grandfathering prior purchasers and 14 say it was not honoured ('bait and switch', 'SCAM', 'Rent what you've paid for'); the cap reductions of 2018–20 arrived unannounced and were discovered by users deleting a tracker and finding the slot gone (23, mean 2.22).
