Report 27: streak length is not readable from the day list (a full interaction spec given); a goal end date and archiving are on the listing and a reviewer could not find them; a streak freeze is listed and zero reviewers mention it; the website link in Settings points at a dead domain — the only support path. Report 28: an in-app 'Restore purchases' and 'Contact support' entry point is missing — four purchase failures and two 'where do I get help' reviews, while the developer answers e-mail within hours. Report 30: edit / delete / pause exist and three reviewers in three countries could not find them ('how do you pause a habit? how do you edit? I've looked everywhere'), one rating 1★ — a discoverability defect, not a missing feature. Report 31: misunderstandings about how to edit or delete a habit, what 'untracked' means, what colours and X/O marks mean and how 'quit' goals count — a UX problem, not a gap. Report 33: misunderstandings rise with feature count — a time-of-day filter hid habits and produced a false bug report; how to reorder or delete; skip vs cancel vs fail; 'every day starts skipped' (a setting); where the timer is; how to connect the Watch. Report 34: 'No widgets!!' two months after widgets shipped, and a request for an easier way to mark yesterday answered by the existing long-press ('That solves 90% of the struggle'). Report 43: roughly a tenth of scheduling complaints ask for shapes the app already has (custom days 'Monday and Wednesday's', timed tasks, untimed tasks) and land as 1★ / 2★; a Mac app is requested although the listing claims Mac. Report 47: the start date before creation exists but is hidden behind blank picker options — the second-largest request in the corpus (21) is a discoverability fix. Report 56: 'a feature-discoverability problem, not a feature-absence problem' — reminders requested twice after shipping (buried in the habit editor; v2.3.2 added a bell icon on every row), back-dating hard to find, widget transparency in the store preview but not findable — 'Shipping a feature is not the same as retiring its request'. Report 57: an AI habit-suggestion feature shipped in 2025 and both reviewers who mention it cannot find it; a Shortcuts 'Check-in ID' exists undocumented. Report 59 (Tappsk): NEG_UI_CONFUSING 152 (1.00%, rising to 1.4% in the latest era) — cannot find how to delete a habit or set a reminder on a habit ('не могу понять как удалить ненужную привычку'). Report 65 (Rabit): CONF_UX 12 (2.41%, mean 3.50) cannot find a control or how to mark a habit done; the timer is hard to find. Report 69 (TheFor): 'I am struggling to find the section of exploring popular routines' (4★). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): a 2026-07-05 review asks for 'cloud sync, so data can be backed up and synchronized across devices' — iCloud sync has shipped since at least 2024-10-14, is praised by three reviewers and is a headed section of the description; an archive/restore feature (v2.3.0) is likewise unknown to a user asking for lost boards back. Report 84 (HabitGrid): MISUNDERSTAND_EXISTING 2 — a 4★ warns 'all your data will be deleted if you change your phone' while the listing advertises 'IMPORT AND EXPORT… restore it at any time' and zero reviews mention it; another asks for widgets five months after they were praised; 'discoverability problems, not missing features'; §8.3 surface export in onboarding and settings before building accounts — 'the cheapest change that answers both reviews'. Report 86 (Today): Restore Purchases exists in Settings and reviewers who lost premium on reinstall never found it (MON_RESTORE 18); statistics live in the profile screen and were found 'by accident' (UX_CONFUSE 74); a skip feature exists and 'nobody understands it' — 'fixing the explanation may be worth more than building anything'.

title: Intra-day completion: tap N times to fill N/N
statement: When a habit's target is more than once a day, each tap should count toward it; one binary tick per day is report 8's #1 unmet need, the only complaint theme still rising, and a stated uninstall. Report 20: multiple check-ins per day (water, medication, teeth) was requested 54 times (mean 3.87) and named as table stakes against Streaks and Productive; never shipped. Report 23: multiple-per-day / partial increments (111, 1.53%) largely shipped in 2016; residual complaints are about partial-progress display. Report 26: multi-count per day (5 glasses of water, 10 pages) requested by 7. Report 27: multiple completions per day shipped ~Aug 2025 and is praised ('the multiple check-ins per day feature is very handy'). Report 29: 'As someone who takes medication twice a day it would be incredibly helpful to mark the same habit done twice a day'. Report 33: multiple completions per day / quantities (water ×8, pills ×3) was the largest 2017–19 request (53, 50 before Aug 2020) and shipping multi-check-in goals in Habitify X retired it (2.9% of E1 → 0.1% of E5). Report 36: multiple completions per day requested by 5. Report 41: countable goals with over-achievement and partial credit ('if a habit needs a count of seven… and you have only performed it four times, you get credit for that'). Report 42: multiple completions per day for water, meals and reps do not exist — 6 reviews (all US, 13.0% of US, mean 1.50), two refund-seeking payers: 'Track your food? Great - you can track it ONCE/day'; 'So you're going to eat or drink water just once a day?' — the marketing promises a counter, the product delivers a daily checkbox. Report 43: 0/2 and 0/4 per-day counters with hourly nagging exist and sell the app. Report 46: several completions per day requested by 12. Report 52: multiple check-ins per day (237 — water × 8, meds morning and evening) and multi-check habits that force a detail sheet even with one-tap enabled. Report 53: brush teeth twice, meditate in two sessions (CORE_MULTI 12). Report 55: the same habit several times a day (CORE_MULTI 5). Report 57: multiple check-ins per day requested from 2019 ('stamping three or four times a day, like for medication'), shipped as 'goal', capped at 5 ('I need 10'), then tier-gated — producing the three angriest change complaints (24 requests). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): within-day granularity is the largest coherent feature gap — 4 of 45 (8.89%) from four storefronts over eight months: count a habit N times a day and sum at day end, more than one reminder a day ('One reminder a day is not enough' for water and steps), a value per day ('walked 5k, then 7k'); two described use cases (water, steps) are currently unserviceable; P1 in the roadmap. Report 65 (Rabit): a times-per-day option that cannot be partially completed — 'tenho que tomar vitamina 2x ao dia, porém não consigo marcar caso eu tenho tomado apenas 1x. É tudo ou nada'; 'i'm not really sure what it is supposed to be used for' (S4). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): duration targets with partial completion — 'if your goal is 120 min, you can tick 20 min of it' — praised. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_COUNT 129 includes 'several times a day'; the yes/no/skip cell cannot hold a count. Report 83 (Roubit): '하루에 프랭크 10회 하기라면' (if it's 10 planks a day) — count-based routines requested (REQ_FLEX_SCHEDULE 10).

title: Habits, focus timer and journal in one simple app
statement: Report 8's 3-in-1 bundle is load-bearing: none of the three parts draws a 1–2★, and users value not switching between three apps — as long as each part stays minimal. Report 49: a bundle of screen blocker ('a godsend… the typical screen time limit apple has… doesn't cut it' — no detractors), Pomodoro, workout and calorie trackers, journal, meditation and book summaries (22 + 23 praise) around the habit core. Report 50: all-in-one praised by 17 (4.94) — habits + tasks + schedule with time blocks + journal + mood + weight in one place. Report 83 (Roubit): routines, to-dos, goals, D-day, diary with mood, quotes and an AI letter in one app — PRAISE_ALL_IN_ONE 23 (4.60%): 'deleted separate to-do, goal and diary apps'; the cost is FEATURE_BLOAT 3 and a long onboarding. Report 86 (Today): per-habit 'cards' (counters, custom charts, milestones, journal, photo gallery, Apple Health metrics, a stress card) — PR_CARDS 70 (4.69★), U:depth_differentiator 192 (10.76%, 4.72★): 'the deciding factor was the extensibility of supplementary information via cards' (jp, paid); ''lead indicators' like calories consumed beside 'lag indicators' like your weight'; 'I use it as sort of a memory box for things I've done'; a named purchase trigger ('little motivation boards was what made me pay'); and NEG_FEATURE_UNUSED 15 (2.80★: 'cards that are unusable in 95% cases') with UX_CONFUSE 74 — 'the cards are simultaneously the reason power users pay and a source of confusion for everyone else'; §8.13 measure card usage against 90-day retention.

title: Every promotional or onboarding modal must be dismissible on the smallest screen
statement: Report 8's full-screen 'add a widget' prompt had an unreachable close button on small iPhones and blocked the app for 20 months. Report 24: pop-ups and unskippable steps (182, mean 2.082) and unskippable completion celebrations; make animations skippable. Report 31: a 'Self-care Christmas' banner hid the bottom habit; a permanent 'Just for you' list cell slowed scrolling and tapping — never let a promotional element occupy a habit row or slow the list. Report 33: a full-screen offer on every open and a banner covering the third habit that cannot be closed (2023–26; upsell 1.7% of E5). Report 55: see [[C274]] — a pop-up whose X started a purchase. Report 64 (Critique AI): a paywall that reads as uncloseable — PAY_SOFTLOCK 39 (9.31%, mean 1.72) across 20 storefronts and 17 months ('no cancel button, no ignore button, no X button. NOTHING!'; 'I cannot press the don't pay now button even if I press it 20 times'; returns after relaunch) — reconciled by one German reviewer: the X 'is invisible, tiny and impossible to find'; two trapped users rated 4★ while asking for help; the rate fell 16.9% → 6.8% after launch but 7 reports remain in the latest quarter; F1: large, visible, reachable on first paint, verified on small screens and after force-relaunch. Report 64 (Critique AI): 'Doesnt work on smaller phones' and 'I can't scroll in the app, which means I can't choose the correct options' — defects that exclude rather than annoy (R7). Report 65 (Rabit): the onboarding questionnaire's advance button rendered below the visible screen (2023–2024) — 'a layout bug, not a logic bug, and trivially fixable' (F6); an ad close button under the status bar on iPhone 13.

title: Harden onboarding before January
statement: The New Year cohort is the largest of the year, writes reviews in its first days, and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day logging defect is amplified about 2× in January (report 8).

title: Let people use the product before they pay
statement: Users forgive a price; they do not forgive paying blind. Report 9's hard paywall before any experience produced 159 'let me look before you charge me' reviews at mean 1.79, and buyers who paid before seeing the product became the angriest cohort (mean 1.94). Report 12: a hard paywall with nothing evaluable produced a paywall corpus — 46.5% of 404 reviews complain about the gate, 172 reviewers left without ever seeing the product, and the theme never dropped below a third of reviews in any year. Report 17: seven reviewers rated an app they never saw ('Can't even look at the settings or examine how the app will handle cancelation'); confirmed payers averaged 3.63 against 1.14 for those blocked at the paywall — the strongest argument in a 38-review corpus for letting people in. Report 18: the reviews that converted best came from people who used the app free for a week or a month first; the reviews that generated refund demands came from people charged before they could evaluate. Report 19: only four non-payers appear in the corpus and all four refused for the same reason — no way to evaluate first; everyone else went through the paywall and then tried to reverse the transaction. Report 25: 'I could not evaluate the product' outweighs 'too expensive' — ~31 of 55 price objections are gate objections; every positive trial review describes having had enough product access to form a judgement; a survey-then-paywall sequence is the lowest-mean theme in the corpus (1.17) because it spends the highest-intent moment and then gates it. Report 26: an evaluation-window problem, not a pricing problem — 'You get about 5 days free to make one flower then you have to pay'; 'the flower stops growing once you reach 17%, which I finished in about 2 weeks'; a user writes the hypothesis: give one garden free 'and that would probably get me intrigued enough to get a subscription'; proposed tests: time-boxed full access, cap 8–10, or one garden to 100%. Report 30: 'nobody forms a habit portfolio of two — the cap converts evaluation into rejection'; the cap, not price, is the top upgrade barrier (15), and the substantive rating of everyone with something specific to say is 2.87. Report 31: 'Free is useless, paid is too expensive to try' — the evaluation argument is the plurality monetisation objection since 2016; 'Tried the 3 free habits and wanted more' was an E1 purchase trigger when the unlock was a $4–9 one-off. Report 33: 'Three habits, and three days, is simply too little'; the evaluation argument is the plurality of monetisation objections; 44 say 'would buy if…'. Report 34: 'two habits is too few to judge the app' is the plurality of 78 monetisation-friction reviews; a 2-habit tier converts believers and repels evaluators. Report 36: a 1-habit free tier 'you can't really test the app without paying'; roughly half of 121 friction reviews are willingness to pay the model cannot accept. Report 41: purchase decisions in hours on a 3-habit free tier ('I bought the lifetime after trying it for like 20 minutes'), while others say 'you can't get a proper demo out of this without having at least 8 or 10 habits'. Report 42: 'you can't get… a test to see whether it's actually worth paying'; a migrating HabitBull power user lost at the wall ('I couldn't move around or familiarize myself enough to justify paying to unlock integral features'); 'every tab I open to poke around is locked'; the 1★ band's 'never used the product' population (~20) needs a trial, the 'paid and regret it' population (13) needs the product to be worth it. Report 43: 'Why not give 2 weeks fully functional, then handicap it to 3?'; 'Would have more stars if I cd test out >3 goals — Prior to paying!' Report 46: 'By the time you discover that you can only track 3 habits with the free version, you've already spent 20 minutes or more setting it up' (16 votes); 'every tab I open to poke around is locked'-style evaluation failures; a 30-day full trial asked for. Report 48: 43 state an intention to pay that the current terms defeat (4.12) — 'I will pay for an app after I use it for a couple weeks and have grown to appreciate the app'; 38 payers describe long free use before paying. Report 50: three of four intent-to-pay reviewers use the free tier first, and two actual payers state the sequence (months free, then pro) — the path a cap cut interferes with. Report 53: 'I was asked to pay too soon, without really trying the app'; 'Let me try before upselling'. Report 54: the strongest conversion stories got enough free room to be convinced — two weeks, one week, a few minutes with the whole feature set visible — while the cap 'terminates evaluation rather than gating it'. Report 56: free-trial-then-charge patterns at competitors are explicitly rejected — 'No obnoxious free-trial trick. Actually free'; 'really free, no false promises'. Report 57: new users who hit the creation ad 'stop using the app before finding out if you like the functionality'. Report 59 (Tappsk): 40 purchasers bought within days because the app worked in the first days ('Поюзал один день и купил навсегда' — used it one day and bought forever; 'took premium the same day I downloaded it'). Report 60 (Mindway): 'the decision the corpus forces' — move the paywall behind first value: the value users report (structure 15, habit outcomes 12, wellbeing 9, mean 4.79) takes days to appear and the current design charges before any of it can happen (ad → questionnaire → 'asked for money right away'); the three reviewers who met the cost as optional averaged 4.33★, the thirteen who met it as a wall 1.69★ — 'how the cost is encountered, not the cost itself, determines the rating'; every one of the 13 confirmed payers wrote a negative review; E1: raise the free cap to a full day's routine (8–10 tasks) for a randomized cohort; E2: replace the count-based paywall with a time-based one — full app, 7 days, no card ('I wish it would of let me try it out first'). Report 64 (Critique AI): the purest case in the ledger — no free tier, 0 of 419 report free ongoing use; 166 (39.62%, mean 1.52) blocked at the paywall; 82.58% never got in (mean 2.35) against 3.87 for those who did (+1.52 stars); 95 (22.67%) propose a way in (free tier 66, trial 26, tiers 21, ads 12); strip out money and 126 reviews remain at 4.41; the 3★ band is 'I want to buy this and cannot' (PAY_PRICE 45.7%, PAY_SCAM zero) — 'If a free or cheaper tier ships, this band converts first'; M3: tracking + XP / leaderboard free, AI analysis, focus mode and coach paid; 'Nobody defends the price from outside the paywall — which is the whole argument for a free tier in one sentence'. Report 67 (Habio): the E2 objection was paying blind — 'I'd love an opportunity to try before I buy!'; MON_HARDWALL 47; the free era E1 averaged 3.03 with 53.42% praise against 1.73 once the wall arrived; §8.8: a real free tier or card-free trial, measuring chargebacks and refund requests rather than only conversion. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): no trial exists anywhere in the corpus and a one-habit free tier cannot demonstrate the product — 'перевірити додаток без покупки було не можливо' ('it was impossible to check the app without buying'); that reviewer bought blind, disliked it, was refused a refund and left 2★; E2: a time-limited full-feature trial measured on refund rate and D7 retention. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): the trial is survivable when disclosed and the product lands — five 5★ met it and converted or shrugged ('I was using it without realising you have to pay after a week — but it was so good I paid'); several bought immediately (「即購入」) — 'the buyers were never the ones who needed persuading over a week'. Report 75 (Habit Streak): the 'everything is paid' reactions (4, mean 2.50: 'Pretty useless unless you pay money'; deleted after ten minutes, titled 'Tư bản' — Capitalist) come from users who bounced within minutes although the free tier permits five habits — the cap 'is hit at setup, before value is felt'; hypothesis: 'the people most likely to pay are the ones who got value free first'; E2: enforce the cap at day 14 rather than at setup. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'only by buying will you know if you need it' (ua 2★); 'This is not a Free app with in-app purchases. This is a $7 app' (1★); REQ_TRIAL 4 at mean 1.75★; §8.9 Q4 asks whether the 3-item tier converts better or worse than a time-limited full trial. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'you can't really explore the app' (bg 4★) — 'a habit tracker with one habit is a demo'; the three who converted did so on comparative value after using it; zero of 71 mention a trial and the description offers none; §8.4.3 a trial or an unambiguous free window. Report 82 (Lasting Change): no free tier exists in the corpus (zero mentions of a free tier or habit limit); 'Continued access to all features requires a subscription'; APP_UNUSED 14 were billed for an app they never opened; the only deliberate buyer converted 'just in case' on fear of a later price, 'not on value', then preferred a paper bullet journal. Report 86 (Today): 'unable to evaluate it with only one card… this should be listed as a paid app not free' (1★, 2016); the paid value (multi-habit dashboards, cards) is invisible at a one-habit cap; §8.9 caveat: the 1★ at a one-habit cap come disproportionately from people who never used the app — removing the cap 'may raise the rating without raising revenue', so test with revenue as the metric.

title: The paid product must deliver what the ads and onboarding demonstrate
statement: Report 9 showed an interactive guided-breathing coach in its ads and onboarding, then never offered it again — 'it's just a checklist' became the worst-rated major theme (99 reviews, mean 1.45), half of them from payers. Report 19: five reviewers paid for a personalised plan promised by a quiz and received a blank tracker plus four thin sister apps ('some useless little apps'); a Spanish-language Instagram ad delivered an English-only app; 'not as advertised' ran at 18.10%. Report 24: acquisition ads and a web questionnaire promise personalisation the plan does not deliver — 'the app asked very few questions and made very many assumptions before designing a plan for me'. Report 41: a buyer paid for the Home Screen widget shown in the listing screenshots while it was 'coming soon' (2★); another: 'no widgets… which was the entire reason I bought it. The preview looks nothing like the app this is a scam'. Report 42: a 'goal for the day' shown in marketing could not be found (1). Report 49: Solo Leveling ads promise an avatar, quests and penalties — 15 'not what the ad promised' (1.40) and 38 'just a checklist' (1.68) vs 38 who love the framing (4.87); an Instagram ad said 'get your free life reset plan today' (advertised free 37, 1.08) — 'the fix is in the ad, not the app'. Report 64 (Critique AI): '$50… expecting actual coaching' — 'all it does is organize workouts I had already organized myself'; 'Temu quality'; an AI that 'points out what's supposedly wrong with you without offering any solutions' (R3: give the AI something to say after the critique). Report 67 (Habio): U_AD_MISMATCH 195 (9.51%, mean 1.08) — Instagram ads showing a 'bionic' bold-first-letter reading tool for ADHD that does not exist (22: 'What a bait and switch!!'), a quiz promising a Myers-Briggs / ADHD profile or tailored plan ('Nothing like that exists in the app', 31), and ads that did not match the product (99); §8.5: withdraw creative for features that do not ship. Report 68 (Ultiself): addiction-themed Instagram / Facebook ads (drinking, smoking, vaping) leading to a general habit checklist — USE_ADDICTION 24, 23 in E6: 'This app advertises itself as a personalised program to help you reduce your drinking- it does nothing of the sort'; 'there was nothing about vaping'; a paid 'personal plan' never delivered ('No actual plan is provided'; MON_NOT_DELIVERED 17); NEG_NOT_AS_ADVERTISED 59; §8.5: addiction ads should lead to a product that addresses the addiction, or not run. Report 82 (Lasting Change): APP_NOT_AS_ADVERTISED 3 — the ads showed free-form habit tracking the app does not deliver; 'Won't let me post photos or upload a profile picture'; notes and photos 'give me an unsupported notification'; 'Experiments don't work and reset daily'.

title: Respect Reduce Motion — no rapid flashing animation
statement: A self-care app's fast animation was reported as a seizure/vertigo risk (report 9, promoted as a safety finding despite one review).

title: Never ask for a rating before the user has used the app
statement: Report 9 put the rating prompt inside sign-up: users were asked for 5★ before seeing the app, the public rating ran 1.35 stars above written reviews, and Apple's guidelines forbid it. Report 12: an in-app instruction to rate 5★ during onboarding — 'It said I had to give them 5 starts so here I am' — was called out by 23 reviewers, two of whom named the exact 4.8 store aggregate; 14 of 77 five-star reviews contradict their own rating. Report 25: eight reviewers say the app asked for a review before they had used it, and one says it would not proceed without a review — if that gate existed, the 5★ share is not a satisfaction measurement for that period. Report 28: 'Every time I checked something off it would ask me to rate it' (5★, asking it to stop) — a prompt fired on the completion tap. Report 29: 'It asks for you to review it the moment you check one thing off' — ratings from people who have not yet used the app. Report 33: prompts 'three in 10 seconds' in 2017–18. Report 43: rating prompts 'every time I open this app' and 'every 2 minutes'. Report 46: 'It's asking whether I like the app just as I downloaded it!'; 'every other time I marked a habit as complete the app popped up a window asking me to rate it'. Report 50: see C094 — a prompt during the intro produces 1★ from users with no opinion. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'Хватит меня каждую секунду просить оставить отзыв' (stop asking me every second to leave a review, 1★) — cadence, not just timing. Report 60 (Mindway): 'Good but forcing me to rate😅🙄 / ITS FORCING MEE' (5★); 28 reviews (12.96%) say the reviewer has only just started ('I'm ready / I'm excited'; 'Just getting started, figuring it out!'; 'Lo voy descargando y ya me esta gustando') — 20 of the 128 5★; two 1★ with neutral text ('To soon to say'; 'Not sure about app yet') look like users rating the experience of being asked to rate; D6: stop harvesting ratings from users who have not used the app — a prompt after a routine completed on the fifth consecutive day would produce fewer, better, more durable reviews (E5). Report 64 (Critique AI): 'it got me to rate it before it charged me money so I gave it a 5 thinking that it was free because I am 13 and broke' — the likely mechanism behind a −2.09-star gap (written 2.589 on 419 vs public 4.68 on 18,785, ≥ 1.84 in every storefront), with 57 reviews (13.60%, mean 4.54) rated without product experience; research: does the prompt fire before the paywall — 'it changes how every dashboard in the business should be read'. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'app solicited a review 3 days in, after I paid for the premium version' (4★) — prompting right after a purchase reads as a second ask. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): never re-prompt someone who has already rated — 'i already rated this highly, but now I keep getting the review prompt' (1★).

title: Never cap or paywall a support conversation mid-crisis
statement: Report 9's AI coach hit its free message cap while a user was 'almost having a collapse'; an emotional-support chat needs an uncapped crisis path and a handoff to real help.

title: A promised pre-charge trial reminder must actually arrive — in-app, with amount and date
statement: Report 10: 'you promised to remind me before charging' is the highest-intensity complaint in a 70,041-review corpus (billing-dispute family mean 1.97, 60% one-star, 17% of all payers); the reminder must be a blocking in-app card on next open, not only a push, and the exact amount and charge date must sit on the trial screen and permanently in Settings. For an ADHD audience the reminder is the feature, not a courtesy. Report 48: charged the full year at the start of a 7-day trial; a receipt shared by 'another active subscriber'. Report 50: no trial-expiry reminder before a ~$50 annual charge (AU) — fix F1 pairs it with the price mismatch. Report 59 (Tappsk): a confirmation e-mail with the renewal date is the report's first immediate fix (MON_AUTO_CHARGE 229, MON_CANCEL_TROUBLE 73). Report 67 (Habio): 'The day before my trial ended, they took the money and THEN emailed me and said my trial was up the following day'; MON_NO_RECEIPT 68 (3.32%); §8.3: a reminder 48 hours before conversion with the renewal amount in local currency and the plan length. Report 68 (Ultiself): no receipt or notice before charges (MON_RECEIPT 17); §8.2: show the renewal price and date on the intro-plan screen and in a receipt email. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): no in-app notice before the free window closed — 'why, with no notice at all?'; one reviewer reports three months instead of one week (unexplained). Report 82 (Lasting Change): BILL_NO_NOTICE 11 (1.00★) — no renewal notice before any charge; 17 learned of the charge from their bank.

title: Automatic cloud backup on by default — never manual opt-in
statement: Report 10: progress stored on-device with a manual opt-in backup produced 551 data-loss reviews (9% of all 1★), a family rate that quadrupled in four years, and clinicians publicly withdrawing recommendations; 37 users did not know a backup was required until after the loss. Warn before any destructive path (delete for storage, phone change). Report 20: recovery from a developer-caused wipe was paywalled behind a manual premium iCloud backup; the recommendation is automatic daily local + iCloud snapshots with restore available to free users, and regression tests on the migration path. Report 23: Settings > Manage Data > Backups existed but was repeatedly discovered via support e-mail; several reviewers upgraded their rating on learning it existed — surface backups in the first-run tutorial, not a support reply. Report 27: iCloud sync exists ('seamless iCloud syncing'; the listing confirms) but is not legible — 'if my device gets reset all the data will be gone or I can recover it?'; a user will not reorder habits for fear of losing data; one churned after an update lost all progress; fix: a Settings line 'Backed up to iCloud · last synced <time>' plus an explicit restore path — a communication fix, not an engineering one. Report 29: optional iCloud backup, off by default and account-free, proposed against 9 data-loss reports and 3 sync requests — while one reviewer names 'I didn't even have to list my email' as the deciding factor. Report 34: a local-first no-account app praised for privacy loses data on reinstall and factory reset; optional iCloud sync would keep data off the developer's servers while fixing loss, multi-device use and exit. Report 41: a recoverable migration loss was recovered only by the developer by hand — the report asks for visible backup / restore with a 'last backed up' state. Report 42: no visible backup / restore; 'update → restart → history truncated' recurs across 2020–2026. Report 43: local-only storage with optional iCloud lost users four years of history in July 2026; the report's #1 fix is iCloud backup on by default with a visible restore path and a 'last backed up' time. Report 46: the report's #2 is a per-habit change history with one-tap 'undo last 7 days' and conflict resolution that never deletes a completed mark. Report 47: a free backup exists since Feb 2024 but the 2026 loss shows sync overwriting local history on update and recovery e-mails not arriving — backup is only as good as its restore path. Report 50: no backup or restore capability mentioned anywhere in 205 reviews after two data-loss reports. Report 69 (TheFor): a Pro purchaser: 'you have to back up you data in case your phone get lost … if auto backup option available on pro plan it wound be batter' — B4: automatic backup inside Pro closes the only paid-user request and mitigates reinstall data loss. Report 76 (Way of Life): cloud backup was a premium feature until v4.3.0 (2026) made 'Backup & Restore free for all users' — §8.2 notes that addresses cost, not the default: automatic, silent iCloud backup on by default and a restore check before any update migrates data; REQ_AUTO_BACKUP 12; NEG_BACKUP_MANUAL 13 (2.77★). Report 86 (Today): iCloud Drive / Dropbox backup was manual and paid; BUG_ICLOUD 17 — 'iCloud was clearly on but there was no automatic backup'.

merged_from.note: existing cards re-attached during consolidation

title: Compensation for lost data must match the loss — never a flat token
statement: Report 10: a flat 5,000-stone remedy offered to users who lost 20,000–200,000 stones, multi-year streaks and unrepeatable items was described as insulting and in bereavement language; restore inventory or history, not a token.

title: Never remove a feature people bought the app for — add alongside, do not replace
statement: Report 10: every major removal (Journeys → streak-based Self-Care Areas, automatic mood check-ins, exact-time goals, milestones, colour palettes) produced a dated backlash, explicit paid cancellations, and none were reversed; generic 'you removed a feature I used' grew 16× in four years. Report 18: the Sept 2024 split of the interleaved routine + to-do list into two tabs drew 32 protests at mean 4.25★ — the paying base — including subscribers who had bought a year because of the merged view days earlier; the weekly view and the Challenge feature were removed in the same release; nobody had asked for the split. Recommendation: restore it as a toggle, since a minority came to prefer the split. Report 23: the interactive widget lost at iOS 14 was partly an Apple platform change, but the five-year gap before restoration cost a top-three downgrade reason; a capability users bought for must be restored, not left behind. Report 24: the 'Make Me Fabulous' activity launcher was removed or hidden after a redesign and background music was removed — both named by long-tenure payers as renewal reasons. Report 25: an Apple Watch app reported 'suddenly removed' (Oct 2025) and Vision Pro support withdrawn — single reports, recorded not asserted. Report 27: the year-at-a-glance grid — the signature view the bundle ID is still named after (goalStreakCalendar) — was demoted behind a per-habit tap in 2025; its praise fell 16.7% → 0% and by late 2025 it appears only as a loss, even from a reviewer who still gave 5★ ('I loved it before the previous update'); the removed one-tap note export produced the corpus's only 2★ — 'one reviewer represents a workflow, not a preference'. Report 31: 'The app gets prettier. The actual functionality gets worse. Every time.' — removed monthly/yearly frequency (58), streak on the main list (52, partly restored then removed again), swipe between days (41); 'That is one of the biggest reasons I paid' (feature removed after paying, 21); a minority liked the redesigns. Report 33: removals came in release-shaped spikes — v2.0 charity points and data (2016), skip and Russian UI (2017), notes/skip to Premium (2019), Habitify X (2020), notes back-dating and editing (Dec 2024 – Jan 2025), compact/incremental/streak widgets (May 2025), passcode lock (2025) — regression 197 (5.00%, mean 2.51), 14.9% of E3; 2★ is the 'I used to love it' band (regression 15.1%, churn 12.2%); every removal needs a toggle or a migration. Report 34: CSV export, present for years, was disabled in 2026; the one-time purchase option vanished 'after updating the app'. Report 36: 'Antes: Excelente. Ahora: Pésima' — a 2★ after widgets went paid. Report 43: 'pause a habit' removed by the 2026 update. Report 46: an unrequested Dec 2022 completion animation cost a subscriber ('I'll not renew'). Report 48: the web app (2015 – ~2019) was discontinued and Windows users lost access — 17 still ask for it; widget interactivity was removed after shipping. Report 50: an update removed single-occurrence editing of recurring habits (see C073). Report 52: a ¥68 buyer asked for a refund after a Dec 2024 redesign removed to-do sorting. Report 76 (Way of Life): the 2023 removal of the old Today widget drew NEG_LOST_FEATURE 7 ('Any updates on when the widget will be fixed?', 3★); §8.8 lists what to keep — the three-state grid, good/bad inversion, skip, charts, the 3-habit free tier. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): a v2.1.0 'major internal overhaul' reset widgets and custom shortcuts and coincides with the corpus's only 'used to be great' review; the era that followed carries 8 of 9 defects. Report 83 (Roubit): the iPhone widget disappeared in a July 2025 update (a paying user, 3★); Dr. Eddy (AI counsellor) is praised 2023-08 → 2024-10 and then asked about as removed (FEATURE_REMOVED 6: 'is it gone or premium-only?'). Report 85 (Habitica): closing guilds and the tavern on 2023-08-08 — NEG_GUILD_SHUTDOWN 32 (2.25★, 2023 → 2026: 'The guilds were the soul of this app'; 'I was in a guild that basically acted as a sort of support group'), multi-year users at 23.3% of these reviews vs 3.86% overall, two of the thirteen most-voted reviews in the corpus, E4 the lowest-rated era (3.37★), community praise 4.4% → 1.0%; the US description still lists Guilds three years later; §8.7 replace what the guilds did with small opt-in moderated groups and a party-matching queue. Report 86 (Today): a widget that had become the primary interface for many (PR_WIDGET 28, 4.50★) was removed without a word and restored under pressure; the iOS-14 home-screen widget requested from 2020-09 to 2025-12 was never built — REQ_WIDGET 47 is 'the only request that grows as the corpus shrinks' (1.98% of E1 → 16.95% of E5).

title: Content and event releases need a crash gate across device generations
statement: Report 10: a monthly event's 'grow potion' animation crashed the app on load for a large cohort (120 crash reviews in Feb 2026, 4–6× baseline), destroying 600-day streaks and locking paid users out for weeks; reviewers blame the event cadence for shipping untested code. Report 31: 1.19.0 (launch crash), the May 2022 hang and 2.7.1/2.7.2 (count corruption) were all shipped to everyone. Report 52: release waves recur on old OS versions (v2.41 on iOS 13 biometric unlock; iOS 14.x launch crash for 20+ days) — F5: a release gate for old iOS and data migrations, staged rollout, crash-safe local store before schema changes; target no month with ≥20 crash reviews. Report 55: F4 — test every build against current and previous iOS versions and screen sizes; staged rollout; halt on a crash spike (no month with >10 crash reviews). Report 59 (Tappsk): the report's immediate fix is 'a release check on the oldest supported iOS and on the show-completed-tasks path before shipping; a fast hotfix path' — the 2021-10 crash hit only older iPhones and the 2023 crash only one setting path; the Turkish habit-reminder crash adds locale to the gate. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): I3 — a regression gate on tap / hit-testing before release plus a fast rollback path; 'nothing in this corpus suggests a process change prevented the next one' and one bad build cost ~0.32 stars on the whole written history. Report 85 (Habitica): §8.1 staged rollout with crash-rate gating — the corpus holds 201 reviews blaming a specific update and single days with 49 crash reports; a halted rollout would have contained three waves. Report 86 (Today): a paid biometric lock shipped in a build where enabling it crashed the app on entry (March 2018, 5 reviews in nine days: 'What was my 30 yuan for?… I appealed to Apple and was told no refund'); the same fortnight carried an IAP outage — 'the month this app broke its paying users on two axes at once'.

title: Every guilt mechanic must be optional — streaks, repair prompts, countdowns
statement: Report 10: the app was praised specifically for not guilting users (476 reviews, mean 4.87); after streaks shipped mid-2024, 96 reviews say it now punishes the missed day the audience was promised it wouldn't, and repairing a streak costs currency. A single 'gentle mode' toggle is the corpus's own proposal. Report 18: an automatic streak 'shield' made the streak number feel fake ('I get complacent since the number won't disappear'), while an ADHD reviewer said a broken streak is the feature that makes them quit and asked to hide the UI; another sat in red all day because the routine could only be finished at night. Conclusion: streak, shield, light and cheer messages are per-user toggles, default shield off. Report 23: loss-framed reminder copy is a guilt mechanic users in four languages ask to switch off or reframe. Report 26: a 'no wither' / Zen mode (the garden does not decay) exists as a premium option; gentleness and no streaks are praised at mean 4.76 and the mental-health segment (32, mean 4.66 — 'this app helped me fix my severe depression') is the clearest argument against any harsher rule. Report 28: rabbit health/energy decay with guilt notifications ('YOUR BUNNY'S LOSING HEALTH COME AND DO HABITS TO FIX IT!') and a challenge-mode full reset penalise exactly the cautious beginner ('I have few habits because I'm starting a healthier lifestyle slowly'); a defender values the stakes — make decay a setting, separate it visibly from the data model. Report 33: an 'Are you sure the day is over?' confirmation on fail/skip with no off switch. Report 36: 7 ask for streaks / reps / loss-on-break (incl. a 45-vote review) while 11 praise the absence of streak shame — make streaks optional, with a 'don't skip twice' rule proposed. Report 41: 'the percentage focus and backseating of streaks made this a thing i actually use' — one streak-prominence request is treated as a minority against the differentiator. Report 46: the skip mark is why perfectionists stay — 'you don't want to break a streak, so you keep going' with 'no punishment other than a break in the color gradient'; rule 17: do not remove or harden the forgiving skip. Report 47: the streak resets to zero on a miss and is praised by 3 as motivating, while the grid's kept colour is the non-punitive part reviewers love; a missed-day marker (4 requests, 3 KR) should be optional. Report 49: an optional hard mode that resets to day 1 with penalty tasks on a miss is loved by a small, intense, entirely satisfied group (13, 4.77) — opt-in severity works; guilt-inducing tone as a default is criticised (13). Report 54: 12 (3.25%, 4.75) praise the deliberate absence of streaks — 'most likely because it does not track streaks (which my black and white brain reads as failure if I am not perfect)… These are skills. Skills can be learned. I am not broken'; 'I have adhd and using streaks has always resulted in beating myself up'; one downloaded because a review said there were no streaks; D6: claim it; §8.5: do not add streaks with penalties. Report 59 (Tappsk): a daily productivity score with a trend arrow demotivates a minority — NEG_SCORE 23 vs PR_SCORE 84: 'ОЧЕНЬ ДЕМОТИВИРУЕТ эта стрелочка которая показывает насколько я продуктивна' (this arrow showing how productive I am is VERY demotivating, 4★). Report 65 (Rabit): a missed habit kills the plant — 'Missing one scheduled habit completely kills a plant?!! … I don't mind a penalty but this is dark souls level'; 'are we supposed to lie?' — users accept the penalty when deserved and reject it when not, so plant death is 'the single riskiest design decision in the product'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the reset divides users — PR_RESET_TENSION 40 value the discipline; a March 2018 update removed the automatic reset (6 welcomed it, 13 asked for it back as late as 2024: 'For some people motivation drops sharply without the reset'); the answer is an option in both directions, not one rule. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): the counter-case — an app whose entire thesis is no streak pressure drew zero negative reactions to that thesis across 71 reviews, 28 storefronts and six languages; CONCEPT_FORGIVING 11 (4.82★): 'if you miss a day it isn't all for nothing; it reflects a healthy relationship with habits'. Report 83 (Roubit): a 1★ from someone for whom the app 'feels too much like a game to use'; the game layer is default-on and not hideable. Report 85 (Habitica): the health penalty for missed Dailies is the pressure some need (PR_PENALTY 34) and drives others out — NEG_PUNISH 23, BUG_DEATH 12, REQ_PAUSE 7: 'I don't want to be punished again for my health problems' (3★); 'I crashed out from the penalties when having a tough time and ended up uninstalling it for almost 3 years' (4★, returned); §8.9 make resting in the inn discoverable and time-limited and test milder death penalties (keep levels) — 'fewer punishment-triggered quits without losing the pressure PR_PENALTY reviewers value'.

title: Credit for non-consecutive, cumulative progress alongside streaks
statement: Report 10: replacing cumulative Journeys with consecutive-streak Self-Care Areas was the lowest-rated change in the corpus (mean 2.76, 21 of 49 one-star); chronic-illness and ADHD users say a streak-only model is structurally incompatible with their lives. Ship cumulative credit next to streaks, not instead of them.

title: Launch-to-core-action path with no interstitials
statement: Report 10: 'overwhelm' is the largest UX complaint (1,046 reviews) — an app sold to people with executive-function difficulty accumulated six sequential screens (quote, mood prompt, event cutscene, visitor, chest, claim-confirm-claim) before the checklist. Report 24: an app sold as an ADHD focus aid is described as itself overstimulating ('This app literally GIVES me adhd') — cluttered/overwhelming 1,324 (3.05%, mean 3.068) and confusing navigation 1,507 (3.47%, mean 2.338), rising through the good eras too (1.90% → 4.26%); 46.1% of clutter requests come from 4–5★ users, so a low-stimulus home screen that opens on today's routine with coaching, Discover, Circles and cross-app promotion below the fold is a retention feature; checking off one habit takes 3–5 screens. Report 47: check-in takes 2–4 taps (long-press → record screen → done; a reviewer counts '記録したい項目を選択→＋→完了→＜') and one-tap logging has been requested since 2019 — too many taps 14 (2.38%, mean 2.86: '気軽にチェック入れたいのに何タップもアクションが多くて億劫になる'); the report's E4 is an optional one-tap mode with the memo screen skipped unless long-pressed. Report 48: 'open the app, click a check mark, exit' is what simplicity means to 817 reviewers — see [[C264]]. Report 65 (Rabit): BUG_ONBOARD 22 (mean 1.45, the lowest of any theme with n>10) — recommended installs that never got past the intro ('TODOS OS MEUS AMIGOS ME RECOMENDARAM'), twice as common outside Brazil, i.e. in the expansion audience.

title: Honour what onboarding asks — a declared limitation must change the suggestions
statement: Report 10: the onboarding asks about disability and then ignores the answer ('I have mobility issues, so I clicked that… ever since, the app has been suggesting that I do things that I've told it I can't do'); 597 accessibility reviews at mean 4.56. Report 24: a long onboarding questionnaire produces an identical plan for everyone — 'You will answer a ton of questions about your habits and goals and then the app will not take any of your answers into account'; 'I told it I drink water all day. The first habit I'm to build is drinking three glasses of water' (no-customisation 175, mean 2.097; forced first habit 124, mean 2.452, consistent across eleven years and six languages). Report 49: asthma, post-surgical injury, nerve damage and mobility limits cannot be entered and running stays the only cardio (10 + 20) — see [[C266]].

title: Values and identity screens are optional in both directions
statement: Report 10: 54 users deleted at a mandatory pet-pronoun step, 109 objected to Pride content, and 111 loyal users (mean 4.57) complained representation was missing; the only intervention the corpus supports is a skip option and a show/hide filter for themed cosmetics — optionality, not editorial change. Report 24: onboarding includes a 'letter from your future self' and a held-finger 'contract' signed with the fingerprint sensor, reached via a social ad and a web questionnaire.

title: Automated suggestions from user text must be safety-filtered; notifications must be crisis-aware
statement: Report 10: the goal-suggestion system parsed a journal entry about suicidal ideation into a goal to 'schedule time for suicide'; diagnosis quizzes returned severe results to children in a 4+ app; a 'you can do this' push arrived right after a text about suicide. Report 24: diet-culture / eating-disorder trigger complaints (61, mean 2.918) in a wellness routine app. Report 28: untargeted ad content inside a 4+ app used by self-declared 8–10-year-olds and by a teacher with students — 'ads for AI homework apps that will write papers for you… encouraging bad habits through these ads'. Report 83 (Roubit): the AI 'support letter' that replies to diary entries receives crisis-level disclosures — '제가 죽고싶었을때가 있는데 이거 덕분에 지금 제가 여기있었어요' (there was a time I wanted to die; thanks to this I'm here now, 5★); 'No es una exageración decir que esta aplicación me salvó la vida'; USE_MENTAL_HEALTH 16 (depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, crisis); one reviewer values that the letters keep 'recommending seeking a professional'; Dr. Eddy (AI counsellor chat) answered a factual question wrongly and is used by a minor for homework; 13 reviews are from students or children behind a 14+ sign-up gate on a 4+ app; §8.3 document and test how the AI responds to self-harm, crisis and minor users, always surface crisis resources, label the letter as AI — 'the question is not frequency but handling'.

title: Visible monthly plan — annual-default trials drive billing disputes
statement: Report 10: the 7-day trial defaults to an annual charge; 23 reviews ask for a monthly plan and several say they would have paid monthly; the annual default is the mechanism behind most of the 404 billing disputes. Report 25: the most specific repeated billing claim is that a 7-day trial renews into the annual plan when monthly was selected ('charged 25,000 pesos when I had chosen the monthly option'; 'You can't choose to be renewed to the 1 month subscription'); make trial→plan mapping explicit and let the user pick the post-trial plan. Report 31: a monthly billing plan was wanted (8) and one user had to switch to monthly to be able to cancel before a €100+ renewal. Report 33: a monthly plan missing in some storefronts or offered only on the web ('only … yearly and lifetime … I would have signed up for a month'; 'pagar 50-60€ como única opción?') — offer monthly in-app everywhere. Report 59 (Tappsk): the 7-day trial converts to the annual (999 ₽) by default; 111 of 306 trial mentions report an immediate charge and the annual sum is what makes the 1★ ('a year's money'). Report 64 (Critique AI): annual-upfront is an upgrade barrier and the billing-dispute class — three payers expected trial or monthly flexibility and got a full-year charge; 'Almeno dividessero il prezzo in mesi'; M5: a monthly or one-time SKU visible before the annual.

title: A random-rotation shop with paid re-rolls and unpurchasable catalogue items is a friction generator
statement: Report 10: goals yield 3–12 stones while items cost 500–900, the shop rotates randomly, and the item you want never appears — 196 complaints from engaged, currency-rich users, the ones most likely to subscribe. Let users buy what they can see. Report 85 (Habitica): challenge prize draws are the main free route to gems and reviewers say they reward lying ('you have to just lie and say you did it', 3★); NOTE_CHEAT 27 notice the honour system.

title: Official community channels must tolerate criticism
statement: Report 10: the Facebook group, Discord and subreddit are described as heavily moderated and hostile to criticism across five years (211 reviews), with paying users 7× over-represented; suppression of criticism resurfaces in every later controversy. Report 85 (Habitica): a staff–volunteer-moderator dispute handled in public — STAFF_CONTROVERSY 19 (0.55%, mean 1.74★, 2022-12 → 2024-11: 'When workers asked for better conditions, they were treated disrespectfully and many were fired'; 'Habitica was one of the least toxic social spaces on the internet') preceded and compounded the guild closure; SUP_NOT_LISTENING 4.7% of E4.

title: Keep the therapeutic core in front of the game layer
statement: Report 10: as breathing, first aid and soundscapes moved behind menus and paywalls, tool mentions fell 15.6% → 2.7% and the core-benefit family 30% → 23%, while reviewers called the product 'a pay-to-play loot box checklist simulator'; the game is why people call it cute and motivating, but it must not be paid for by burying the layer people came for. Report 64 (Critique AI): a paying reviewer's verdict splits the product — the AI plan is not worth it, the coaching and challenges are.

title: Cosmetic and colour variety as the paid layer
statement: Report 10: buyers name extra colour options, seasonal items and a larger shop as the specific hook ('I started getting finch plus solely because I found the extra color options… very motivating'); restricting palettes later (Aug–Sep 2026) drew a backlash. Report 36: cosmetic gating (≈10 premium skins) is 'broadly accepted when it is the only gate' — 'So far the app is mostly free aside from cosmetics (understandable)' — and 3 of 34 payers bought for skins; selling skins separately on top of the membership reads as double-charging ('$15 for permission to buy a $10 skin'). Report 47: more colours unlocked by watching a video (2022) — the one rewarded-ad surface reviewers accepted. Report 52: themes sold separately (~¥6 each, 2018) then made free for members — a buyer was refunded. Report 76 (Way of Life): paid themes / add-ons (MON_BUY_ITEMS 27, 4.44★) are bought — 16.48× over-represented among purchasers — but gating dark mode specifically drew a 3★. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): PAID_INAPP_CONTENT 1 — 'Love the bonus of buying and planting a forest' (5★): cosmetic content bought in-app rather than a tier; the only purchase in the corpus tied to a named thing. Report 83 (Roubit): 'Ultimate' yearly plan adds exclusive themes and outfits; Gold Carrots sold as consumables ($0.99–$9.99); PAYWALL_COSMETICS 4 (0.80%, 'A bit greedy') vs REQ_CUSTOMISE_CHARACTER 14 at 5.00★ — cosmetics are wanted and lightly resented as a paid layer.

title: Monthly seasonal event with a paid reward track
statement: Report 10: event completion is a stated purchase trigger, but events are also the named cause of the 2026 crash and data-loss clusters, FOMO complaints, and the sponsored-IP values breach.

title: Completion verification / anti-cheat
statement: Report 10: 158 users volunteer that they check boxes without doing the task and ask to be held accountable (mean 4.59); its sibling 'it's just a checklist' (111) is the churn thesis. Report 71 (MyStreaks): 'I feel like people cheat and just put a random number so they're on the discover feature… people still acknowledge those who have a large number of streaks' — editable streak counts ranking on a social Discover feed make the community's currency forgeable, a flaw 'independent of how many people mentioned it' that grows with the community; §8.2 #6: non-editable counts or a visible 'edited' mark on Discover. Report 85 (Habitica): NOTE_CHEAT 27 — the honour system is noticed but rarely treated as a flaw; it becomes one where gems are the prize ('you have to just lie and say you did it').

title: Configurable day boundary and hemisphere seasons
statement: Report 10: 146 reviews say the app assumes a conventional daytime schedule and northern-hemisphere seasons; night-shift workers and southern-hemisphere users ask for a movable day boundary. Report 18: a configurable day-end time was requested ~15 times across KR, JP and US, and the timezone stayed on Korean time for diaspora users from 2021 to 2024 (US daylight saving unhandled). Report 23: day-boundary / midnight reset requested (54, 0.74%, emerging, mean 4.02). Report 25: a day-start time setting exists for shift workers but is capped at 11:45. Report 26: a user-set day boundary requested alongside backfill (29); persistent across five years. Report 27: a Monday week-start setting asked twice in early 2024 (DE/AU) and never again. Report 31: a day-start offset for late sleepers and shift workers (capped at 5 am) was later removed; day-start / midnight rollover 18. Report 34: 'My day always ends after midnight' — a configurable day start, citing Habitica's setting. Report 41: custom day-start and week-start shipped May 2025 after being requested from 2021; night-shift day reset 5. Report 46 (counter-signal): none; the grid's day boundary is not raised. Report 49: the wake-time control permits only ~5–10am, excluding night-shift, graveyard and FIFO workers — 31 reviews at 3.42 (well above the corpus), 23 stating their shift, US +2.15pp, several saying they want the product while uninstalling; the daily recap closes the day at a fixed ~9pm (10) — 'the cheapest high-value fix in the report'; a partial fix turned a 4★ into 5★. Report 52: night owls' check-ins after midnight land on the next day — 50 text mentions ask to end the day at 2–4 am. Report 53: end the day at 1–5 am and handle time-zone travel (CORE_DAYSTART 9). Report 59 (Tappsk): NEG_DAY_BOUNDARY 19 — 'Как быть совам' (what about night owls, 1★); the report proposes a user-set day boundary alongside back-dating. Report 65 (Rabit): 'My day does not start or end at 12am… I track my water usage past midnight and it doesn't reset after I sleep??'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the previous day is recordable until 3 a.m. — praised as grace (PR_GRACE 41) and by a night-shift worker ('choosing yesterday or today after midnight is welcome for night workers'), yet late studiers and shift workers get caught ('if I record at 15:00 one day, I can't record at 10:00 the next'; NEG_DAYBOUNDARY 11, REQ_DAYBOUNDARY_SET 6) — Japan's specific rule friction. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_DAY_ROLLOVER 9 (custom day end, 2014 → 2024). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_DAY_START 1 (custom start of day) shipped in v2.4.0; REQ_BEDTIME 1. Report 83 (Roubit): 'not getting carrots for tasks done after midnight kills motivation' (kr) — a later day boundary requested. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 1.0.19 'Custom week start' shipped after two week-boundary defects (a weekend tick toggling both days). Report 85 (Habitica): NEG_DAYSTART 16 — the custom day start interacts with a server-side rollover that sometimes fails (BUG_RESET 93). Report 86 (Today): day-start time requested in 2016 (a twenty-item Japanese list); a time-zone check-in bug fixed 6.5 years after the first report.

title: Accessibility stack: VoiceOver, motion, sound and light sensitivity, text size
statement: Report 10: 597 accessibility reviews (0.85%, mean 4.56) from blind, mobility-limited, chronically ill, motion-, sound- and light-sensitive users; dark mode is argued as an accessibility need, not a preference ('Cute clothes for the bird were apparently shippable'). Report 23: accessibility / VoiceOver 19 (0.26%, mean 3.79). Report 24: accessibility (vision, font, VoiceOver) 129 (0.30%, mean 3.101). Report 26: a detailed, actionable VoiceOver defect report — images without alt text, focus loss, elements announced only as 'botão' — plus larger text and low-contrast reports; dynamic type was added and praised; promoted on inclusion/legal grounds at 5 reviews. Report 31: no VoiceOver support, small fonts/buttons (19) — ship VoiceOver labels, Dynamic Type and 44 pt targets. Report 33: memo input breaks under Japanese IME. Report 36: respect the silence switch and add a global audio toggle (2, one an uninstall). Report 41: the Mac app has no text zoom — 'text and icons are too small on my 27-inch display' (the only accessibility report). Report 42: premium pop-ups 'difficult to click out of' alongside a text-size accessibility complaint. Report 43: 'this app works with voiceover since I am a voiceover user' (the only screen-reader confirmation); 'The text is small, I can not see to read it!' Report 46: accessibility requests 8 (font size, VoiceOver, reading needs — 'unique reading needs' from a dyslexic 5★); a VoiceOver regression on iOS 15 (IT). Report 47: time-picker digits unreadable in dark mode (2); the skip key hidden by the keyboard (Jul 2025); the settings button hidden by long tab names (a payer). Report 48: accessibility 6 (3.50). Report 53: VoiceOver compatibility shipped on request (2022) for blind users. Report 54: a detailed VoiceOver report (many fields and buttons unreadable, DE, 1★, offering to re-review once fixed) and Dynamic Type text cut off — 'below the 1% bar, but flagged under the standing exception for accessibility, and cheap to fix'. Report 57: dark mode paywalled against photosensitivity. Report 60 (Mindway): time entry on a 24-hour clock only, no AM/PM option — 'This confuses me a lot'; F6: add AM/PM time entry, 'one review, one line of work, and it is the only reported input-level usability defect in the corpus' — respect the user's locale time format. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an app that cannot be operated by tapping is an accessibility failure in effect — the June build; zero explicit accessibility requests otherwise. Report 76 (Way of Life): the listing ships a colour-blind mode; REQ_COLORBLIND 1; REQ_FONT 2; REQ_LANDSCAPE 9 (3.44★). Report 86 (Today): accessibility evidence is absent — 2 incidental mentions in 1,785 — 'an evidence gap, not an all-clear'; a full-screen-photo app with text over imagery has obvious contrast risk and 'unreadable text on light wallpapers' was reported in 2016.

title: Per-day / per-habit notes and journal text
statement: A note field on each check-in is pure upside and requested by happy users (reports 2, 3, 7); a single cramped line is the common complaint; charging for journal text while mood is free drew complaints (report 9). Report 20: notes per day was the single most-requested feature in the corpus (79, mean 3.66) and never shipped. Report 23: per-completion notes were requested from 2015 (43, 0.59%) and shipped ~Mar 2023; the residual ask is navigation between notes. Report 25: a notes / journal / mood field per day requested by 7 (mean 4.43). Report 26: a journal / gratitude note requested (~4). Report 27: daily memo prompts exist and their value is disputed ('simply yet engaging daily memo questions' vs 'the note taking doesn't really have a point to it'); a fuller daily log is wanted. Report 28: journal/notes per day and mood tracking used by 38 (4.63%, mean 4.29). Report 31: notes/journal per entry and timestamps (added Jan 2017) — 82 mentions (mean 3.52); 'last done / minutes ago' removed in 2022–23. Report 33: per-habit per-day notes / journal moved to Premium in Apr 2019 (free users lost 300 days of notes) and in Dec 2024 – Jan 2025 lost back-dating and editing (1,000+ gym days logged in memos). Report 34: notes per completed day are Premium (praised 11, mean 4.91); notes on missed days and opening a note from the calendar requested by 9 (a 'No Spend' habit). Report 36: notes on a habit requested by 3. Report 43: journal / per-day notes praised by 9 (mean 4.44) — but a journal prompt forced on every skip in the 2025 redesign drew a 1★ from a long-time payer. Report 46: journal / per-day notes shipped Dec 2023 (praised 12, mean 4.67) after 9 requests. Report 47: a per-day memo attached to each check-in is the diary feature Korean and Japanese reviewers name as the differentiator (memo + photo 32, 5.43%, mean 4.75); a note-length limit is asked by 3; one user stopped writing memos after the 2026 data loss. Report 48: per-entry notes praised by 21 (4.95), requested by 14; whether notes are free is disputed in-thread. Report 50: see [[C268]] — the journal is a primary reason to choose the app and its editor the worst-quality surface. Report 52: check-in notes are the largest unmet need (JRNL_WANT 668, 3.24%, very strong) and a praised micro-diary with 'on this day in past years' (234, 4.85). Report 54: notes per habit requested (3, 4.67). Report 56: per-habit description / notes requested by 3 — ship a short label first; journaling is a separate question. Report 57: notes allowed only on successful check-ins — 9 ask across six years and three languages to write why they failed ('I want to write down why I couldn't do it on the days I failed'). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a per-day value / note ('walked 5k, then 7k') requested by a 4★ reviewer. Report 64 (Critique AI): a notes space requested (ch, 5★). Report 65 (Rabit): a notes / description field per habit (REQ_DESC 2) and calendar notes on why a habit was missed (S7). Report 67 (Habio): the daily reflection journal is one of the two things the corpus says to keep. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a note per check-in requested (REQ_MEMO 7, mean 4.43). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): a free-text note / link on a habit (3 — one to attach a yoga video link), the largest request. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): the memo written on the check cell itself (9, 4.67) — 'The memo isn't tucked away, it's on the check itself, so when you scan back you don't have to open them one by one… the memo usability really is one of a kind'. Report 75 (Habit Streak): a daily note / journal and completion timestamps requested by one 4★. Report 76 (Way of Life): per-day notes are free and praised (PR_NOTES 174, 2.24%, 4.86★, 1.53× among purchasers); friction is reaching and searching them (REQ_NOTES_VIEW 13, NEG_NOTES_UX 4) and photos (REQ_PHOTO 9). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_NOTES 2 (Aug–Sep 2024) shipped as check-in notes / Journal in v1.9.0 (2025-08-14). Report 83 (Roubit): a diary with mood logging is the emotional core (PRAISE_DIARY 24); REQ_DIARY_FEATURES 10 — photos, more moods, memos, more than one entry a day ('I pay so letters are unlimited, which is good, but I can only write one a day'). Report 84 (HabitGrid): notes shipped in 1.0.5 and were praised eight months later; 'add a note' is part of the ideal described by a 5★. Report 86 (Today): a journal card exists (PR_JOURNAL 24) yet a note per check-in is the second-most-upvoted request (31 up / 47: 'to record it at that point in time. That way you can know yourself more accurately', cn 5★; REQ_NOTE 12) — never shipped.

title: Sub-tasks / sub-routines nested inside a habit or routine
statement: 'Shower routine' reused inside 'morning routine'; sub-habits are what heavy users ask for after categories (reports 1, 5, 7). Report 41: sub-tasks with time per step requested by 7, one blocking a purchase ('I need sub tasks with time for each'). Report 52: sub-tasks requested (62, weak). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_SUBTASKS 6.

title: Multiple profiles (me, kids, pet, work)
statement: Requested alongside folders in report 1 — separate people or contexts inside one app. Report 23: family/multi-person use inside one account is a stated reason for more task slots. Report 85 (Habitica): families run it as a shared chore system (USE_FAMILY 58) and a paid group plan exists for shared task lists — but is reported unusable in the iOS app.

title: Updates must not break function or wipe progress
statement: 'Then Boom… updated! Now… the progress is gone' (report 4); a nine-week window of hard functional failures (report 8); an update broke chronological sorting across four countries in one week (report 9); near-daily forced updates are themselves a complaint (report 10). Report 18: a July 2026 update told a mid-term subscriber to buy a new plan; lag, solved by 2025, regressed sharply (1.83% → 5.38%) as routine modes, intensity levels and note/tracker features were added. Report 26: the 2022 'music cannot be turned off' defect (10 reviews, May–Nov 2022) was fixed and stayed fixed — a clean, closed defect; the later inverse (music won't play) is 3 reviews. Report 27: the 2025 update broke launch on iOS 26 and removed the one-tap note export, the day-tap record popup, the single-screen annual overview and backfill from the annual grid — the same update that shipped multi-check-ins and flexible frequency; 'feature removals in this app are more expensive than feature absences'. Report 28: a listing version ten months older than the newest reviews coincides with 2026 freezing, crashing and broken-login reports — 'verify the app on current iOS and ship an update'; the 2022 rabbit-off-screen, can't-clean-the-room and orange-screen bugs were fixed and stayed fixed. Report 31: v2 rebuild (Mar 2022) brought 10–30 s tap lag, a broken Watch app and removed past-entry editing (restored in 2.0.8); v3.0 (Jan 2023) brought a week-start bug and a custom-count +1 bug. Report 33: v2.0 (Nov 2016) wiped data and Premium; Habitify X broke the Watch; 'update made it worse' spiked 7.6% in 2020 and 5.8% in 2025. Report 43: regression after update 16 (2.51%) — 3 → 4 → 9 by era, eight of the nine recent inside Oct 2025 – Jul 2026; three updates in two days then 'I can no longer access the app… All the I spent created things are lost'. Report 46: 'The new IOS update has wiped all of my historical and tracking data' (GB, 1★, Sep 2022); a Sep 2020 'won't open after the update' cluster of six reviews in three days across five storefronts. Report 47: an update in August 2026 overwrote years of history (8 reviews in 3–20 Aug); an update in 2022 scrambled habit order (5); the back button vanished in Nov 2020; 'アプリ更新したら勝手にデータ上書きされて'. Report 48: paid subscription not recognised after an update (3); the 2015 v3.0 release lost data for 25 and duplicated trackers for 20. Report 52: an update that could not be downloaded or reinstalled produced 12 reviews on one day (31 Jul 2023); BUG_UPDATE 524 (2.54%, 3.26). Report 53: re-certify Watch app and widgets on every iOS release — iOS 11.3, iOS 13 and iOS 18/26 each broke a surface. Report 55: crash waves after the July 2017, 2018 and 2020 updates; fixes reported twice, the second after nine months. Report 56: a sync update deleted habits; defects clustered in the Jun–Jul build cycle. Report 57: 'an update broke it' is constant for seven years (update_regression 59, 7.57%) — a Sep 2020 release broke the note keyboard (21 reviews in three days, mostly still 5★) and a Jun 2020 release stopped launch (8); 'every update breaks something that worked. Please just leave it alone'. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_UPDATE 103 (2.83★) and the four release-clustered regressions ([[C031]]); the quietest release era (E4, 2022-03 → 2023-05) is also the best-rated (4.70★, praise 80.3%, defects 3.5%), and the regression era that followed the lowest since launch on crashes. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'Seems like each time when it updates the habits progress for the last week wipes. These happened two times already' (KZ, 2★, Aug 2026) and a total loss on launch ten months earlier — present before the June regression and still present after it was fixed; I4: treat habit history as migration-critical data with an integrity check on upgrade — 'in a streak product, destroyed history destroys the only thing the user has accumulated'. Report 65 (Rabit): plants purchased under Plus re-locked behind a padlock after an update; 14 reviewers attribute a regression to a specific release (BUG_UPDATE, mean 2.71). Report 76 (Way of Life): U_UPDATE_REGRESSION 84 (1.08%, mean 3.08★); BUG_UPDATE_BROKE 54 (2.80★) — 21 from 2012-11/12 (a release that left the app unusable or corrupted data: 'latest release has left this application unusable'), 12 from 2016-05/06 (crash on 'updating journal' at launch; reviews from six countries within two days), a 2017-07 release that wiped histories ('Latest update deleted my entire history', 5★), the 2014-06 v3.0 flat redesign called awful and greedy (NEG_UPDATE_WORSE 17), the 2023 loss of the Today widget; 10.50% of 1★; the two worst months in 16 years (2012-11 at 4.38★, 2015-01 at 4.36★) are both regressions. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'now we have reached a point with the new update, where the app can't even open without crashing' (dk 1★, 2025-08-26) — the only reliability regression, and it opened the 70-day window holding all six of the corpus's one-star reviews; defects then fell to zero for 37 consecutive reviews. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): U:defect_any 0.9% (E1) → 0.0% → 19.5% (E3, mean 2.50★); 8 of 9 defects after v2.1.0 (2026-02-11), 'a major internal overhaul' whose own notes warn 'widgets and custom shortcuts need to be re-configured', followed within four days by a 'Deduplicate data' tool 'as some people reported duplicated boards and check-ins'; a crash on board creation fixed by name 11 days later; a self-described daily user: 'I loved how easy it was to use, how reliable it was… Now UI bugs have made it unusable' (1★); the two worst-rated eras follow a rename and an overhaul. Report 83 (Roubit): 'new bugs seem to appear with every update, so I'm thinking of switching apps' (3★); two blank-screen waves coinciding with releases (6.1.24 'Dreaming Idol' theme; 6.4.50 ad-rewards) — timing not proven cause; BUG_UPDATE_LOOP 7 — a forced update that cannot be installed (2022, Feb–Mar 2025, Mar–Apr 2026); widget removed in July 2025 for a paying user; U:defect_any 14.7% (E1) → 73.5% (E4); 'the product broke under paying users' — 14 of 27 payers report a defect. Report 85 (Habitica): U_BUG_ANY 1428 (41.45%, mean 2.81★) over eleven years — BUG_CRASH 415, BUG_REGRESSION 201 blame a specific update; the waves are dated: 2016-11 (72 reviews, 54 crashes on the Rewards page), 2017-10 (86, 45 crash on launch), 2021-08-20 (49 reviews in one day, 47 crashes: 'crashes and auto closes in a matter of seconds'); crash reports fall to 2.1% from 2024 but the newer defects are quieter and more corrosive — Dailies not resetting (BUG_RESET 93), taps on the wrong task, widgets not refreshing; 386 of 488 1★ carry a defect; §8.1 'a staged rollout with crash-rate gating would have contained 2016-11, 2017-10 and 2021-08-20'. Report 86 (Today): five datable crash waves in ten years — launch Mar 2016 (Editors' Choice, 21 crash reviews in three weeks, 'Great crash simulator'), iOS 9/10 Oct–Nov 2016 (18), Face ID / Touch ID Mar 2018 (enabling the paid lock crashed the app), iOS 12 / watchOS 5 Sep 2018 (the Watch app), and the black-screen build 1.9.63 of 2022-11-09 with the next release 1,030 days later; BUG_UPDATE 42 (2.55★); the mean fell 4.16 → 4.14 → 3.59 → 3.51 → 3.07 across five eras — 'reliability, not features, is what destroyed this product'; the pre-2019 vs 2019-onward gap is 0.61★ over 458 reviews, 'not a bad week; it is the product's trajectory'.

title: Never let fear of losing history be the reason people pay
statement: Report 11: the only stated purchase motive was 'I had 3 years worth of history I didn't want to lose' on an app with no export or backup; when the entitlement then failed, the loyal long-tenure user became the 1★ 'scam' review. Sell durability (backup, export, long-history analytics) as a gain, never gate access to what the user already built. Report 33: a weekly check-in cap locked free users out of long streaks ('After 500 days I was pay-walled'). Report 34: 'forced to keep paying … if you don't want to lose all your history' — export disabled and a paid backup before delete, both 1★. Report 36: 'the most dangerous customer' is the multi-year free user who changed device or ran out of habits in 2026 — data in the app, no export and no sync, 'cannot leave cleanly and cannot continue without paying' (LOCKIN). Report 57: free-tier history cut to 30 days while backup is Premium — 'in the end I learned for the first time that without paid Premium, backup and recovery are impossible'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): 'Going paid is unavoidable, but suddenly not being able to see my past history either — isn't that unkind?' — locking history converts a pricing decision into hostage-taking in the users' own words; 'the difference between I decided not to pay and they took my medication log'. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'I lost all my habits when I got a new phone even though I paid for the app' (5★) — cloud backup sold as premium for most of the app's life, then made free in 4.3.0. Report 86 (Today): backup and restore is the paid feature and 12 of the 55 data-loss reviewers had paid — 'selling backup and then losing data is the corpus's sharpest breach of trust': 'the third time I've opened the app to find months worth of data has been randomly corrupted/lost… despite having paid extra to back it up' (1★); 'I lost my 3 years data due to an issue in restore backup' (it 1★); 'the crucial backup was overwritten and even the restore data was wiped' (jp, titled 'Farewell, Today'); nobody in the corpus reports buying for backup — 'the paid features that convert are the ones users can see'.

title: One clear SKU shelf — every plan distinctly named, stating its period, and delivering exactly what its label says
statement: Report 11: three SKUs shared the identical display name 'Habits PRO Functions' at $1.99 / $6.99 / $8.99 and none named a period, while reviewers described 'annual', 'VIP' and 'lifetime' purchases — neither the user nor support could tell what had been bought. Report 12: ten SKUs including three 'Weekly Subscription' and two 'One-Time Payment' entries at different prices, visible on the store page. Report 19: charged ≠ agreed ($29.99 annual agreed, $59.99/month billed) when the plan bought was never named back to the buyer. Report 30: Monthly $5.99, Yearly $44.99, a second Yearly $29.99 and Lifetime $59.99 — 'Te dicen que es de por vida el plan y es solo para un año' ('Cuidado, engañan'), and the monthly option could not be bought ('it charges for a year'); five of the six reviewers who reached payment had a bad outcome. Collapse the shelf. Report 41: the Lifetime SKU was intermittently invisible — 'I can no longer see the lifetime plan which I would like to purchase!'; 'When activated trial there was a lifetime subscription option. Now don't see it'; 'bummed I missed out on the lifetime deal'; and a Chinese user found no purchase entry at all — 'the cheapest revenue recovery in the report'. Report 42: seven concurrent IAPs, five near-identically named at $39.99 / $59.99 — reviewers quote wildly different prices by year and storefront. Report 43: the purchase sheet does not say 'one time' — 5 reviewers (mean 4.20) could not tell whether $2.99 was monthly or once, three of them 5★ users trying to buy ('can't seem to figure out if the $2.99 is per month or a one time purchase.?') and one who wrote a 2★ believing it was monthly; the thing the sheet fails to state is the product's most-praised attribute. Report 46: three concurrent premium SKUs (ED Premium Monthly, Everyday Premium Year, ED Full Year Access) beside a lifetime; a web price cheaper than in-app ('only $12 a year on the website, more in the app'). Report 49: the UK's advertised £1.99–£2/month resolves to a £24.99–£29.99 annual charge at checkout (misleading checkout 8.86% of GB, +7.48pp) while 'price too high' runs below global — 'the checkout presentation, not the price level, is what is generating one-star reviews'; a monthly plan costing more for two months than the annual for twelve (15). Report 52: two one-time tiers (小太阳 / 大太阳) with no upgrade credit between them; tier confusion carries a ×5.11 payer lift. Report 54: a one-time purchase that 5 reviewers think is a subscription ('the one time fee for a whole year'; 'is the ¥68 membership a one-off lifetime buyout?'). Report 60 (Mindway): 'When purchasing, it implies the option of monthly billing, but auto drafts the whole year' (1★, 'It seems scammy'); the annual is chosen to escape the weekly ('paid the $40 annual to avoid $7/week') and then regretted — plan clarity at purchase is one of the five paid-user issues; F2 includes the monthly-vs-annual selection screen. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'What is the difference between the 34 and 59 paid subscription?' — a buyer had to publish a 5★ review to ask, because the paywall did not answer it; M2: differentiate the two tiers on the paywall itself. Report 75 (Habit Streak): nine SKUs from $1.99 to $79.99, six named only 'Premium' or 'Premium access' with no period — 'A shopper cannot tell from the listing whether Premium — $11.99 is a month, a year or forever'; §8.1 #2 rename them (no reviewer complains — an external observation).
