statement: Report 75 (Habit Streak, 41 reviews): v1.56.0 (2025-10-21) raised the free tier from 3 to 5 habits with the release note 'You asked, we listened' — the corpus confirms the change (three reviewers report 3 before it, two report 5 after, never both) and measures no benefit: money-negative share flat 33.3% → 35.3%, cap objections flat 2 → 2, mean rating 4.28 → 3.53, 1–3★ share 16.7% → 41.2%, and the tone hardened from 3–4★ with volunteered praise ('which is unfortunate… other than that, I would recommend!') to two 1★ ('se stupide'; 'Pff franchement c est soulant'); at n=17/18 the differences are not statistically separable, but 'the objection survived the concession in identical form, at the new number… Anyone proposing to move it to 7 should know that the last move bought nothing measurable'; the best-argued complaint asks to gate features, not habit count ('faite le gratuit ça et mettez des trucs premium en plus'); §8.2 do not raise the cap again as a sentiment fix. Related: [[C007]] (generous fixed cap), [[C133]] (gate on capability not quantity), [[C222]] (hard cap with a pressure valve), [[C270]] (earned capacity). Report 86 (Today): the counter-evidence at small numbers — raising the cap from one to three did buy back sentiment (71 complaints in 2016 → 0 in 2017–2020, one angry 1★ converting to full price the same month) because one habit is 'a screenshot, not a trial'; the null result in report 75 was 3 → 5, past the point where the cap stopped being the objection.

title: When the pricing model changes, the historical review corpus keeps advertising the old one — state the current model on the listing and paywall, and honour every old receipt automatically
statement: Report 76 (Way of Life, 7,764 reviews over 16 years): premium was a $4.99 one-time unlock from 2010 and became a subscription in 2023; in the subscription era (E6, 906 reviews) MON_SUBSCRIPTION is 40 reviews at mean 2.70★ (4.42% of the era, 15 of the corpus's 181 1★) and splits three ways — lifetime buyers told to subscribe again ('Ich hab mir die App 2015 oder so als voll Version gekauft', 1★; '之前永久内购没了？重新订阅？', 1★), new users who arrived expecting the one-time price because 'reviews said it was a one time payment' (3★), and prices differing week to week ('last week the price was $29, this week is $99', 4★); some veterans were grandfathered ('grandfathered into the new system', 5★), so the path existed but was not reliable; restore failures rose 0.91% → 1.55% and support silence peaked (SUP_NONE 9 of 20 in E6). A decade of 5★ reviews praising 'a one time charge' keeps recruiting users who then feel misled; §8.1 restore premium for any old receipt on any device without a subscription prompt, and show one stable price per region stating monthly / annual / lifetime. Related: [[C186]] (never revoke what earlier buyers paid for), [[C218]] (listing copy stays true), [[C113]] (one stable disclosed price), [[C003]] (lead with lifetime). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): year-one reviews sold the app as 'no subscriptions… one time payment of $10'; when the model changed the description still said nothing about money at all and the only 'used to be great' review (1★) lists 'the lack of a subscription' among what it lost — 'a market that was sold a specific promise — one payment, no subscription — encountering a different one, with no listing text to mediate the change'. Report 86 (Today): 'I paid for this app and reviewed it years ago (when it was under a different pricing model)… for the $300 you're asking for now' (5★) — a decade of one-time-price reviews now sits beside a $299.99 SKU.

title: Backup and sync must run on infrastructure reachable in every storefront the app is sold in — a blocked provider makes the app's data unsafe in that market
statement: Report 76 (Way of Life): backup was Dropbox-only in the early years; 17 of the 18 NEG_DROPBOX_BLOCKED complaints are from the Chinese storefront (2014-07-18 → 2016-03-08; 'Dropbox中国区都屏蔽了吧' — Dropbox is blocked in China, 3★), the other from sg; cn also carries BUG_BACKUP 5 (7.35× global) and REQ_BACKUP 9 (6.30×), and was the app's second-largest storefront (528 reviews) before it went quiet after 2018 (never more than 12 reviews a year). A backup path that a market cannot reach is, for that market, no backup: data loss follows on the next phone change. Related: [[C132]] (do not sell where the app cannot function), [[C034]] (data never lost), [[C153]] (automatic cloud backup on by default), [[C026]] (markets where rails fail). Report 85 (Habitica): a server-dependent client sold on the Chinese storefront that cannot reach its servers there — 'in mainland China it keeps failing to connect' (4★); access complaints outnumber game complaints on cn.

title: The free tier must let the differentiator be experienced — a cap that hides the product's own thesis converts on nothing the user has felt
statement: Report 77 (Habit Tracker: Streak-Free / Momentumly, 71 reviews): the product's thesis — forgiving, multi-habit momentum instead of streaks — is the best-supported finding in the corpus (19 of 71, 26.76%, mean 4.89★, zero below 4★), yet the free tier is one habit, so 'the product's own differentiator (forgiving multi-habit momentum) is not experienceable free'; 'a habit tracker with one habit is a demo'; the four who hit the cap rate it 2.50★ ('you can't really explore the app'), MON_PAYWALL_BLOCKS 7 (9.86%, 2.86★) is the largest negative code, and the three reviewers who did convert converted on comparative value against trackers they had already tried — 'an informed judgement they could only make after using it'; §8.4.1 the paywall does not lead with the concept although the listing and title do; §8.4.3 a trial or an unambiguous free window is the mechanism that lets the cap be tested without changing it. The report does not recommend raising the cap (no conversion data) — it establishes that at one habit the thing being sold cannot be felt. Related: [[C147]] (let people use the product before they pay), [[C182]] (a pre-use hard paywall makes every purchase non-evidence-based), [[C133]] (gate on capability not quantity), [[C007]] (generous fixed cap), [[C063]] (free trial before purchase). Report 86 (Today): 'one habit is not a trial, it is a screenshot. A one-habit cap in an app whose paid value is multi-habit dashboards prevents the prospect from ever seeing the thing they would be buying' — MON_TRIAL_REQ 33 (1.85%) made identically in 2016 ('Expand the free app to allow a proper trial and then ask for money') and 2024 ('one is not enough for a trial'); a confused user who deleted the app 'otherwise I'd have bought it'.

title: A free cap's acceptability is set by the bundle around it — the same number reads as generous or as a wall depending on what else is free; moving a loved feature behind the wall changes sentiment as much as changing the number
statement: Report 79 (Ripples / Checker, 172 reviews): the free tier was three boards for the whole 770-day window and three reviewers on three storefronts state the number — in October 2024 and July 2025 as generosity ('for widgets and 3 habits without limitations'; 'three habits… without huge limitations', both 5★), in January 2026 as 'met 3 boards ben je totaal niks' (3★). What changed between those dates was not the cap but the home-screen widget — the single most-praised feature in the corpus (PRAISE_WIDGET 27, 15.70%, mean 5.00★, not one below 5) — moving behind the paywall in a 101-day window (2025-07-16 → 2025-10-25); paywall-shape complaints went from 0 of 110 reviews in the first era to ~10% of reviews after, the one explicit upgrade in the corpus was 'for more boards' (the cap was converting on its own), and a 4★ proposes the compromise himself: 'make 2 widgets available in free version, one the bigger one and one the minimalist one'. 'The cap is not the lever that broke; the bundle around it is.' §8.4.1: a widget is a daily impression of the product — removing it from the free tier removes the strongest retention and word-of-mouth surface in exchange for pressure on a cap that already worked. Related: [[C007]] (generous fixed cap), [[C222]] (hard cap with a pressure valve), [[C293]] (raising a cap does not buy back sentiment), [[C001]] (never move a free feature behind the paywall), [[C009]] (basic widgets are free). Report 86 (Today): the cap's own size is the bundle here — the same one-habit grievance at 1.97★ vs the three-habit grievance at 3.60★, and a four-year silence in between; a single review attests a 5-habit stage.

title: A public roadmap converts — and becomes a promise users hold you to
statement: Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): PRAISE_ROADMAP 17 (9.88%, mean 4.94★) — reviewers repeatedly cite a public roadmap as a reason for confidence and for buying: 'following a roadmap full of nice upgrades'; 'what I personally miss (notes and custom units) is already planned by the developer! So I'll probably buy the full version soon'; one bought and then said they were waiting on the roadmap ('чекатиму на здійснення усього задуманого по роудмепу'); three purchase intents were conditional on named roadmap items (reminders + sync; notes + custom units; Russian) and all three later shipped. The counterweight is a 3★ whose entire text is 'Please complete roadmap', and a solo developer's pipeline that ships incremental asks (notes, reminders, compact widgets, start-of-day, multi-board view — mostly within 12–18 months, one reviewer editing the review up: 'so happy to have compact boards now!') but leaves the structural ones (Watch, iPad, import) open. Related: [[C196]] (a subscription is a promise of continued delivery — back it with a visible cadence), [[C059]] (be visibly responsive), [[C239]] (a personal origin story builds trust and turns a later gate into a betrayal).

title: Never attach an app subscription to another product's checkout by default — the subscription is its own opt-in line with its own amount, period, renewal date and final-total confirmation, and a 'book only' choice must never produce a recurring charge
statement: Report 82 (Lasting Change, 175 reviews, mean 1.88★): the product people set out to buy is a personalised book from the developer's website; the app subscription arrives attached to that purchase — BILL_TIED_TO_BOOK 43 (24.57%, mean 1.05★), the largest non-rhetorical code ('I had only intended to purchase the Lasting Change book and ended up with a subscription to this app'; 'I purchased the book for $50.99 which was fine. Along with that purchase is an undisclosed subscription that is $30.99'; 'a $131 purchase has turned into an ongoing financial commitment of $55 per month'); U:consent_failure 56 (32.00%, 1.11★) and BILL_NO_CONSENT 36 with a perfect 1.00★ mean; one reviewer explicitly unselected the app at checkout, was billed anyway, re-ran the checkout to test the seller's claim and found no opt-in ('you are automatically subscribed to it with a purchase of the physical book'); a post-pay upsell page positioned a £74.69 lifetime price so it read as an upgrade delta with 'no explicit confirmation step showing the full amount'; the bundle is priced below the book alone so the subscription is effectively forced; 'Not one review in 175 describes choosing to subscribe to this app because of something the app does.' The book itself is liked (BOOK_PRAISE 14 vs BOOK_CRITIC 8: 'Love the book, don't fall for the scam') — a liked physical product cannot rescue the app that bills for it. §8.3: separate lines, subscription default off, full total before charging, recurring terms in the confirmation email. Related: [[C285]] (a paid add-on is never bought on a single tap), [[C210]] (bill App Store users through the App Store), [[C111]] (show the price up front), [[C283]] (never sell by manipulation).

title: A headline star rating that sits far above its own written reviews is a signal to audit, not a satisfaction figure — find where and when star-only ratings are collected before trusting them
statement: Report 82 (Lasting Change): the text corpus averages 1.880★ while the ratings-weighted public mean across the same 26 storefronts is 3.838★ (848 ratings, 673 star-only) — a 1.958-star gap, and more than two full stars in every one of the four high-volume storefronts (us 2.00 vs 4.10, gb 1.09 vs 3.27, ca 1.31 vs 3.72, au 1.29 vs 3.55); 72.00% of text reviews are one-star, at least one 5★ is a fraud warning, and the public 4.1★ 'does not reflect the content of the reviews underneath it'; two readings the report does not choose between — text-writers are a negatively selected minority, or star-only ratings are collected in a context text reviews are not — and §8.8 asks where in the lifecycle and from whom the stars are gathered. In ordinary corpora the gap is a few tenths (report 79: +0.18; report 77: +0.27; report 76: up to +0.38 per storefront); a two-star gap across every major market is the signature of a rating stream and a review stream describing different populations. Related: [[C231]] (written reviews are a complaint channel — audit the funnel), [[C094]] (ask for reviews well), [[C076]] (never seed the launch rating). Report 83 (Roubit): the counter-case — here the written reviews lead the public rating downward during a bug wave (Japan text 3.36★ vs public 4.48★) because loyal users file bug reports at five stars and the cumulative star base lags; §8.10 'don't read cumulative 4.66★ as current satisfaction'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the no-gap baseline — +0.009★ between public and text means for a free app with no billing surface; the two-star gap in report 82 is a billing-surface artefact, not a property of star ratings. Report 85 (Habitica): public exceeds corpus by 0.26–0.78★ in every eligible storefront for an app with an eleven-year defect history — the ordinary 'people write when something breaks' gap, an order of magnitude below the report 82 anomaly. Report 86 (Today): public 4.5–4.8★ vs corpus 3.97★ — a 0.6–0.8 gap on a ten-year corpus with a collapsed review rate; 'the true signal is in the text, which is why every finding here is text-derived'.

title: The support form and account deletion must not live behind the surface most likely to break — a tab outage must never take the reporting and exit paths down with it
statement: Report 83 (Roubit, 500 reviews): in two waves (2025-11-06 → 11-10 and 2026-05-16 → 06-09) the Diary and Settings tabs opened a white screen — BUG_DIARY_SETTINGS_BLANK 40 (8.00%), 14 of the 15 reviews in the first window and 26 of 37 in the second; Settings holds the in-app support form and account deletion, so the bug cut off the way to report it and the way to leave: SUPPORT_UNREACHABLE_INAPP 6 — '設定にもいけないから不具合報告が出来なくてやむなくこちらに書かせて頂きました' (I can't reach Settings to report the bug, so I had no choice but to write here, 4★); '設定画面に入れないので何もできない' (I can't get into Settings, so I can't do anything — about deleting the account, 1★); reviews became the support desk (SUPPORT_QUESTION 43, 8.60%) and 19 of the 40 blank-screen reports were filed at four or five stars by loyal users. §8.1: 'Move the support form and account deletion somewhere that does not depend on Settings loading'; a release gate on Diary and Settings opening, staged rollout with blank-screen telemetry, a fallback read-only diary view, diary export. Related: [[C036]] (a support channel reachable outside the app), [[C249]] (account deletion completes in one step), [[C235]] (a first-run failure escape hatch), [[C188]] (the app must open offline).

title: A premium currency must have a slow, honest earned path — a currency free players cannot earn turns free-core goodwill into 'pay-to-win' and rewards lying
statement: Report 85 (Habitica, 3,445 reviews over eleven years): the free core earns goodwill (PR_FREE 68, MON_NOT_REQUIRED 44: 'it doesn't hide functionality behind a paywall'; 'No annoying pop ups (which makes me actually want to spend money to support the devs)') and the gem economy spends it — MON_GEM_GATE 47 (1.36%, mean 3.34★): quests, hairstyles, backgrounds and pet food sit behind gems that free players can barely earn ('The quests and many customization items are stuck behind gem paywalls'); MON_P2W_PERCEIVED 19 at 1.84★ ('After subscribing you are allotted the ability to buy 24 gems for only $6 more dollars'); the complaint is growing — 4.2% of E5 reviews against at most 1.0% in any earlier era; the current free route is challenge prize draws, and 'you have to just lie and say you did it'; the request is not for free gems but for a slow, earned route (streak rewards, achievements, an expensive gold-for-gem exchange); §8.5 replace prize draws with a small earned trickle and measure subscription starts and honesty proxies, not gem balances. Stated purchasers are few (55, 1.60%) and buy as patronage — 'I upgraded just to help support the developers' (23.6% of payers) — so the subscription's value is trust, which the currency erodes. Related: [[C241]] (sell entitlements as non-consumables), [[C270]] (earned free capacity reads as generosity), [[C164]] (a random-rotation shop with paid re-rolls is a friction generator), [[C238]] (a rewarded path for those who cannot pay), [[C061]] (goodwill conversion).

title: Check-in latency must be independent of accumulated history — an app that slows with every completed day drives away exactly the users who proved it works and most likely paid
statement: Report 86 (Today Habit tracker, 1,785 reviews over 10.3 years): the most damaging defect in the corpus appears only once a user has succeeded — BUG_PERF 70 (3.92%), rising from 0.74% of E1 to 16.95% of E5; reviewers quantify it: 'it takes about 5 seconds to register, if I'm registering a long streak of 50 day's or so, which is how I've been using it for 3 years, it takes so long I've stopped bothering' (gb 1★); 'past 1,000 days a single tap means a mysterious freeze then a crash' (jp 1★); '200 check-ins is not really a large amount of data; the storage must be inefficiently programmed' (de 3★); 'It can take over a minute from when you mark something as done… I've contacted support multiple times over the past 6 months' (1★); 17 of the 70 (24.3%) also record leaving or being blocked; Germany is the performance-complaint market (11.69%, three times global); paid reviewers report defects at a higher rate because they use it longer with more habits — 'exactly the condition under which this app degrades'; one reviewer connects the full-screen-photo visual model directly to the slowness. §8.1: 'test it the way users experience it: seed 20 habits × 1,000 check-ins and measure tap-to-confirmation. Do not test on a fresh install.' Related: [[C083]] (performance must not degrade with habit count), [[C264]] (log-entry friction is sacred), [[C065]] (paying customers are the highest 1★ risk).
